- **A2** (AGENTS.md): 5 `### Full Prompt` headers → `### Prompt (excerpt)` + blockquote pointing to `.claude/agents/*.md`. Reality: embedded blocks lack model:/effort: frontmatter the shipped prompts carry. `grep "Full Prompt" docs/AGENTS.md` → none.

- **AR10** (ARCHITECTURE.md:422): "Six live fixtures"+6-list → "Seven"+added rubric-revision-loop. Same evidence as M4.
- **AR11** (ARCHITECTURE.md): golden-cassette "PR reviewers see this rather than 50MB JSON" → "Golden cassettes (debugging references)"; invariants are the gate, no PR-time live run. Evidence: `test.yml:13,19` (no cron, workflow_dispatch only, goldens debugging-only).
- **Q2** (QUICKSTART.md:3): "Ultimate Workflow Plugin … in 5 minutes" → "claude-workflow plugin installed and verified" (dropped unmeasured time; rebranded). Evidence: `plugin.json:2` name=claude-workflow. Same stale brand also fixed in AGENTS.md:3 / HOOKS.md:3 / ARCHITECTURE.md:3 (all in my owned files).
- **Q4** (QUICKSTART.md:157): "Should show all green checks" → scoped to CORE SYSTEM + GIT INTEGRATION must-pass; advisory checks commonly warn + are tolerated. Evidence: `bd doctor` re-run 2026-06-14 → `⚠ CLI Version 0.47.1 (latest 1.0.4)`, `⚠ DB-JSONL Sync Count mismatch`, `✖ Sync Divergence (3)`; bd-compat pin #28 tolerates any exit code.

### PROVEN-WITH-CAVEAT (1, R8 — honest downgrade, prove-or-remove)
- **R8** (README.md:24-29): absolute "PRs and Beads tasks auto-link to GitHub (issues, PRs, close-on-merge)" → "GitHub issue auto-linking is provided (bd-github-link.sh: posts a back-link comment on close, parses Closes #N); its call shapes are verified by the bd-github-link L1 test against a stubbed gh, not a live round-trip." - All 13 stale-doc rows were genuinely contradicted by current code/config — none were already-true mislabels. The cluster traces to ONE root cause: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md + docs/HOOKS.md carry v2-era pseudocode (keyword router, allowlist filter, 5-hook count, 500-cap) that the v3 implementation superseded but the docs never tracked. Recommend a doc-vs-code drift guard (L1 grep test asserting hook-count / fixture-count / denylist-not-allowlist) so these can't silently re-stale.

    canonical fixture state. Subsequent runs then see those tasks as
    already-present, making beadsTasksCreated diff = []. Fixed snapshotFixture
    to capture pre-run HEAD SHA and restoreFixture to reset to that SHA (not
    plain "HEAD" which itself moves during the run).
  - Run 3 (919s): PASSED. Golden refreshed with proper hookSequence (232 events
    including 4 Stops — 2 block + 2 implicit-approve), 6 beads tasks created
    with qa-approved transitions, plugin loaded cleanly, no errors, no denials.

   - multi-domain-signup: beadsTaskCount==2 vs >=3 (orchestrator didn't decompose into 3 children)
5. Those 3 were promoted from same-run replays via lib/promoteReplay.ts.
6. After commit + push (7167ebd), CI L3-live STILL failed on all 6 fixtures.

ROOT CAUSE DIAGNOSIS:
Model behavior is non-deterministic enough that even fresh same-day goldens drift against subsequent runs. The matchesGolden normalizer in lib/goldenCompare.ts compares:
- tool call sequences (Bash/Read/Edit ordering)
- subagent invocation count
- hook firing sequence
- file write set
- Beads label transitions

Real-Claude variability shifts:
- Bash↔Read ordering swaps regularly (the model decides whether to peek-then-do or do-then-verify)
- Subagent count varies (orchestrator sometimes invokes devops for shim setup, sometimes not)
- Beads tasks created varies (depends on whether orchestrator decomposes into siblings or one task)
- Permission denials surface inconsistently (AskUserQuestion sometimes triggered)

The normalizer is too STRICT for the actual variability of the model.

WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY FIX IT (any of these — pick one):

A) MORE TOLERANT NORMALIZER (probably 1-2 days of work):
   - Compare structural SETS rather than ordered sequences for tools (allow Bash/Read order to swap freely).
   - Compare subagent COUNTS within tolerance (±1 invocation OK).
   - Make hook firing sequence position-agnostic.
   - Add a "looseness" score per fixture; allow some drift threshold.

B) SEMANTIC MATCHING (probably 3-5 days):
   - Stop matching tool sequences. Match outcomes: "did backend get invoked AT ALL", "did QA approve at the end", "were any auth-related files written", etc.
   - This is what the spec-level assertions already do (subagentInvoked, hookFired, etc.). matchesGolden becomes a "did the trace look broadly similar" check rather than a structural-snapshot.

C) DROP matchesGolden ENTIRELY (probably 1 hour):
   - Remove the assertion from all 6 specs.
   - Keep all the OTHER spec-level assertions (subagentInvoked, hookFired, noPermissionDenials, etc.) — those are what actually test plugin behavior.
   - L3-live becomes a "did the plugin route end-to-end correctly" test, not a "did the output look exactly like last time" test.
   - Lose: regression detection against past behavior shifts.
   - Gain: stable CI, no $30-60 re-record cost per drift event.

D) ADVISORY-ONLY L3-LIVE (5 min):
   - Set `continue-on-error: true` on the L3-live job in .github/workflows/test.yml.
   - L3-live still runs, still surfaces failures in the job summary, but doesn't block PR merging.
   - Keep matchesGolden as a "for visibility" signal.
   - This is the cheapest stopgap while deciding between A/B/C.

E) MOVE matchesGolden TO L4 ONLY (~30 min):
   - L3-live on PR keeps the spec-level assertions but drops matchesGolden.
   - L4 daily drift watch keeps matchesGolden as the canary signal.
   - Drift is documented, doesn't block PRs.

RECOMMENDED PATH: D (5 min) as immediate unblock, then C or E as the longer-term resolution. Avoid A/B until we know whether we actually use matchesGolden for anything in practice.

FILES IMPLICATED:
- .claude/tests/e2e/lib/goldenCompare.ts (the normalizer)
- .claude/tests/e2e/specs/*.spec.ts (6 specs, all call matchesGolden)
- .claude/tests/e2e/cassettes/golden/*.jsonl (6 captures committed)
- .github/workflows/test.yml (L3-live job config)
- /tmp/g8-rerecord-final.log (full vitest output from the last refresh attempt)

DON'T DO:
- Another fresh RECORD_GOLDEN run. Same drift wall, ~$30-60 wasted.
- Loosen the matchesGolden normalizer ad-hoc without a clear theory of which dimensions are noise vs signal.

<!-- BD-MCP-DOC: spec v1 -->
# SPEC — 1vq.1 Sol reviewer lane helpers + gate subcommands (v4.0.0 Phase V2, epic 1vq)

Source: `docs/plans/v4-trimodel.md` Phase V2 + the executable plan's V2 section. Prompts/docs (qa.md, orchestrator.md, CODEX_SETUP.md, README) are 1vq.2 — NOT this task. All offline/zero-cost; the stub codex server makes every test run without OpenAI access.

## Governing rules (from the release spec — violations are design failures)
- Sol is ADVISORY and STRICTLY OPTIONAL: absence/failure/timeout of the Codex MCP connection must behave identically to "not connected". A degradation spec must prove byte-identical gate behavior.
- **D5 (structural): `qa-gate.sh`, `verify-before-stop.sh`, and the new `review-check.sh` must contain ZERO references to codex or the reviewer lane.** Lane selection is prompt-side only. A structural grep test enforces this.
- The change-set-hash-bound qa-approved record stays the ONLY release credential — nothing here creates a second release path. The V3 gate ENFORCEMENT (approve refusals, Stop discipline) is NOT in this task; you only land the record writers + the counting helper.
- Bounded diligence: caps live in ONE place (`.claude/review-config`); cap-hit sets `stopped_by`, never loops.

## Architecture decisions (final — implement as stated)
- D1: gate-countable records = Beads comments (greppable via `bd show --json`); bulk artifacts = `.claude/.qa-tracking/review-*.json` files (agents may doc-mirror; not your concern).
- D2: ONE counting/independence implementation = `review-check.sh`, subprocess-invoked (mirrors how impact-report.sh --hash-only is shared).
- D3: Codex transport = the pure-bash FIFO JSON-RPC client pattern already in `impact-report.sh` (~lines 269-424: FIFO + wait_for_id). `codex mcp-server` is a native binary; stub seams `CODEX_MCP_BIN` + `CODEX_MCP_ARGS` (stub = `CODEX_MCP_BIN=node CODEX_MCP_ARGS=<stub.js>`) mirroring CODE_GRAPH_MCP_BIN/IMPACT_REPORT_NODE.
- D8: ordered severity enum `critical>high>medium>low>info`; `risk_threshold` uses the same enum.

## Deliverables

### 1. `.claude/review-config` (NEW, committed; rubric-config style)
```
risk_threshold_default=high
max_findings=10
max_review_iterations=3
timeout_seconds=300
malformed_retry=1
```

### 2. `.claude/scripts/codex-detect.sh` (NEW) — subcommands `detect [--refresh]`, `status`
Layered detection, always exit 0: (a) fast path: jq `.mcpServers.codex` from `${CODEX_USER_CONFIG:-$HOME/.claude.json}` — absent ⇒ lane=claude, method=config-absent (~0s, the common teammate case); (b) present ⇒ truthful stdio handshake: spawn the registered command (env overrides `CODEX_MCP_BIN`/`CODEX_MCP_ARGS`), JSON-RPC `initialize` then `tools/list`, require a tool literally named `codex`, within `${CODEX_DETECT_TIMEOUT_S:-5}`; any failure/timeout/missing-tool ⇒ lane=claude with method naming the failure; always kill the spawned server. Writes `.claude/.qa-tracking/reviewer-lane.json` atomically: `{"reviewer_lane":"codex"|"claude","method":"handshake|config-absent|handshake-failed|timeout|no-codex-tool","codex_cmd":...,"codex_args":[...],"detected_at":"<ts>"}`. `status` prints the file (or `claude/no-flag`). NOTE: bi3.1 already left a dormant probe seam in model-select.sh's `detect_reviewer_lane` that defers to this script when executable — after you ship it, verify the model-roles artifact's `reviewer_lane` follows it (and the statusline shows `rev:sol` when lane=codex).

### 3. `.claude/scripts/session-start.sh` — integrate detect
After the model-select block, run `codex-detect.sh detect` under the same timeout/gtimeout guard (5s), fold one line (`reviewer_lane: codex|claude`) into the context, failures into warnings. Fail-open. Re-sync fixtures.

### 4. `.claude/scripts/review-check.sh` (NEW) — the ONE validator/counter
Subcommands (strict JSON envelope on stdout; exit 0 ok / 4 violation / 2 bd-unavailable / 1 usage):
- `validate-request <file>`: request schema below; error keys `missing_risk_threshold`, `missing_stop_condition`, `risk_threshold_invalid_enum`, `missing_key:<k>`, `invalid_json`.
- `validate-artifact <file>`: artifact schema below; error keys `missing_key:<k>`, `verdict_invalid_enum`, `finding_item_invalid:<why>`, `finding_id_malformed` (grammar `^R[0-9]+-F[0-9]+$`), `severity_invalid_enum`, `stopped_by_invalid_enum`.
- `gate <task-id> [--comments-json <file>]` (offline L1 seam substituting `bd show --json` output): implement EXACTLY —
```
impl = unique captures /^IMPLEMENTER: role=([a-z]+) / over comments   # may be empty
art  = LAST comment matching /^REVIEW-ARTIFACT v1 /                    # none -> exit 4 review_artifact_missing
reviewer = token reviewer=([A-Za-z0-9._-]+); threshold = token risk_threshold=(\w+)
findings = parse token findings=[<id>:<sev>,...]                       # [] => empty
independent = (impl empty) OR (reviewer NOT IN impl)                   # empty set = vacuous pass
open = findings with rank(sev) >= rank(threshold)
       minus ids having a /^RESOLVED <id> / comment containing non-empty fix= AND test= tokens
       minus ids whose LATEST /^ARBITRATION <id> / comment has decision=overrule   # sustain keeps open
!independent -> exit 4 reviewer_not_independent; open>0 -> exit 4 unresolved_findings (+open_finding_ids); else 0
```
Envelope: `{ok, artifact:{...summary...}, reviewer_identity, implementers:[], independent, open_findings, open_finding_ids:[], error_key?, observations}`.

### 5. Request/artifact JSON schemas (files under `.claude/.qa-tracking/`)
- Request `review-request-<sanitized-tid>.json`: `{contract_version:"1", task_id, iteration, risk_threshold*, stop_condition*, change_set_hash, spec, diff, completion_contract, impact_report}` (*mandatory non-empty).
- Artifact `review-artifact-<sanitized-tid>-r<i>.json`: `{contract_version:"1", task_id, reviewer_identity:"sol-codex"|"qa-claude", reviewer_model, reviewed_hash, risk_threshold, stop_condition, verdict:"approve"|"findings", findings:[{id,severity,location,evidence,description}], iterations, stopped_by:"verdict"|"stop_condition"|"cap:max_findings"|"cap:max_review_iterations"|"cap:timeout"}`.

### 6. `.claude/scripts/codex-review.sh` (NEW) — root-invoked Sol driver
`codex-review.sh <task-id> --request <file> --iteration <n>`: validate request (via review-check; fail ⇒ exit 4) → read caps → `--iteration > max_review_iterations` ⇒ exit 6 → resolve server cmd/args from `${CODEX_USER_CONFIG:-$HOME/.claude.json}` (env overrides) → FIFO client: initialize → `tools/call {name:"codex", arguments:{prompt:<envelope>, sandbox:"read-only", cwd:$PROJECT_DIR}}` → overall wall-clock `timeout_seconds` ⇒ kill + exit 5 (no artifact) → extract final text, strip fences, validate as artifact; on invalid, up to `malformed_retry` corrective turns via `tools/call {name:"codex-reply", arguments:{conversationId:<from first result>, prompt:"Validation failed: <error_key>. Emit ONLY the corrected JSON object."}}`; still invalid ⇒ exit 5 → truncate findings to `max_findings` + set `stopped_by=cap:max_findings` when exceeded → FORCE fields: task_id, iterations=<n>, risk_threshold/stop_condition from request, reviewer_identity="sol-codex", reviewer_model from registration/env → write artifact file atomically, echo its path, exit 0. Envelope text: independent ADVISORY reviewer; never approves/labels/modifies; exactly ONE JSON object as final message; blocking bar = risk_threshold; STOP when stop_condition met; at most max_findings findings, most severe first; id grammar R<iteration>-F<n>; then the schema and the full request JSON.
**Schema re-verification (REQUIRED before coding the stub):** codex-cli 0.145.0 is installed on this machine. Probe the REAL server's tool schema offline: run `codex mcp-server` via your own FIFO client (or `printf` a JSON-RPC initialize+tools/list into it) and capture the `codex` tool's inputSchema — the stub must enforce the REAL argument names (prompt/sandbox/cwd may differ; conversationId name for codex-reply likewise). Record what you found in a bd comment. Do NOT invoke the `codex` tool itself (that would hit OpenAI) — tools/list only.

### 7. `qa-gate.sh` — three NEW subcommands (record writers; NO approve/Stop enforcement changes in this task)
- `review-record <tid> [--file <path>]` (mirror grade-record's style byte-for-byte): validate via `review-check.sh validate-artifact` (subprocess — no second validator), then post the comment:
  `REVIEW-ARTIFACT v1 iteration=<n> reviewer=<id> model=<m> reviewed_hash=<h> risk_threshold=<sev> verdict=<v> stopped_by=<s> findings=[<id>:<sev>,...] at <ts>: <one-line summary>` (empty ⇒ `findings=[]`). JSON envelope out.
- `resolve-finding <tid> <finding-id> --fix '<ref>' --test '<ref>' '<summary>'`: validate the id exists in the LATEST REVIEW-ARTIFACT comment; empty fix/test ⇒ exit 1; post `RESOLVED <id> at <ts>: fix=<ref> test=<ref> — <summary>`.
- `arbitrate <tid> <finding-id> <overrule|sustain> '<rationale>'`: same id validation; empty rationale ⇒ exit 1; post `ARBITRATION <id> decision=<d> at <ts>: <rationale>`.
Update usage()/header docs. These grammars are LOAD-BEARING V3 contracts — byte-exact as specified.

### 8. Tests (L1 `.claude/scripts/tests/`, L2 `.claude/tests/component/specs/`, META prefix + TEXT anchors)
- L1 `review-check.test.sh`: validate-request rejections (missing risk_threshold / missing stop_condition / bad enum → exact error keys, exit 4); validate-artifact full schema matrix; META: sensitivity (a checker copy with the mandatory-field check stripped must PASS the bad fixture — proving the real check is load-bearing).
- L1 `review-count.test.sh` (via `--comments-json`): below-threshold ignored; RESOLVED lacking test= stays open; ARBITRATION sustain stays open / overrule clears / latest-wins; reviewer==implementer ⇒ exit 4 reviewer_not_independent; empty implementer set ⇒ vacuous independent; **META (plan-mandated): strip an ARBITRATION comment from a good comment-set fixture → the gate-count assertion must flip to unresolved_findings.**
- L2 `codex-detect.sh` spec: fake CODEX_USER_CONFIG absent → claude/config-absent; stub handshake OK → codex; hung stub (never answers) → timeout→claude; crashing stub → handshake-failed→claude; stub advertising NO `codex` tool → no-codex-tool→claude (META); `--refresh` rewrites; reviewer-lane.json feeds model-select artifact + statusline `rev:sol`.
- L2 `codex-review.sh` spec with a RECORDING stub codex MCP server (node script speaking real JSON-RPC over stdio, enforcing the REAL verified inputSchema, logging every request): (a) approve verdict → valid artifact + review-record posts the comment; (b) findings-above-threshold → gate reports open; (c) stub returns max_findings+3 → truncated + `stopped_by=cap:max_findings`; (d) stub sleeps past timeout_seconds (use a tiny cap in the fixture config) → exit 5, no artifact file; (e) prose-then-JSON first reply → corrective codex-reply turn used (stub-recorded); **META (plan-mandated): mutate the recorded artifact's stopped_by from cap:max_findings to verdict → the cap assertion must FAIL.**
- L2 `review-separation-records.sh` (record-writer coverage): review-record/resolve-finding/arbitrate comment grammars byte-exact (grep the posted comments); id-not-found rejections; empty-evidence rejections.
- L2 `reviewer-lane-degradation.sh` (**the degradation proof**): run an identical sequence (seed comments → review-record a qa-claude artifact → review-check gate) in two fixtures — one with reviewer-lane.json=codex + stub server present, one with neither — and diff captured outputs/comments (timestamps normalized): EMPTY. Plus the structural grep: `qa-gate.sh`, `verify-before-stop.sh`, `review-check.sh` contain zero `codex|reviewer.lane|reviewer_lane` matches; **META: inject a codex reference into a copy → structural assertion fails.**

### 9. Fixture sync
All new/modified `.claude/scripts/*.sh` (codex-detect, review-check, codex-review, qa-gate, session-start) byte-synced into the 7 e2e fixtures (manual cp; drift guard will verify). `.claude/review-config` is config — check empirically whether fixtures need it (L2 fixtures symlink scripts and may source the config; seed the fixture lib if the specs need it).

## Constraints
bash 3.2 + jq; stdout contracts + META discipline (LESSONS 3fn, llh.20); comment writers are the ONLY writers of their grammars; qa-gate/verify-before-stop APPROVE/RELEASE LOGIC UNTOUCHED (V3 does enforcement — do not add refusals now); no version bump; no permissions.deny; helpers never invoke the real `codex` TOOL (tools/list handshake only; everything else stubbed); remember helper-rewritten/bash-written files don't enter changed-files.txt (LESSONS bi3.2) — write test fixtures via bash where tracker pollution matters, but your DELIVERABLE scripts via normal Edit/Write so they're gate-tracked.

## Verification before reporting done
All suites green (L1 + L2 + `make lint` + vitest drift guard); the real-schema probe result recorded on the task; JSON manifests parse. F7 contract; llm_observations mandatory.

## REAL codex-cli 0.145.0 schema probe (offline, tools/list ONLY — codex tool NOT invoked)

Probed the installed server via `codex -m gpt-5.6-sol mcp-server` with a FIFO JSON-RPC client: `initialize` + `notifications/initialized` + `tools/list`. serverInfo.version = `0.145.0`. Two tools advertised: `codex`, `codex-reply`.

### `codex` tool inputSchema (VERBATIM key facts)
- `additionalProperties: false` — unknown args are REJECTED. The stub MUST reject them; codex-review.sh MUST send only known props.
- `required: ["prompt"]`.
- Known props: `prompt` (string), `sandbox` (enum: `read-only`|`workspace-write`|`danger-full-access`), `cwd` (string), `model`, `approval-policy` (enum untrusted|on-request|never), `base-instructions`, `compact-prompt`, `config` (object), `developer-instructions`.
- SPEC envelope `{prompt, sandbox:"read-only", cwd}` is FULLY VALID. `read-only` is a real enum member.

### `codex-reply` tool inputSchema
- NO `additionalProperties:false` (extra props tolerated).
- `required: ["prompt"]`.
- `threadId` (string) — CANONICAL. Description: "required, but kept optional for backward compat".
- `conversationId` (string) — **DEPRECATED**: "use threadId instead".
- **DELTA vs SPEC**: SPEC assumed `conversationId`; the REAL preferred field is `threadId`. codex-review.sh will pass `threadId` (primary) and the stub will accept `threadId` (also tolerate `conversationId`).

### tools/call RESULT shape (from openai/codex `codex_mcp_interface.md`, corroborated by web)
```json
{
  "content": [{ "type": "text", "text": "Hello from Codex" }],
  "structuredContent": { "threadId": "019bbed6-...", "content": "Hello from Codex" }
}
```
- Final agent message text: `.result.content[].text` (mirrored at `.result.structuredContent.content`).
- Thread id for follow-ups: `.result.structuredContent.threadId` (NOT a top-level `conversationId`; historical issues #3712/#8388/#8580 fixed by PR #18093 which propagates threadId in 0.14x).

### Consequences for codex-review.sh + recording stub
1. Extract final text via `.result.content[] | select(.type=="text") | .text` (fallback `.structuredContent.content`); strip fences; validate as artifact.
2. Extract thread id via `.result.structuredContent.threadId`.
3. Corrective turn: `tools/call {name:"codex-reply", arguments:{threadId:<id>, prompt:"Validation failed: <key>. Emit ONLY the corrected JSON object."}}`.
4. Recording stub enforces: codex requires `prompt`, rejects unknown props (additionalProperties:false semantics), validates `sandbox` enum; returns `{content:[{type:text,text:<artifact>}], structuredContent:{threadId, content}}`; codex-reply requires `prompt` + a thread ref.

codex.js wrapper is a pure passthrough spawn of the native binary (no arg rewriting).

<!-- BD-MCP-META: {"kind":"design-decision","source":"devops-agent"} -->
## Design decisions (post context-gathering, pre-implementation)

**codex-detect.sh no-arg contract**: `detect` and no-arg are aliases — both run full layered detection (config fast-path → 5s stdio handshake requiring a `codex` tool), write reviewer-lane.json atomically, and print ONLY the lane word (`codex`|`claude`) to stdout (diagnostics to stderr). This satisfies bi3.1's dormant `detect_reviewer_lane` seam (model-select.sh:494-512 runs `bash codex-detect.sh` no-arg and uses stdout live) AND session-start's `codex-detect.sh detect` capture. `--refresh` = same (force re-probe). `status` prints the JSON file or `claude/no-flag`.

**Hermeticity fix (necessary)**: On this codex-configured machine, shipping codex-detect.sh makes `detect_reviewer_lane` return codex, which would break existing L2 assertion `specs/model-select.sh` R1 ("artifact reviewer_lane defaults to claude") and slow session-lifecycle by 5s/call. Fix: add `export CODEX_USER_CONFIG=<nonexistent-in-fixture>` to `mk_fixture` (lib/fixture.sh). The ONLY consumer of CODEX_USER_CONFIG is the new codex-detect.sh, so this is purely additive host-isolation — component tests must not depend on the host's ~/.claude.json. My codex-detect / codex-review / degradation specs override CODEX_USER_CONFIG per-case.

**D5 structural purity**: review-check.sh/qa-gate.sh/verify-before-stop.sh contain ZERO codex/reviewer_lane refs. review-check.sh uses only generic tokens (`reviewer=`, reviewer_identity/reviewer_model — none match `codex|reviewer.lane|reviewer_lane`). I will NOT enum-validate reviewer_identity against the literal "sol-codex" (that string contains "codex") — presence-only, matching the SPEC's explicit error-key list (no reviewer_identity_invalid_enum). qa-gate.sh review-record reads `.reviewer_identity` from the artifact generically, never hardcodes "sol-codex".

**gate comment parsing**: `bd show --json` → array → `.[0].comments[].text`; take `split("\n")[0]` (first line) of each comment since all grammar records are single-line, making the counting line-oriented and robust. `--comments-json <file>` seam accepts an array of comment objects `{text}` or plain strings.

**codex-review result extraction** (from real schema): final text = `.result.content[]|select(.type=="text").text` (fallback `.structuredContent.content`); thread id = `.result.structuredContent.threadId`; corrective turn uses `codex-reply` with `threadId` (real canonical field; conversationId deprecated). reviewer_model parsed from `-m <model>` in resolved args (real reg = `-m gpt-5.6-sol`), env override CODEX_MCP_MODEL.

## QA review — 1vq.1 Sol reviewer lane (v4.0.0 Phase V2)

### Suites run by QA (not just trusting F7)
- L1 `make test`: 21/21 (incl. new review-check.test.sh + review-count.test.sh; both META blocks green).
- L2 `make test-component`: 27/27 specs, 744 assertions, 0 fail (codex-detect D1-D7, codex-review C1-C5 + stopped_by META, review-separation R1-R6, reviewer-lane-degradation structural+behavioural+META).
- `make lint`: exit 0; explicit shellcheck of the 3 new scripts clean.
- vitest drift guard `_fixture-script-sync`: 161/161 (5 scripts x 7 fixtures byte-identical). e2e-unit 389 pass / 5 skip.
- Manifest + settings.json parse OK; SessionStart..SessionEnd hook events intact.

### Independent verification highlights
- D5 purity: grep `codex|reviewer.lane|reviewer_lane` AND word `sol` = 0 in qa-gate.sh, verify-before-stop.sh, review-check.sh.
- Degradation invariant confirmed LIVE: this machine resolves reviewer-lane=codex/handshake, statusline shows `rev:sol`, yet the degradation spec proves byte-identical gate behaviour vs codex-absent. Optional-lane invariant holds with the lane actively on.
- Diff discipline: qa-gate.sh diff = only the 3 record-writer subcommands + REVIEW_CHECK_SCRIPT var + usage()/header docs + dispatch. cmd_approve/cmd_block/cmd_choose and release logic byte-untouched; verify-before-stop.sh not in the change set. NR==408 META retargeted to a shift-proof first-match text anchor (sound).
- Gate predicate re-derived by hand: below-threshold ignored; sustain keeps open; overrule clears; latest-wins both directions (incl. RESOLVED latest-wins via tail -1); RESOLVED needs non-empty fix= AND test=; reviewer==implementer -> exit 4; empty impl set -> vacuous independent; missing artifact -> exit 4. Token-injection via reviewer_model (fake reviewer=/findings=) defeated by field ordering + head-1/greedy-findings match.
- codex-review vs RECORDING stub: stub enforces the real 0.145.0 schema (additionalProperties:false -> unknown-arg toolError; prompt required; sandbox enum; codex-reply uses threadId). No test path can reach a real codex server (CODEX_MCP_BIN=node forced; mk_fixture pins CODEX_USER_CONFIG to a nonexistent path). timeout->exit 5 leaves NO artifact; cap-hit forces stopped_by=cap:max_findings; corrective codex-reply turn stub-recorded.
- J26 injection: hostile finding description with backticks/$() through review-record and resolve-finding summary -> NO shell execution, grammar intact. Finding text (location/evidence/description) correctly excluded from the gate-parsed comment.
- Secrets scan on new files: none. (OAuth work was not part of this task.)
- Out-of-scope confirmed: the 7 agent `model:` pins + settings CLAUDE_LATEST_OPUS are helper-written model-lane dirt (absent from changed-files.txt); not 1vq.1 deliverables.

### Findings
- A (MEDIUM, latent -> filed claude-workflow-plugin-vg8): a schema-VALID REVIEW-ARTIFACT with a newline in a header scalar (reviewed_hash) is accepted by validate-artifact, embedded by review-record, then truncated by the gate's split-newline-index-0 -> findings token drops to line 2 -> gate reports open=0/PASS despite a real critical finding. No live release path in V2 (gate not wired to release). validate-artifact is spec-faithful (closed error-key list); the gap is the unenforced single-line invariant. Fix belongs in validate-artifact (reject control chars in scalars) and/or the gate (treat a findings=-less artifact line as malformed).
- B (LOW, must-fix in-loop): codex-detect.sh spec line 133 calls `assert_not_contains`, undefined anywhere in the test tree. Under the runner's `set +e` it is a silent no-op (exit 127 to stderr), so the D7 "lane=codex NOT collapsed to a single model" negative guard never executes. The sibling positive assertion (rev:sol present) does run and pass, so the visible D7 outcome is covered. Trivial fix: define assert_not_contains in lib/assert.sh or use a grep-based negative check.

### Disposition
All 9 deliverables + all plan-mandated METAs green; D5 holds; grammars byte-exact; injection prevented; fixtures byte-identical. Both findings are non-blocking for this task's stated acceptance (no live release path; visible outcomes covered). Proceeding to rubric grading per section 6 (needs-grading relay) with both findings carried; not approving on this spawn.

### FINDING B (LOW, test integrity) — vacuous D7 negative guard
**Reproduced:** `specs/codex-detect.sh:133` called `assert_not_contains`, defined ONLY in the L1 `model-roles.test.sh` (different tier, never sourced by the L2 runner). Runner stderr: `assert_not_contains: command not found`; the spec printed **21** assertion lines and **0** mentioning the D7 negative guard. Under the runner's `set +e` it was a silent exit-127 no-op.

**Fix:** added a real `assert_not_contains` to `.claude/tests/component/lib/assert.sh` (mirrors `assert_contains`, inverted: PASS when absent, FAIL+forbidden/haystack message when present; bumps the shared counters so it is COUNTED). Header helper list updated.

**Sensitivity pair added** (the guard would now fail if lane=codex ever collapsed): positive control asserts the SAME all-equal role mapping with `reviewer_lane=claude` DOES render `• model:`, plus a negative that the collapsed render carries no `rev:sol`. So the guard demonstrably discriminates lane=codex from lane=claude. codex-detect spec: 21 → 24 counted assertions.

**Class sweep:** diffed every `assert_*/mk_*/shim_*` identifier called across all L2 specs against the definitions in `lib/` — **no other undefined helper** exists. That was the real risk (one silent no-op implies more).

### FINDING A (MEDIUM latent, vg8) — gate finding-suppression via embedded newline
**Reproduced end-to-end** (newline in `reviewed_hash`): (1) `validate-artifact` ACCEPTED it (exit 0); (2) the one-line record split — line 1 ended at `reviewed_hash=h`, line 2 began `EVIL-SECOND-LINE risk_threshold=high ... findings=[R1-F1:critical]`; (3) `gate` returned `open_findings=0, error_key="", exit 0` — a live **critical** finding silently suppressed.

**Fix, both layers (D5 purity intact — zero codex/lane refs added):**
1. `validate-artifact`: new error key `scalar_contains_control_char:<field>` rejecting newline/CR/tab (jq `[[:cntrl:]]`) in the scalars the record grammar EMBEDS — contract_version, task_id, reviewer_identity, reviewer_model, reviewed_hash, risk_threshold, verdict, stopped_by, `findings[].id`, `findings[].severity`. Runs BEFORE the enum/id-grammar checks so the error key names the real cause.
   *Deliberately PRECISE scope:* the reviewer's free-form prose (`location`/`evidence`/`description`) and the non-embedded `stop_condition` stay multi-line-legal — a blanket ban would reject legitimate Sol output and burn a corrective retry for zero safety gain. L1 pins both directions (multi-line `description`/`evidence` still ACCEPTED).
2. `gate` (defense in depth, TEXT-anchored `MALFORMED-ARTIFACT-GUARD-START/END`): a `^REVIEW-ARTIFACT v1 ` line lacking a **well-formed** `findings=[...]` token is now `review_artifact_malformed` (exit 4), never "zero findings". Strengthened beyond the brief to require a CLOSED bracket, because a newline inside a finding id yields `findings=[R1-F1` — a token that is present but unclosed, which a `lacks findings=` check would have missed. This also protects records ALREADY in a Beads DB (layer 1 can't retro-fix those).
3. `qa-gate.sh review-record`: **verified no change needed** — it validates through the review-check subprocess, so it now refuses the exploit artifact (exit 1, `scalar_contains_control_char:reviewed_hash`, **0** comments posted). qa-gate.sh is byte-unchanged, so only review-check.sh needed re-sync.

**Post-fix verification of the original exploit:** layer 1 exit 4 ✓ · layer 2 exit 4 `review_artifact_malformed` ✓ · review-record refused, zero comments posted ✓.

- L1 `review-check.test.sh` §2b: newline-in-reviewed_hash, CR-in-reviewer_identity, tab-in-reviewer_model, newline-in-finding-id, newline-in-finding-severity → exact error keys; plus two PRECISION cases (multi-line description/evidence still accepted). 30 → **39** assertions.

## Live Codex-doc verification — deltas vs the SPEC's assumed commands

Verified against: codex-cli 0.145.0 (installed), Claude Code 2.1.220, `learn.chatgpt.com/docs/*` (the `developers.openai.com/codex/*` paths 308-redirect there), and the shipped binary's own model catalog. Every command in CODEX_SETUP.md was EXECUTED on this machine; none of them invokes the `codex` tool, so verification cost $0.

**1. `model_reasoning_effort = "max"` IS accepted — the spec's "max if accepted, else xhigh" resolves to `max`.**
Two independent confirmations: the binary's embedded guidance ("GPT-5.6 supports `none`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, and `max`. If omitted, GPT-5.6 defaults to `medium`.") and the live catalog — `codex debug models` reports gpt-5.6-sol efforts = low, medium, high, xhigh, **max**, ultra, with max = "Maximum reasoning depth for the hardest problems". Doc recommends `max`, `xhigh` documented as the fallback.

**2. DOCS LAG (recorded in the doc).** The PUBLISHED config reference still lists `minimal | low | medium | high | xhigh` for `model_reasoning_effort` and does not mention `max`/`ultra`. The shipped binary accepts both. CODEX_SETUP.md states this explicitly instead of quoting the stale reference — and tells the reader to check `codex debug models` rather than trust either source. Related: `codex login status -c model_reasoning_effort=bogus` does NOT reject the value, so "try it and see" is not a valid verification path; the catalog query is.

**3. `ultra` exists and is exactly what the SPEC told me to avoid — now with a citation.** Catalog: "Maximum reasoning with automatic task delegation"; binary guidance: "Use Ultra reasoning effort for proactive multi-agent behavior". The doc names it and explains why automatic delegation breaks bounded diligence.

**4. SPEC ASSUMPTION SOFTENED: `codex mcp-server` is NOT undocumented upstream.** `learn.chatgpt.com/docs/mcp-server` documents the command, both tools (`codex`, `codex-reply`), `threadId` as the follow-up handle, and the `structuredContent` result shape — and does not label it experimental. The banner is therefore honest rather than wrong: the transport is documented, but (a) Claude-Code-as-the-client is community wiring, not an OpenAI-supported integration, and (b) the surface moves fast enough that the published config reference already lags the binary. Re-verify-on-edit instruction retained.

**5. Auth nuance.** The upstream MCP-server page states it requires an OpenAI API key. In practice ChatGPT-plan login also drives it: this machine reports `Logged in using ChatGPT` and `claude mcp get codex` -> `Status: ✔ Connected` (and 1vq.1's live `rev:sol` ran on that auth). Documented both paths with the billing split (plan credits vs Platform API rates).

**6. NEW, load-bearing, not in the SPEC: user scope is a MECHANICAL requirement, not just etiquette.** `codex-detect.sh` reads `.mcpServers.codex` from the TOP LEVEL of `~/.claude.json`. Verified empirically that `--scope local` writes to `.projects["<abs-path>"].mcpServers` in the same file (3 unrelated projects on this machine carry servers there) and `--scope project` writes the repo `.mcp.json`. The probe sees NEITHER -> `method=config-absent` -> silent Claude lane with no error. So the never-commit warning has two independent reasons, and "registered at the wrong scope" is the FIRST row of the troubleshooting table.

**7. Model-tracking mechanism found + verified (spec asked for "whatever the docs offer").** `codex debug models` renders the catalog with a `priority` preference ordering. Day-zero one-liner, executed: `codex debug models | jq -r '.models | map(select(.visibility=="list")) | sort_by(.priority) | .[0].slug'` -> `gpt-5.6-sol`. Full listing today: sol(1), terra(2), luna(3), gpt-5.5(7), gpt-5.4(16), gpt-5.4-mini(23).

**8. CORRECTION to the SPEC's pinning advice.** The spec preferred a config default over hard-pinning `-m`. But `codex-review.sh` derives the recorded `reviewer_model` from `CODEX_MCP_MODEL` -> a `-m`/`--model` pair in the REGISTERED ARGS -> else the literal string `codex`. Dropping `-m` still runs the config model but degrades the audit trail to `reviewer_model: "codex"`. The doc therefore recommends BOTH: config default (so interactive sessions track it too) AND keep `-m <slug>` in the registration (so the artifact records the real id), with a one-command refresh recipe.

**9. Stale-default trap documented.** The operator's `~/.codex/config.toml` pins `model = "gpt-5.2-codex"` — a slug no longer present in the catalog at all — while the registration's `-m` masks it for MCP runs. Documented generically as a "reconcile both" step. I did NOT modify anything outside the repo.

Doc commands executed successfully during verification: `command -v codex`/`--version`, `codex login status`, `claude mcp get codex`, `codex debug models` (both jq one-liners), `codex-detect.sh detect --refresh` -> `codex`, `codex-detect.sh status | jq -c '{reviewer_lane, method}'` -> `{"reviewer_lane":"codex","method":"handshake"}`. Additionally, the qa.md 6p.1 request-assembly snippet and the 6p.2 artifact schema were run verbatim against the real shipped validators: `validate-request` -> ok, `validate-artifact` -> ok, and a negative control (`stopped_by="bogus"`) -> exit 4 `stopped_by_invalid_enum`. `review-record` was deliberately NOT run against the live task (it would post a fake REVIEW-ARTIFACT comment into this task's audit trail); L1/L2 already cover it.

title: mutation-sweep.sh: per-mutant test-cmd inherits parser stdin (mutants.txt), drains it -> sweep stops after ~3-4 mutants
description:
Discovered during G2.6ix re-sweep (claude-workflow-plugin-llh.5).

SYMPTOM: a sweep over targets whose tests read stdin (verify-before-stop.sh / post-edit.sh / qa-gate.sh all do `INPUT=$(cat)`) reports e.g. killed:3 survived:0 generated:56 — only 3-4 of 56 mutants actually run; the rest are silently never processed. The summary looks "clean" (0 survivors) and is dangerously misleading.

ROOT CAUSE: the parser drive loop reads the mutant wire format via `while IFS= read -r line ... done < "$MUTANTS_FILE"` (mutation-sweep.sh ~line 469-502). For each mutant it calls run_mutant, which runs the per-mutant test command in a subshell at ~line 424-427:
    (
        cd "$wt" || exit 1
        CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR="$wt" timeout_cmd "$MUTANT_TEST_TIMEOUT_S" bash -c "$TEST_CMD"
    ) >/dev/null 2>&1 || test_rc=$?
stdin is NOT redirected, so fd0 is inherited from the `while read < mutants.txt` loop. When $TEST_CMD invokes a hook that does `INPUT=$(cat)` (or any bare `cat`/`read`), it consumes the REMAINING lines of mutants.txt. The parser's next `read` then hits EOF and the loop exits — the sweep terminates after only the mutants consumed before the first stdin-reading test.

IMPACT: any sweep whose test-cmd exercises stdin-reading code under-runs catastrophically and reports a falsely-clean survivor set. This silently defeats the whole tier for hook-script targets (the primary use case).

FIX (one line): redirect the per-mutant test invocation's stdin from /dev/null, e.g.
    ) </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1 || test_rc=$?
on the subshell at ~line 427. (Equivalent: `exec </dev/null` at the top of the subshell, or read the mutants file on a dedicated fd: `while read -u 9 ...; done 9< "$MUTANTS_FILE"`.)

WORKAROUND used in llh.5 (no production edit): prefixed the --test-cmd string with `exec </dev/null;`. With that prefix the sweep correctly processed all 56 mutants.

SECONDARY (lower severity): `MUTANT_TEST_TIMEOUT_S` (and SWEEP_TIMEOUT_S) are read as `${VAR:-default}` AFTER `. "$CONF"` sources mutation.conf, which sets them as plain assignments — so an env-var override is clobbered by the conf value. An operator passing `MUTANT_TEST_TIMEOUT_S=240` on the command line is silently ignored (stays 60). Consider honoring an env override (source conf with `:-` guards, or let a CLI flag win). Workaround: point MUTATION_CONF at a temp conf copy with the desired timeout.

Discovered-from: claude-workflow-plugin-llh.5 (G2.6ix survivor triage). Run that exposed it: .claude/.mutation-runs/20260613T100354Z (killed:3/56) vs the corrected .claude/.mutation-runs/20260613T102846Z (exec </dev/null + 240s timeout, all mutants processed).

comments.text:
<!-- BD-MCP-META: {"kind":"qa-note","source":"qa-agent","from_task":"claude-workflow-plugin-llh.5"} -->
## QA triage (from llh.5 gate review) — ledger impact + severity, NOT fixing here

Confirmed REAL by code read + live repro. Both halves reproduce:
- **stdin-drain** at `mutation-sweep.sh:424-427`: the per-mutant subshell runs `timeout_cmd ... bash -c "$TEST_CMD"` with only `>/dev/null 2>&1` (no stdin redirect); the parser loop reads `< "$MUTANTS_FILE"` (line ~502), so fd0 is the mutants file. All three intended sweep targets read stdin via bare `cat` (`verify-before-stop.sh:478`, `post-edit.sh:19`, `qa-gate.sh:1100` `raw=$(cat)`), so a custom test-cmd exercising them drains the mutants file -> early-stop.
- **conf-clobber** at `mutation-sweep.sh:65-71`: `[ -f "$CONF" ] && . "$CONF"` sources `mutation.conf` (plain assignments `MUTANT_TEST_TIMEOUT_S=60` line 41, `SWEEP_TIMEOUT_S=1800` line 47) BEFORE the `${VAR:-default}` lines, so an env override is silently clobbered.

**Live repro this session:** first re-sweep `20260613T100354Z` = generated 56 / killed 3 / survived 0 (early-stop, falsely-clean). I re-ran a scoped vbs sweep with the `exec </dev/null` workaround + temp-conf timeout and it processed past mutant 6 with 0 survivors — workaround confirmed effective.

### LEDGER IMPACT (for G4 / RELEASE_AUDIT.md) — narrower than first feared

365 does **NOT** retroactively invalidate the v3.4.0 C.3 acceptance numbers. I verified the original C.3 run `20260612T063107Z` processed **all 32 mutants** (killed:4 / survived:28; survivors span `verify-before-stop.sh:175..869` + `post-edit.sh:16..120`) — NOT a 3-4 early-stop. Reason: C.3 used the **default** `--test-cmd` (`DEFAULT_TEST_CMD="bash .claude/scripts/tests/run-tests.sh"`, the L1 suite), whose hook invocations pipe their *own* stdin (`echo '{...}' | bash hook`) and never inherit the sweep's fd0. So the CHANGELOG C.3 claim (32/4/28, 27 genuine/1 equivalent) and the calibration precision 0.9412 (computed over a fixed calibration-set, sweep-independent) both stand.

**But** the bug DOES narrow `RELEASE_AUDIT.md` row **R18** (currently PROVEN): the claim "runs them in throwaway git worktrees against the free L1/L2 tiers" holds only for the **default L1** test-cmd. Any **L2-inclusive custom `--test-cmd`** (which the claim implies is supported, and which is the natural way to exercise hook behavior) silently under-runs via this bug and reports a falsely-clean survivor set. Recommendation for G4: **drop R18 from PROVEN to PROVEN-WITH-CAVEAT** with this row cited, and add to this bug's description an explicit statement that it masks sweep coverage for custom (L2-inclusive) test-cmds. The bug currently documents the symptom but not the R18/C.3 relationship.

### Severity

P2 (current) is arguably light given the bug "silently defeats the whole tier for hook-script targets" with a falsely-clean report — the dangerous part is the *silent* under-run, not a loud failure. Consider P1, OR keep P2 but add a loud guard (assert processed==generated, or fail the sweep if survived==0 AND processed<<generated). Left open and unfixed per llh.5 scope; flagging for the G4 owner.

title: B.1 code-graph-mcp server: scaffold, indexer, 7 tools, tests
description: New .claude/mcp/code-graph-mcp/ (Node stdio, sibling layout). Zero-native-compile preferred: web-tree-sitter + vendored wasm grammars, wasm SQLite. Languages per detect-stack.sh: ts/js/tsx, python, go, rust, java, ruby, php, bash. Index .claude/.code-graph/index.db gitignored, incremental by content hash, lazy build on first tool call. 7 tools: code_search/code_context/symbol_callers byte-compatible with code-context-mcp; impact_of (transitive, depth cap); dead_code (unreferenced exports); dependency_path; code_index_health. bd-mcp error conventions. L3 vitest polyglot fixtures + incremental-reindex tests; L2 stdio boot spec; META-TEST corrupt index. Spec Phase B.
notes:
COMPLETED: .claude/mcp/code-graph-mcp/ scaffolded with the 7-tool surface:
code_search, code_context, code_index_health (byte-compatible with the
existing code-context-mcp), plus symbol_callers, impact_of, dead_code,
dependency_path (new-stable). Zero native compile.

GRAMMAR PROVENANCE: @vscode/tree-sitter-wasm@0.3.1 (MIT, published
2026-04). Vendored 10 .wasm grammars under grammars/ totalling 9.6 MB:
typescript (^0.23.2), tsx (^0.23.2), javascript (^0.25.0), python
(^0.25.0), go (^0.25.0), rust (vscode-built), java (^0.23.5), ruby
(^0.23.1), php (0.24.2), bash (^0.25.0). Full provenance table in
grammars/MANIFEST.md. We tried tree-sitter-wasms@0.1.13 first but it
ships the legacy 'dylink' custom-section name; web-tree-sitter 0.26
requires 'dylink.0'. The vscode-built grammars use the modern format.

SQLITE CHOICE: sql.js@1.14.1 (wasm). Spec mentioned node:sqlite (Node
22+) as an alternative; we stay on sql.js because the plugin floor is
Node 18.17. Trade-off: sql.js loads the whole DB into memory, but
realistic index sizes are a few MB so this is fine. Documented in
README + db.js header.

LAZY BUILD VERIFIED: server boot ~110ms (no DB read, no parsing); first
tool call triggers ensureIndex which preloads parsers and walks the
project; subsequent calls hit the warm DB in milliseconds.

LANGUAGE COVERAGE (honest, see README matrix):
- ts/tsx/js: defs (functions, classes, methods, types, exports), calls
  (incl. member+new), imports (relative paths resolved to local files
  via common extensions + index files)
- python: defs (def, class, top-level assignments), calls, imports
  (dotted modules resolved to .py / __init__.py)
- go: defs (incl. methods + type specs + consts/vars), calls (incl.
  selector method calls), imports (recorded by name only — module
  resolution not attempted)
- rust: defs (fn, struct, enum, trait, impl, mod, const, static),
  calls (incl. macros), imports (recorded by name only)
- java/ruby/php/bash: per-language def smoke + calls (tree-sitter-ruby
  0.23 removed method_call node — query updated accordingly)

WHAT THE STATIC GRAPH CAN'T SEE (echoed in tool descriptions): dynamic
dispatch, reflection / metaprogramming, macro expansion, renaming
re-exports, external library calls. dead_code carries an extra-loud
caveat block because false positives there are common (barrel
re-exports, externally consumed surface).

SYMBOL_CALLERS PREEXISTING: NO. The .mcp.json
_phase7_codebase_graph_target.tools_to_expose listed symbol_callers
but the current code-context-mcp ships only 3 tools (code_search /
code_context / code_index_health). It is new-stable with this server
and called out in the README.

TESTS:
- node:test suite (3 files, 31 tests, ~1.5s):
  - tests/indexer.test.js: 7 tests (cross-file resolution, incremental
    rebuild fires only on hash change, pruning drops deleted files,
    polyglot smoke for rust/java/ruby/php/bash, CORRUPT_INDEX contract,
    force=true)
  - tests/tools.test.js: 14 tests (all 7 tools incl. seeded transitive
    closure for impact_of, seeded orphan unusedHelper for dead_code,
    middle->deep dependency_path + not_connected branch, healthy/
    unhealthy/uninitialized health, both-seeds-present rejection)
  - tests/server.test.js: 9 protocol-level tests (Zod validation,
    structured error envelopes carry hint+example)
- L2 spec .claude/tests/component/specs/code-graph-mcp.sh: 29
  assertions covering boot, tools/list, health round-trip,
  malformed-args envelope, META-TEST corrupt-index reports unhealthy,
  META-TEST sensitivity (stub the detection branch, assert the
  unhealthy assertion now fails). Uses the rubric-loop.sh awk-stub +
  sentinel anchor-drift-guard pattern. All passing in make test-all
  (20 specs, 388 assertions total).

VERIFICATION RUN (cold-start stdio): initialize -> serverInfo.name=
code-graph-mcp / version=1.0.0; tools/list returns the 7 tools with
inputSchemas; code_search({query:"buildServer"}) returned 3 matches in
~3.3s wall (cold first build of the plugin repo). Subsequent calls are
ms. Pasted in the agent return JSON.

NOT TOUCHED (B.2 follows): .mcp.json, .claude-plugin/plugin.json,
code-context-mcp/. The new server is OFF the wire in this task. Gate
not approved; no commit, no push.

KEY DECISIONS:
- Dedupe symbols by (file_id, name, start_line, start_col) in the
  indexer's per-file map, merging is_export when an export_statement
  also captures the inner def. Without this, every exported symbol
  appears twice and the single-candidate resolver refuses to bind any
  edge to it.
- Skip-by-rel-path .claude/.code-graph + .claude/.qa-tracking instead
  of skipping .claude/ wholesale. The plugin's own source lives in
  .claude/, so a wholesale skip would make the server unable to index
  its own home repo (and any user-extended .claude/scripts/ tree).
- Lazy first build is in ensureIndex inside each tool handler — never
  in module init, never at server boot. Boot stays instant.
- File seed for impact_of uses the file's symbols PLUS file_dependents
  (importers). Symbol seed walks transitive callers only. Both seeds
  share the same nodes[] shape; file seed adds the file_dependents
  array.
- Errors carry both hint: and example: in every CodeGraphError. The
  example is a worked valid call so a self-correcting agent can retry
  without a human round-trip.

Includes the 4-option design menu inherited from 366.9 PLUS the mechanical option C (orchestrator pre-computes impact_of at root and embeds results in the QA delegation packet, making QA's job verification not invocation). References all 4 run traces (runs 1-4).
   - **claude-workflow-plugin-9ke** (p2, bug): label-milestones invariant structurally cannot pass on approve-flow runs (trace.beadsLabelTransitions is a net diff; transient qa-pending invisible). Two repair options (refine trace capture to record transition events vs redefine invariant as 'qa-approved implies cycle'); recommend Option 1. Evidence: run-3 + run-4 identical engine failure on demonstrably correct workflows (qa-gate.sh enter/approve calls present in both traces).
   - **claude-workflow-plugin-366.9** closed completed-with-followup: cue shipped to both surfaces and verified IN-FILE; run-4 demonstrated the channel gap; superseded by n6d.

3. **Run-4 anchor + seed trace**:
   - Copied cassettes/replays/node-react-auth-2026-06-12T02-18-12-871Z.jsonl to cassettes/seed/.
   - New .claude/tests/e2e/specs/_phase-b-run4-trace.unit.spec.ts (10 active assertions + 1 skipped artifact-missing branch). Pins:

4. **Working tree hygiene**: outer tree clean except legitimate additions:

   - cassettes/seed/node-react-auth-2026-06-12T02-18-12-871Z.jsonl (new seed copy).

   - No new worktree gitlinks; .gitignore rule from ac7b8b4 holds (verified: only worktrees dir is the fixture's internal .git/worktrees/, which is .gitignored).

   - make lint -> EXIT 0.
   - make test (L1) -> 12 specs / 87+ assertions / 0 fail.
   - make test-all (L2) -> 21 specs / 411 assertions / 0 fail.
   - make test-e2e-unit -> 13 specs / 158 pass / 5 skipped / 0 fail.

=== LLM OBSERVATIONS ===

The headline insight from run 4 is one we cannot get to from offline analysis: even with the most explicit possible cue ('use `mcp__plugin_claude-workflow_code-graph__impact_of` ... so the qa-queried-impact-of invariant is satisfied'), the QA agent did not invoke the tool. That changes the design space for n6d: the cue is not the bottleneck. The mechanical option (orchestrator pre-computes impact_of at root and embeds results) is the only path with a structural rather than a probabilistic guarantee, because the orchestrator either DOES make the call or it doesn't — and orchestrator behaviour on tool-call presence is much more predictable than QA's behaviour on a prose cue. That option also fits the role split cleaner: the orchestrator has the tools, QA does the review, results flow downhill.

The label-milestones bug is purely an instrumentation gap masquerading as a workflow violation; the workflow itself is fine. Filing as p2 because it does not affect production behaviour, only our ability to assert on it.

Ready for QA review.

title: Bug: test-live FIXTURE=<fixture> fails to resolve spec file when fixture name != spec name (5 of 7 fixtures unrunnable)
notes:
IN PROGRESS: Bug fixed under evidence-before-fix protocol.

G1 — Bug reproduction (before fix):
  Cmd: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=fake make test-live FIXTURE=node-react-auth CONFIRM=1
  Result: vitest filter "specs/node-react-auth.spec.ts" → "No test files found, exiting with code 1" → make rc=2
  Zero API spend: failure before any HTTP call.

ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED:
  Makefile's test-live built vitest filter as $(FIXTURE).spec.ts. Spec files
  are SCENARIO-named, not fixture-named. Verified the mapping from each
  spec's `FIXTURE_PATH = path.resolve(__dirname, "..", "fixtures", "<name>")`:
    node-react-auth        → happy-path.spec.ts          [MISMATCH]
    go-cli-refactor        → go-cli-refactor.spec.ts
    monorepo-frontend-only → monorepo-frontend-only.spec.ts
    multi-domain-signup    → multi-domain-signup.spec.ts
    python-django-bug      → python-django-bug.spec.ts
    qa-block-recovery      → qa-block-recovery.spec.ts
    rubric-revision-loop   → rubric-revision-loop.spec.ts
  Only node-react-auth is mismatched (task prompt said only rubric-revision-loop
  was 1:1; actually 6/7 are — the lone exception is node-react-auth).
  Makefile's own help (line 49) and README docs advertise FIXTURE=node-react-auth,
  so fixture name is the documented interface.

G2 — Failing test (before fix):
  New L2 component spec: .claude/tests/component/specs/resolve-fixture-spec.sh
  17 assertions across 6 acceptance points. Run pre-fix:
  Specs: Total: 1  Passed: 0  Failed: 1
  Assertions: Passed: 1  Failed: 16
  (Failures: every resolver invocation hits "No such file or directory" —
   the helper didn't exist yet, which is the precise failure shape we want
   the test to surface.)

RESOLUTION MECHANISM:
  Added .claude/scripts/resolve-fixture-spec.sh (new helper). It scans
  .claude/tests/e2e/specs/*.spec.ts for a path.resolve(...,"fixtures",
  "<FIXTURE>") reference and prints the matching spec filename. Unknown
  fixture → exit 1 with a listing of available fixtures on stderr. Missing
  arg → exit 2 + usage. Honours CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR for installed-plugin
  scenarios; falls back to script-relative plugin-root derivation. Skips
  underscore-prefixed unit specs (_*.unit.spec.ts) so they can't shadow
  a live spec match.

  Makefile test-live now (a) resolves first, then prompts — so a typoed
  FIXTURE fails fast before the cost preview, (b) shells out to the helper
  per fixture, (c) prints "resolved spec(s) -> <list>" so the user sees
  the resolved targets BEFORE confirming, (d) preserves FIXTURE=required,
  cost-confirmation, multi-fixture FIXTURES=, and CONFIRM=1 behaviour.

  Resolver design rationale documented inline in the script header: the
  alternative — a static dispatch table — would drift the next time
  someone adds a spec, which is the exact regression class we're fixing.
  Scanning the source-of-truth (the spec's own FIXTURE_PATH constant)
  means the resolver stays correct without an extra maintenance burden.

FILES CHANGED:
  .claude/scripts/resolve-fixture-spec.sh                  (new — 92 LOC)
  .claude/tests/component/specs/resolve-fixture-spec.sh    (new — 110 LOC)
  Makefile                                                 (test-live recipe)

G3 — Failing test now passes (post-fix):
  Specs: Total: 1  Passed: 1  Failed: 0
  Assertions: Passed: 17  Failed: 0

FULL TEST SUITE:
  make lint:       rc=0 (shellcheck clean — explicit shellcheck of new
                   files also rc=0)
  make test-all:   L1 unit 20+25+31+30+87 + worktree(10) = clean,
                   L2 component Specs 21/21 Passed, Assertions 409/0 Pass/Fail

POST-FIX DRY-PROOF (no CONFIRM=1, fake API key — must abort at prompt
without starting any paid run):
  $ ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=fake-key-for-dry-proof make test-live FIXTURE=node-react-auth < /dev/null
  test-live: about to run 1 live fixture(s): node-react-auth
  test-live: resolved spec(s) -> happy-path.spec.ts
  test-live: estimated cost ~ $5-$10 USD (Claude Opus 4.7; 2026-05 baseline)
  test-live: proceed? (y/N) test-live: aborted.
  (RESOLVED SPEC IS PRINTED BEFORE THE PROMPT. ZERO API SPEND.)

CASSETTE-DIFF AUDIT (per task — "check cassette-diff for the same
mapping assumption"):
  cassette-diff is NOT affected. Cassettes are written by runFixture as
  `<fixture>-<ISO>.jsonl` (see .claude/tests/e2e/lib/runFixture.ts:684)
  using path.basename(fixturePath), so files in cassettes/replays/ and
  cassettes/golden/ are FIXTURE-NAMED (e.g. cassettes/golden/node-react-auth.jsonl,
  not happy-path.jsonl). The cassette-diff recipe constructs paths from
  FIXTURE directly and matches the on-disk reality. Confirmed by ls of
  cassettes/golden/ and cassettes/replays/.

COST-TABLE AUDIT (per task — "verify names there match real fixtures"):
  Makefile lines 58-63 list per-fixture cost estimates. Names: node-react-auth,
  go-cli-refactor, monorepo-frontend-only, multi-domain-signup, python-django-bug,
  qa-block-recovery — ALL real fixtures (verified by ls fixtures/). No spec
  names leak. rubric-revision-loop is not in the table (it joined later);
  out of scope for this bug fix.

LLM OBSERVATIONS:
  - The task prompt's "only rubric-revision-loop has 1:1 fixture↔spec naming"
    is inverted — actually 6/7 fixtures are 1:1; node-react-auth is the
    lone outlier. The bug's symptom is correct but the diagnosis-prompt

    unrunnable" (in the bd title) is also wrong: just 1 fixture is broken.
    Title remains accurate enough for now (the broader interface is broken

  - "find the L2 component spec from 0.8" — no such existing spec covers
    test-live's guards. I created the first L2 coverage for test-live as

   'mcp__puppeteer matches any tool provided by the puppeteer server'
   'mcp__puppeteer__* wildcard syntax that also matches all tools from the puppeteer server'
   'mcp__puppeteer__puppeteer_navigate matches the puppeteer_navigate tool'
   The same naming registry applies to subagent 'tools:' allowlist entries
   (the docs do not show MCP entries in 'tools:' examples but the canonical
   tool-naming registry is shared across the permission system).
   Plugin-bundled MCP tool form (code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp):
   'mcp__plugin_<plugin-name>_<server-name>__<tool-name>'.

     mcp__plugin_claude-workflow_code-graph  (plugin-load prefix, code-graph)
     mcp__plugin_claude-workflow_bd          (plugin-load prefix, bd)
     mcp__code-graph                         (project-scope prefix, code-graph)
     mcp__bd                                 (project-scope prefix, bd)
   Both prefixes are declared because plugin.json and .mcp.json register the
   servers under different prefixes (plugin-load = full plugin-namespaced;
   project-scope = bare server name). The agent files are bundled by
   plugin.json AND committed to the project tree, so either path can be the

title: Dirty-on-entry recovery wipes uncommitted fixture.yaml before snapshotHarnessMetadata captures it
description: Cause B from Run 3 forensic. In runFixture.ts the order is: (1) dirty-on-entry check runs 'git reset --hard HEAD && git clean -fd' at lines 811-818; (2) snapshotFixture runs at line 838 which calls snapshotHarnessMetadata. If the fixture's nested-git HEAD does not contain the operator's intended fixture.yaml (e.g. the outer plugin repo updated fixture.yaml in commit 256e0c1 but the fixture's nested git HEAD = 7207544 'auto-init' predates that), the operator's edit appears as uncommitted relative to the nested HEAD. The dirty recovery wipes it, snapshot captures already-wiped bytes, and the end-of-run restore writes the wiped bytes back. Net: fixture.yaml -28 lines vs outer HEAD on disk, satisfiesInvariants() fails with 'no invariants declared'.
notes:
COMPLETED OFFLINE (no paid runs). Evidence-before-fix protocol followed.

=== ROOT CAUSE (verbatim, with citations) ===

In runFixture.ts (pre-fix), the dirty-on-entry self-heal at lines 811-818 ran BEFORE snapshotFixture at line 838. Sequence in run 3 of Phase B:
  1. Fixture's nested git HEAD = 7207544 ('fixture: initial state (auto-init)', Mon May 11 2026) predates the outer plugin repo's invariants commit 256e0c1 (Fri Jun 12 2026).
  2. Outer repo's fixture.yaml has the invariants block; inner repo sees those 28 lines as UNCOMMITTED relative to its own HEAD.
  3. runFixture sees 'git status --porcelain' dirty → fires recovery: 'git reset --hard HEAD && git clean -fd -e node_modules'.
  4. Reset wipes the operator's intended invariants block. clean wipes crash-leftover untracked files.
  5. snapshotFixture(line 838) calls snapshotHarnessMetadata which now reads the POST-RESET (no-invariants) fixture.yaml bytes.
  6. End-of-run restoreHarnessMetadata writes those post-reset bytes back → working tree ends -28 lines vs outer HEAD.
  7. Mid-run, satisfiesInvariants() reads the file at this state → parseInvariantsFromYaml returns 0 → matcher fails with 'no invariants declared in fixture.yaml'.

Empirical verification offline:

title: Bug: MANUAL_ADOPT_REQUIRED gate is dead — subshell mutation lost; cmd_apply auto-rewrites pins despite unparseable created_at
description:
**Severity**: P0. Hotfix vlp.1's contract violated — "never silent stale pin" is unenforceable in production.

**Repro** (offline; bash /tmp/probe-manual.sh):

```
# Listing has ONE entry, claude-fable-5, with unparseable created_at "BOGUS-DATE".
# Current pin: claude-opus-4-7.
# Per contract (model-select.sh:49-52, 496-503): apply must REFUSE the rewrite and emit the LOUD adopt notice; the session keeps the current pin.

Pin BEFORE: claude-opus-4-7
model-select: winner 'claude-fable-5' has missing/unparseable created_at; manual adoption required: /workflow-model claude-fable-5
updated: orchestrator: claude-opus-4-7 -> claude-fable-5
updated: qa: claude-opus-4-7 -> claude-fable-5
updated: backend: claude-opus-4-7 -> claude-fable-5
updated: frontend: claude-opus-4-7 -> claude-fable-5
updated: devops: claude-opus-4-7 -> claude-fable-5
model-select: switched claude-opus-4-7 -> claude-fable-5
Pin AFTER:  claude-fable-5
```

The notice fires (via _warn — stderr passes through subshells), but the gate at cmd_apply:500 NEVER prevents the rewrite. The pin IS changed.

**Root cause** (file:line evidence):

`.claude/scripts/model-select.sh:491` reads `best=$(pick_best "$models")`. The `$(...)` is a command substitution subshell. Inside pick_best, line 341 does `MANUAL_ADOPT_REQUIRED="$picked_id"`. Bash semantics: variable assignments inside a `$(...)` subshell modify the subshell-local copy only; the parent process's variable is untouched. So when cmd_apply checks `if [ -n "$MANUAL_ADOPT_REQUIRED" ]` at line 500, it always sees the empty string from line 89. The "loud notice + manual /workflow-model adopt" contract documented at lines 49-52 of the file header is bypassed in 100% of unparseable-date cases.

Same subshell pattern at lines 468 (cmd_resolve) and 551 (cmd_status); the impact at those sites is smaller (no rewrite) but the manual-adopt gate is uniformly dead.

**Why the L2 spec missed it**: specs A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H, X, Y, Z, W, I cover happy paths + exclusion + cache + sort tie-break + lying picker. ZERO assertions exercise the unparseable-created_at branch. The MANUAL_ADOPT_REQUIRED gate is untested.

**Fix sketch** (two viable approaches):

1. Pass MANUAL_ADOPT_REQUIRED out of pick_best via stdout sentinel. Have pick_best print `MANUAL\t<id>` on the manual-adopt path and `<id>` otherwise; have cmd_apply parse the prefix.
2. Write MANUAL_ADOPT_REQUIRED to a temp file inside pick_best and have callers read it after the substitution. (Less clean — relies on shared filesystem state.)

Approach 1 is cleaner: the sentinel travels via the already-used stdout channel, no shared mutable global needed.

**Required regression tests**:
- L2 spec: unparseable created_at on winner -> apply refuses rewrite (assert pin unchanged); resolve still prints the id with the LOUD notice on stderr; status surfaces "cached best: <id> (manual adopt required)".
- L2 spec META-TEST: strip the gate from cmd_apply, assert the preceding test fails (sensitivity).

**Scope**: Item 1 of hotfix vlp.1 must be re-opened. The other vlp.1 deliverables (created_at sort, exclusion semantics, --refresh, statusline pin, ranking rewrite, docs sweep) are intact and verified.

Discovered during QA review 2026-06-12 of vlp.1 by atsamaz@preql.com.

title: F2/F4/F5/F7/F8 ignore COMMAND_EXCLUSIONS; fault-classes.md claim is false
description:
Phase C.1 mutation generator: only F1, F3, F6 invoke should_skip(), which is the function that enforces COMMAND_EXCLUSIONS. F2 (guard deletion), F4 (variable-default removal), F5 (pipeline-segment drop), F7 (sentinel mutation), and F8 (arithmetic) all read the target file line-by-line WITHOUT checking should_skip. fault-classes.md lines 232-235 claim 'The generator pattern list explicitly skips any line whose first token is in the exclusion set (mutation.conf key command_exclusions).' This is materially false for 5/8 fault classes.

Currently latent — no destructive-command-with-mutatable-shape lines exist in .claude/scripts/*.sh. Becomes exploitable the moment a target with such a line is added or mutated manually.

Mutants apply inside a throwaway worktree (good) but the test command runs with the user's environment (inheriting $HOME, $SAFE_BASE, etc.). A mutant of `rm -rf "${SAFE_BASE:-/tmp/safe}"` becomes `rm -rf "${SAFE_BASE}"` and IF that env var is set to the user's home in the parent shell, the mutant deletes $HOME despite the worktree containment.

Fix: add `should_skip "$line" && continue` to gen_f2, gen_f4, gen_f5, gen_f7, gen_f8 — symmetric with F1/F3/F6. Add an L1 assertion: for each fault class, build a fixture with an rm-shaped trigger line and assert the generator emits zero mutants.

Proof in QA notes:

  PROBE target:
    rm -rf "${HOME:-/}"            (F4 trigger)
    rm -rf "${SAFE_BASE:-/tmp/safe-default-dir}"  (F4 trigger)
    rm -f file | grep foo | wc -l    (F5 trigger)
    rm -rf qa-approved.lock          (F7 trigger)
    rm -f "$((COUNTER + 1)).log"    (F8 trigger)

  Actual generator output:
    F4 emitted 3 mutants (all 'rm -rf ...' lines)
    F5 emitted 1 mutant (drops 'grep foo' segment)
    F7 emitted 1 mutant ('qa-approved' -> 'qa-approve')
    F8 emitted 1 mutant ('+ 1' -> '+ 2')

```bash
# --------------------
```

```bash
# denylist-shared.sh component spec — claude-workflow-plugin-3mg.1 (Phase V4).
#
# ONE definition of "which paths are reviewable", three consumers:
#
#   post-edit.sh           what gets TRACKED into changed-files.txt
#   impact-report.sh       what enters the canonical change set + its HASH
#   verify-before-stop.sh  what the Stop gate treats as needing REVIEW
#
# The L1 spec denylist-source.test.sh guards the STRUCTURE (all three source
# `.claude/scripts/workflow-denylist.sh`, none carries a literal copy). This
# spec guards the BEHAVIOUR: a single edit to the lib must move all three
# consumers at once, and the two patterns 3mg.1 added must actually change
# what the gate sees.
#
# WHY IT MATTERS (the defect that motivated the consolidation)
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Before 3mg.1 only verify-before-stop's copy knew about `.claude/worktrees/`
# and the e2e fixture churn. post-edit therefore TRACKED worktree paths that
# the Stop gate could not SEE: they entered the change-set hash the approval
# is bound to while being invisible to the gate's own view of the change set.
# The hash and the gate disagreed about what "the changes" were, and the only
# symptom was an occasional un-releasable approval nobody could explain.
#
# SECTIONS
#   A. CANARY (the sensitivity proof). One pattern added to the lib, three
#      consumers observed. Each leg is asserted BEFORE the edit (control) and
#      AFTER (effect), then the lib is restored and the control re-asserted —
#      so a green run cannot come from fixture drift.
#   B. MEMORY PATTERNS (shipped behaviour). MEMORY.md and .claude/memory/
#      leave the reviewable set BEFORE F1 doc-only classification, so a
#      memory-only change set releases with NO gate record instead of being
#      auto-approved as `doc-only`. CLAUDE.md is the anti-overreach control:
#      it is behaviour-bearing and must still gate.
#   C. HASH MIGRATION. Changing the denylist re-hashes recomputed change sets,
#      so an approval recorded before the change no longer matches and the
#      gate re-blocks (LABEL_WITHOUT_RECORD). That is the correct fail-closed
#      direction; this section pins BOTH the block and the recovery path that
#      actually works. See the C4 note — the remediation the block reason
#      prints is incomplete, and this spec pins that gap rather than papering
#      over it.
#
# THE SYMLINK HAZARD (read before editing this file)
# --------------------------------------------------
# mk_fixture SYMLINKS the plugin's real scripts into the fixture. An in-place
# `sed -i` against `$FIXTURE/.claude/scripts/workflow-denylist.sh` can rewrite
# THE REAL PLUGIN FILE through the link. Every mutation here goes through
# mutate_denylist_lib, which `rm`s the symlink and `cp`s a private copy FIRST,
# and A5 asserts afterwards that the real plugin lib is still canary-free.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helpers shared by all three sections.

# mutate_denylist_lib <fixture> <extra-alternative>
#   Replace the fixture's workflow-denylist.sh SYMLINK with a private copy
#   whose WORKFLOW_DENYLIST_REGEX gains <extra-alternative> as a leading
#   alternation branch. Prints the real (plugin) path it copied from so the
#   caller can restore the symlink.
mutate_denylist_lib() {
    local root="$1" alt="$2"
    local lib="$root/.claude/scripts/workflow-denylist.sh"
    local real
    real=$(readlink "$lib" 2>/dev/null || printf '%s' "$lib")
    rm -f "$lib"                 # break the link BEFORE writing anything
    cp "$real" "$lib"
    chmod +x "$lib"
    # -i.bak is the spelling both BSD and GNU sed accept.
    sed -i.bak "s#^WORKFLOW_DENYLIST_REGEX='#WORKFLOW_DENYLIST_REGEX='${alt}|#" "$lib"
    rm -f "$lib.bak"
    printf '%s' "$real"
}

restore_denylist_lib() {
    local root="$1" real="$2"
    local lib="$root/.claude/scripts/workflow-denylist.sh"
    rm -f "$lib"
    ln -sf "$real" "$lib"
}

# hash_of <fixture> <line>...  — the canonical change-set hash impact-report.sh
# computes for a tracker containing exactly <line>... This is the same
# `--hash-only` entry point qa-gate.sh approve and the Stop gate use, so the
# assertions below measure the shipping hash, not a re-implementation.
hash_of() {
    local root="$1"; shift
    local tracker="$root/.claude/.qa-tracking/changed-files.txt"
    : > "$tracker"
    local l
    for l in "$@"; do printf '%s\n' "$l" >> "$tracker"; done
    CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR="$root" bash "$root/.claude/scripts/impact-report.sh" --hash-only 2>/dev/null || echo ""

# hook does and report whether the path landed in changed-files.txt.
track_path() {
    local root="$1" p="$2"
    local tracker="$root/.claude/.qa-tracking/changed-files.txt"
    : > "$tracker"
    printf '{"tool_input":{"file_path":"%s"}}' "$p" \
        | CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR="$root" bash "$root/.claude/scripts/post-edit.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1
```

```bash
printf 'src/pre.ts\n' > "$TRACK3"
TID3B=$(cd "$F3" && bd create "second cycle, same session" -t task -p 1 -l devops,qa-pending --json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.id // empty')
bash "$QG3" enter "$TID3B" >/dev/null 2>&1
assert_eq "gbv2-3.4: a second enter leaves the existing baseline byte-identical" \
    "$B3_BEFORE" "$(cat "$BASE3")"

# ===========================================================================
# SECTION 4 — approve: FULL refresh.
#
# Approve means "everything dirty right now has been reviewed", so the whole
# working tree becomes the new reference point — including the files enter
# deliberately excluded.
# ===========================================================================
# Tracker set BEFORE enter: enter regenerates the impact report for the
# CURRENT change set, and approve refuses on a stale report — so changing the
# tracker after enter would make this section measure the staleness refusal
# instead of the baseline refresh.
printf 'src/edited.ts\n' > "$TRACK3"
bash "$QG3" enter "$TID3" >/dev/null 2>&1
bash "$CT3" set "$TID3"
seed_review_records "$TID3" "qa-claude" "backend" "$F3"
APPROVE4=$(bash "$QG3" approve "$TID3" "reviewed the session's edit" 2>&1 | tail -1)
# Assert the approve actually landed. Without this, every assertion below
# would silently degrade into "enter's baseline is still there".
assert_json_field "gbv2-4.0: approve succeeded" "$APPROVE4" '.status' "approved"
assert_eq "gbv2-4.1: provenance names qa-gate-approve" \
    "qa-gate-approve" "$(baseline_header_field "$BASE3" captured_by)"
B4_BODY=$(baseline_body "$BASE3")
assert_contains "gbv2-4.2: the refreshed baseline now INCLUDES the approved edit" \
    "src/edited.ts" "$B4_BODY"
assert_contains "gbv2-4.2: ...and still the pre-existing dirt" "src/pre.ts" "$B4_BODY"
# 4.3 Consequence: nothing is left to gate.
: > "$TRACK3"
bash "$CT3" clear
assert_eq "gbv2-4.3: after approve the tree matches the baseline and Stop releases" \
    "ALLOW" "$(stop_decision "$F3")"

# ===========================================================================
# SECTION 5 — legacy `approved-baseline`: read for one release, retired on the
# first v2 write. An install that upgrades mid-cycle must not lose its
# reference point and get a spurious full-tree block.
# ===========================================================================
LEGACY3="$F3/.claude/.qa-tracking/approved-baseline"
LEGACY_BODY=$(cd "$F3" && git status --porcelain | LC_ALL=C sort)
rm -f "$BASE3"
printf '%s\n' "$LEGACY_BODY" > "$LEGACY3"
: > "$TRACK3"
bash "$CT3" clear
assert_eq "gbv2-5.1: a v1 approved-baseline is still honoured when no v2 file exists" \
    "ALLOW" "$(stop_decision "$F3")"
# 5.2 A new pre-dirty file is still NEW relative to the legacy snapshot.
printf 'export const post = 1;\n' > "$F3/src/post-legacy.ts"
: > "$TRACK3"
assert_eq "gbv2-5.2: dirt not in the legacy snapshot still blocks" \
    "block" "$(stop_decision "$F3")"
# 5.3 The first v2 write retires the legacy file.
CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR="$F3" bash "$QG3" baseline-capture --by test-harness >/dev/null 2>&1
assert_eq "gbv2-5.3: the first v2 write created the v2 file" "yes" \
    "$([ -f "$BASE3" ] && echo yes || echo no)"
assert_eq "gbv2-5.3: ...and deleted the legacy approved-baseline" "no" \
    "$([ -f "$LEGACY3" ] && echo yes || echo no)"

# ===========================================================================
# SECTION 6 — THE `-d .git` FIX, in a real linked worktree.
#
# In a linked worktree `.git` is a FILE containing `gitdir: ...`, so the old
# `[ -d "$PROJECT_DIR/.git" ]` predicate answered NO. Two things silently
# switched off there: the baseline writer (approve wrote nothing) and the Stop
# gate's git-status fallback. With an empty changed-files.txt the gate then
# had NO detector at all — it FAILED OPEN and released unreviewed work, in
# exactly the isolation:"worktree" topology the plugin tells agents to use.
# Both predicates now ask `git rev-parse --git-dir`.
#
# The worktree is created OUTSIDE the fixture on purpose: a checkout under
# `.claude/worktrees/` is denylisted, which would mask the very detection
# this section measures.
# ===========================================================================
WT_PARENT=$(mktemp -d -t gbv2-worktree.XXXXXX)
WT="$WT_PARENT/linked"
WT_OK=1
(cd "$F3" && git worktree add -q "$WT" -b gbv2-linked) >/dev/null 2>&1 || WT_OK=0

if [ "$WT_OK" != "1" ] || [ ! -e "$WT/.git" ]; then
    printf 'SKIPPED: gate-baseline-v2 section 6 (git worktree add unavailable in this environment)\n'
else
    # Give the worktree the hook surface a real checkout has.
    mkdir -p "$WT/.claude/scripts" "$WT/.claude/.qa-tracking"
    for s in "$(plugin_root)"/.claude/scripts/*.sh; do
        [ -f "$s" ] || continue
        ln -sf "$s" "$WT/.claude/scripts/$(basename "$s")"
    done
    fast_stack_stub "$WT"
    BASE_WT="$WT/.claude/.qa-tracking/gate-baseline"
    TRACK_WT="$WT/.claude/.qa-tracking/changed-files.txt"
    : > "$TRACK_WT"

    # 6.1 The precondition that broke the old predicate.
    assert_eq "gbv2-6.1: the linked worktree's .git is a FILE, not a directory" "file" \
        "$([ -d "$WT/.git" ] && echo dir || { [ -f "$WT/.git" ] && echo file || echo missing; })"
    assert_eq "gbv2-6.1: ...so the old \`-d .git\` predicate would have said NO" "no" \
        "$([ -d "$WT/.git" ] && echo yes || echo no)"
    assert_eq "gbv2-6.1: ...while rev-parse --git-dir says YES" "yes" \
        "$(git -C "$WT" rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo yes || echo no)"

    # 6.2 The writer works there now. Pre-fix it took the "no git repo" arm,
    # removed any baseline and returned success — no snapshot, silently.
    printf 'export const w = 1;\n' > "$WT/src/pre.ts"
    CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR="$WT" bash "$WT/.claude/scripts/qa-gate.sh" \
        baseline-capture --by test-harness >/dev/null 2>&1
    assert_eq "gbv2-6.2: baseline-capture writes a snapshot inside a linked worktree" "yes" \
        "$([ -f "$BASE_WT" ] && echo yes || echo no)"
    assert_contains "gbv2-6.2: the worktree snapshot carries the worktree's dirt" \
        "src/pre.ts" "$(baseline_body "$BASE_WT")"

    # 6.3 With everything baselined the gate releases — no false block.
    : > "$TRACK_WT"
    assert_eq "gbv2-6.3: a fully-baselined worktree releases" "ALLOW" "$(stop_decision "$WT")"

    # 6.4 THE load-bearing assertion. New dirt after the baseline must BLOCK.
    # Pre-fix the fallback never ran in a worktree, so this released: the gate
    # failed OPEN on genuinely unreviewed work.
    printf 'export const unreviewed = 1;\n' > "$WT/src/unreviewed.ts"
    : > "$TRACK_WT"
    assert_eq "gbv2-6.4: unreviewed new work in a linked worktree BLOCKS (was: failed open)" \
        "block" "$(stop_decision "$WT")"
    # Causation, as in 1.4: remove ONLY the unreviewed path; the baselined
    # dirt stays put and the release comes back.
    rm -f "$WT/src/unreviewed.ts"
    : > "$TRACK_WT"
    assert_eq "gbv2-6.4: precondition — the baselined dirt is STILL dirty" \
        "1" "$(dirt_lines "$WT" | grep -c 'src/pre\.ts' | tr -d '[:space:]')"
    assert_eq "gbv2-6.4: removing ONLY the unreviewed path restores the release" \
        "ALLOW" "$(stop_decision "$WT")"

    (cd "$F3" && git worktree remove --force "$WT") >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
fi
rm -rf "$WT_PARENT"

[ "$FAIL" -eq 0 ]
```
