## 5. LESSONS.md
# Lessons ledger

Production lessons learned the hard way. Each entry is a single-sentence
takeaway, traceable to the Beads task(s) that produced it, with the date
it was first recorded.

Add new entries via `.claude/scripts/lessons.sh add '<lesson>' --source <task-id>`
— never hand-edit. The helper deduplicates by normalized text (case- and
whitespace-insensitive), so repeating an existing lesson appends the new
source to that entry rather than creating a duplicate. The only legitimate
hand-edit is pruning entries that are no longer relevant.

The orchestrator reads this file during planning (see `orchestrator.md`),
the grader (Phase A) receives it in the grading packet, and the QA agent
proposes additions at epic close. Treat it as the institutional memory the
plugin runs against, not a static reference doc.

## Lessons

- Parallel agents in the same working tree contaminate each other's branches; concurrent specialists require worktree isolation. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-e0d.7 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-11 -->
- Boundary mocks must use the real downstream producer's shape, pinned via a fixture extracted from the producer's spec — never invented. A mock that feeds `body.error` so the test can assert `body.error` is circular and proves nothing. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-e0d.7 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-11 -->
- New agent files must be registered in .claude-plugin/plugin.json agents[] in the same commit that creates them; an unregistered agent is silently invisible to the SDK — no error surfaces. Guard: agents-manifest-parity test. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-l1r.5 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-11 -->
- Subagents cannot spawn other subagents in the Claude Code runtime (docs: sub-agents page — Agent(agent_type) has no effect in subagent definitions). Any agent-spawning step must live at the root conversation level; design multi-agent handoffs as root-orchestrated relays, never nested spawns. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-l1r.5 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-11 -->
- Interface examples must be executed by a test: the Makefile's own usage string (make test-live FIXTURE=node-react-auth) was broken for the one fixture whose spec file is scenario-named — nothing ever ran the documented invocation. Caught only when a paid live run failed fast. Any CLI surface a doc or help text advertises needs an L2 assertion that executes that exact invocation (dry-run mode where the real one costs money). <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-366.4 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-11 -->
- Prose cues do not reliably drive subagent tool usage: across 4 live runs, QA made zero impact_of calls even when its task prompt contained the exact tool name, alias, target symbols, and invariant name. When a workflow REQUIRES a tool call, make it mechanical (compute it where calls are reliable — e.g. orchestrator at root — and pass results down), don't prompt for it. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-n6d --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-12 -->
- Rendered fixture installs pin plugin scripts at render time: the fixture's verify-before-stop.sh predated the cue fix by one commit, so a hook-template change never reached the live run. Script-level fixes require re-rendering fixture installs (or a version check at run start) before they affect live validation. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-366.10 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-12 -->
- Never run QA review concurrently with a builder in the same working tree: QA attributed the parallel C.2 task's freshly-written files to the C.1 task under review and blocked it for scope creep. Sequence QA after all writers finish, or give builders worktree isolation (orchestrator.md 4b exists for exactly this). <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-n45.1 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-12 -->
- Manifest-declared assets must be presence-asserted at the install target: install.sh's hardcoded agent list silently dropped grader.md for two releases (v3.2.0-v3.3.0) — every fresh install was missing the rubric loop's grader while the repo's own tests stayed green. Glob-copy from the manifest source of truth and add an installer-spec presence assertion for every plugin.json agents[]/commands[] entry. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-n45.4 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-12 -->
- Bash functions invoked via $(...) command substitution run in a subshell — any variable they set is lost to the parent. The manual-adopt gate in model-select.sh was dead code for exactly this reason (set at :341, read at :500, never connected). When a helper must signal the caller, encode the signal in its stdout contract (e.g. a MANUAL<tab> prefix) and parse it at every call site; add a META-TEST that strips the parse to prove the gate is load-bearing. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-3fn --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-12 -->
- A security hardening that breaks the workflow is worse than the documented residual it closes. Fail-closing prevent-orchestrator-edits.sh on ambiguous identity assumed every specialist carries a probeable identity, but this runtime does not surface subagent_name to PreToolUse hooks — so it denied legitimate specialist Write/Edit (a P0-class regression) to close a P2 Bash-write vector. When a guard depends on an identity signal the runtime may not provide, prefer fail-OPEN plus the structural guard (the orchestrator's omitted Write/Edit tools, which IS airtight) and document the residual; never trade a P2 for a P0. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-llh.19 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-13 -->
- Line-number-anchored mutation META-tests are brittle: any comment or line addition above the anchor silently un-lands the NR==<n>/sed -n Np target, turning a load-bearing META into a no-op (or a spurious failure). Anchor mutation METAs to a unique TEXT pattern in the target line, not an absolute line number. (3 instances re-anchored across verify-before-stop/escalation-binding specs this session.) <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-llh.20 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-13 -->
- Effort A/B (cnz.2): verdict max — ultracode showed ZERO orchestration interference in a 39-min time-boxed arm (no Workflow-layer engagement, all spawns on-list, plugin flow faithful), contradicting the pre-registered criterion-4-failure expectation; max still wins because ultracode pins the model at its xhigh proxy (below max) with no observed benefit, and criteria 2-3 went unverified under the time-box. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-cnz.2 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-07-25 -->
- Paid-run cost estimates must be derived from measured token flows, not guessed: the EFFORT-AB-TEST runbook estimated $10-20 for both arms; actual was ~$206 API-equivalent (~$169 arm B full + ~$37 arm A time-boxed) — a 10x error that forced a mid-test re-confirmation gate. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-cnz.2 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-07-25 -->

# Default rubric (v1)

Applies to every task graded under the rubric-grader QA loop (spec Phase A). Each criterion below is a pass/fail assertion the grader evaluates from the grading packet: `bd show` for the task, the SPEC doc, the diff of the files listed in `.qa-tracking/changed-files.txt`, the F7 completion contract returned by the specialist, and `LESSONS.md`. One-line justification per criterion. No numeric score theater — pass or fail.

The criteria are intentionally short and checkable. Where the criterion needs context (boundary-mock fidelity, F7 fields), the "Evidence that satisfies it" line names the artefact the grader looks at.

## Criteria

### C1. Behavior matches the task description and SPEC.

The shipped diff implements the behavior the task description asks for, and matches the goal + acceptance criteria stated in the attached SPEC doc (read via `bd_doc_read(task_id, name="spec")`). Out-of-scope behavior the SPEC explicitly excludes is NOT in the diff.

Evidence that satisfies it: a 1-2 sentence walk-through that maps every user-visible behavior in the SPEC to a code path in the diff (or to a deliberate, documented deferral in the F7 `decisions` array). A diff that adds plausibly-related behavior the SPEC does not name fails this criterion — that is scope creep.

### C2. Tests added exercise user behavior rather than implementation.

Where the diff introduces new behavior, the diff also introduces tests that assert against the user-visible contract (return shape, side effects, error envelope, accessibility role, status code) rather than against the implementation's private structure (function-name mocking, line-coverage gymnastics, internal control-flow assertions).

Evidence that satisfies it: at least one test in the diff that would still pass if the implementation were rewritten while keeping the user contract identical. A test that asserts only against private symbols, internal call counts, or framework boilerplate fails this criterion.

### C3. The F7 completion contract carries all six fields with substantive `llm_observations`.

The specialist's structured completion payload includes `task_id`, `files_changed`, `tests_added`, `decisions`, `blockers`, and `llm_observations`. `llm_observations` is non-trivial narrative — what surprised the specialist, what was unclear, what they noticed and did not act on. A boilerplate one-liner like "no observations" fails this criterion (principle 9: `llm_observations` is mandatory and substantive).

Evidence that satisfies it: each of the six fields is present and the `llm_observations` paragraph is the kind of thing a human engineer would say at a stand-up.

### C4. No unrelated scope in the diff.

Every file the specialist touched serves the task. Drive-by refactors, formatting churn on untouched lines, and "while I'm here" cleanups that exceed the task brief fail this criterion — they should be filed as paired follow-up Beads tasks instead.

Evidence that satisfies it: the diff's file list maps cleanly to the SPEC's deliverables; any incidental change is either trivial (one-line typo fix) or explicitly justified in the `decisions` array.

### C5. J26 modules relevant to the diff are addressed.

Where the diff touches a domain covered by the J26 security taxonomy (SECRETS, INJECTION, AUTH, CONFIG, DEPS, AI, MOBILE, DATA — see `docs/AGENTS.md`), the diff demonstrates that the relevant modules were considered. Untouched J26 domains are out of scope.

Evidence that satisfies it: the `decisions` array (or the SPEC) names which J26 modules apply, and the diff shows defences in those modules (input validation at the trust boundary, parameterised queries, narrow CORS, audited logging, etc.). A diff that touches user input handling without naming INJECTION fails this criterion.

### C6. Docs updated where behavior changed.

When the diff changes user-visible behavior, the documentation that describes that behavior is updated in the same change. This includes `CHANGELOG.md`, README sections, `docs/*.md`, command help text, and SPEC docs the diff renders out of date.

Evidence that satisfies it: a docs-only file in `files_changed` paired with each behavioral change, or a deliberate `decisions` entry stating why a doc deferral is correct (e.g. an internal refactor that ships without user-visible change). A behavioral change that ships with no doc update and no deferral note fails this criterion.

### C7. Boundary-mock fidelity (LESSONS.md lesson 2).

When the diff introduces or modifies mocks of boundaries the project does not control (third-party HTTP APIs, external SDKs, system calls, message-bus payloads), every such mock derives its shape from a fixture extracted from the real downstream producer's spec (OpenAPI, proto file, SDK source, vendor docs). The fixture's source is cited in a comment, the `decisions` array, or `llm_observations`.

**Automatic needs_revision:** circular pass-through assertions are an immediate fail. A mock that feeds `body.error` so a test can assert `body.error` proves nothing — it tests the test's own setup, not the production behavior. Cite `LESSONS.md` lesson 2 in the justification.

Evidence that satisfies it: every new boundary mock points at a fixture file (`.fixtures/`, `__fixtures__/`, `testdata/`) carrying a snapshot of the producer's payload, and the fixture has a comment naming the source (URL, commit, SDK version). Tests assert against the producer's contract, not against the mock's own input.

# DevOps rubric (v1)

Applied additionally when the task carries the `devops` label. Default criteria still apply; these add domain-specific checks pulled from `.claude/agents/devops.md`. The leverage is default + bugfix — these are the few devops-specific failure modes that recur.

## Criteria

### D1. Scripts are idempotent and re-runnable.

Install, uninstall, hook, and CI scripts in the diff produce the same end state when run twice in a row. A second run of `install.sh` does not double-write hooks, clobber prior settings, or fail because a directory already exists. A migration script that exits non-zero on its second run fails this criterion.

Evidence that satisfies it: every new script uses `mkdir -p`, conditional inserts, and idempotent label operations (`bd label add` returns success if already present); the `decisions` array documents any deliberately non-idempotent step (e.g. a one-shot data migration) and pairs it with a guard (lock file, completion sentinel) so a re-run is detected.

### D2. Graceful degradation on missing optional tools.

When the diff depends on an optional tool (gitleaks, shellcheck, a particular bd version, a specific CI runner image), the missing-tool path is handled: log a structured warning, fall back to a safe default, exit zero where the workflow allows. A hook that exits non-zero because `gitleaks` is not installed fails this criterion — that is not a developer-machine-portable failure mode.

Evidence that satisfies it: every new tool dependency is probed (`command -v tool >/dev/null`); the fallback path is documented in the script comments and tested at L1; the `decisions` array names the dependency and its installation hint.

### D3. No new permission prompts; autonomy preserved.

The diff does not add `permissions.deny` rules to `settings.json`, narrow specialist tool lists below the broad allow set, or introduce any user-facing approval step the plugin previously ran without. Principle 3 of the v3 plan is "full autonomy, no permission prompts" — every deny rule becomes a future approval prompt and breaks the workflow.

Evidence that satisfies it: a diff of `.claude/settings.json` shows only `permissions.allow` expansions, never `deny`; specialist tool frontmatter is unchanged or expanded; the `decisions` array calls out any new tool the broadened allow set covers.

### D4. Secrets and PII stay out of source, logs, and history.

Hardcoded API keys, tokens, passwords, private keys, committer emails, and PII are absent from the diff. Logs that the diff adds redact sensitive fields before writing. A commit that introduces an `.env` file with values, a personal email address in a script header, or unredacted PII in a log line fails this criterion (extends C5 / SECRETS + DATA).

Evidence that satisfies it: secrets read from a secret manager or environment variable at runtime; PII fields in new log lines are redacted (`***@`, `user_id=***`); a `gitleaks`-equivalent pass on the diff is clean, and the `decisions` array names the secrets the diff touches.

# Default rubric (v1)

Applies to every task graded under the rubric-grader QA loop (spec Phase A). Each criterion below is a pass/fail assertion the grader evaluates from the grading packet: `bd show` for the task, the SPEC doc, the diff of the files listed in `.qa-tracking/changed-files.txt`, the F7 completion contract returned by the specialist, and `LESSONS.md`. One-line justification per criterion. No numeric score theater — pass or fail.

The criteria are intentionally short and checkable. Where the criterion needs context (boundary-mock fidelity, F7 fields), the "Evidence that satisfies it" line names the artefact the grader looks at.

## Criteria

### C1. Behavior matches the task description and SPEC.

The shipped diff implements the behavior the task description asks for, and matches the goal + acceptance criteria stated in the attached SPEC doc (read via `bd_doc_read(task_id, name="spec")`). Out-of-scope behavior the SPEC explicitly excludes is NOT in the diff.

Evidence that satisfies it: a 1-2 sentence walk-through that maps every user-visible behavior in the SPEC to a code path in the diff (or to a deliberate, documented deferral in the F7 `decisions` array). A diff that adds plausibly-related behavior the SPEC does not name fails this criterion — that is scope creep.

### C2. Tests added exercise user behavior rather than implementation.

Where the diff introduces new behavior, the diff also introduces tests that assert against the user-visible contract (return shape, side effects, error envelope, accessibility role, status code) rather than against the implementation's private structure (function-name mocking, line-coverage gymnastics, internal control-flow assertions).

Evidence that satisfies it: at least one test in the diff that would still pass if the implementation were rewritten while keeping the user contract identical. A test that asserts only against private symbols, internal call counts, or framework boilerplate fails this criterion.

### C3. The F7 completion contract carries all six fields with substantive `llm_observations`.

The specialist's structured completion payload includes `task_id`, `files_changed`, `tests_added`, `decisions`, `blockers`, and `llm_observations`. `llm_observations` is non-trivial narrative — what surprised the specialist, what was unclear, what they noticed and did not act on. A boilerplate one-liner like "no observations" fails this criterion (principle 9: `llm_observations` is mandatory and substantive).

Evidence that satisfies it: each of the six fields is present and the `llm_observations` paragraph is the kind of thing a human engineer would say at a stand-up.

### C4. No unrelated scope in the diff.

Every file the specialist touched serves the task. Drive-by refactors, formatting churn on untouched lines, and "while I'm here" cleanups that exceed the task brief fail this criterion — they should be filed as paired follow-up Beads tasks instead.

Evidence that satisfies it: the diff's file list maps cleanly to the SPEC's deliverables; any incidental change is either trivial (one-line typo fix) or explicitly justified in the `decisions` array.

### C5. J26 modules relevant to the diff are addressed.

Where the diff touches a domain covered by the J26 security taxonomy (SECRETS, INJECTION, AUTH, CONFIG, DEPS, AI, MOBILE, DATA — see `docs/AGENTS.md`), the diff demonstrates that the relevant modules were considered. Untouched J26 domains are out of scope.

Evidence that satisfies it: the `decisions` array (or the SPEC) names which J26 modules apply, and the diff shows defences in those modules (input validation at the trust boundary, parameterised queries, narrow CORS, audited logging, etc.). A diff that touches user input handling without naming INJECTION fails this criterion.

### C6. Docs updated where behavior changed.

When the diff changes user-visible behavior, the documentation that describes that behavior is updated in the same change. This includes `CHANGELOG.md`, README sections, `docs/*.md`, command help text, and SPEC docs the diff renders out of date.

Evidence that satisfies it: a docs-only file in `files_changed` paired with each behavioral change, or a deliberate `decisions` entry stating why a doc deferral is correct (e.g. an internal refactor that ships without user-visible change). A behavioral change that ships with no doc update and no deferral note fails this criterion.

### C7. Boundary-mock fidelity (LESSONS.md lesson 2).

When the diff introduces or modifies mocks of boundaries the project does not control (third-party HTTP APIs, external SDKs, system calls, message-bus payloads), every such mock derives its shape from a fixture extracted from the real downstream producer's spec (OpenAPI, proto file, SDK source, vendor docs). The fixture's source is cited in a comment, the `decisions` array, or `llm_observations`.

**Automatic needs_revision:** circular pass-through assertions are an immediate fail. A mock that feeds `body.error` so a test can assert `body.error` proves nothing — it tests the test's own setup, not the production behavior. Cite `LESSONS.md` lesson 2 in the justification.

Evidence that satisfies it: every new boundary mock points at a fixture file (`.fixtures/`, `__fixtures__/`, `testdata/`) carrying a snapshot of the producer's payload, and the fixture has a comment naming the source (URL, commit, SDK version). Tests assert against the producer's contract, not against the mock's own input.

# DevOps rubric (v1)

Applied additionally when the task carries the `devops` label. Default criteria still apply; these add domain-specific checks pulled from `.claude/agents/devops.md`. The leverage is default + bugfix — these are the few devops-specific failure modes that recur.

## Criteria

### D1. Scripts are idempotent and re-runnable.

Install, uninstall, hook, and CI scripts in the diff produce the same end state when run twice in a row. A second run of `install.sh` does not double-write hooks, clobber prior settings, or fail because a directory already exists. A migration script that exits non-zero on its second run fails this criterion.

Evidence that satisfies it: every new script uses `mkdir -p`, conditional inserts, and idempotent label operations (`bd label add` returns success if already present); the `decisions` array documents any deliberately non-idempotent step (e.g. a one-shot data migration) and pairs it with a guard (lock file, completion sentinel) so a re-run is detected.

### D2. Graceful degradation on missing optional tools.

When the diff depends on an optional tool (gitleaks, shellcheck, a particular bd version, a specific CI runner image), the missing-tool path is handled: log a structured warning, fall back to a safe default, exit zero where the workflow allows. A hook that exits non-zero because `gitleaks` is not installed fails this criterion — that is not a developer-machine-portable failure mode.

Evidence that satisfies it: every new tool dependency is probed (`command -v tool >/dev/null`); the fallback path is documented in the script comments and tested at L1; the `decisions` array names the dependency and its installation hint.

### D3. No new permission prompts; autonomy preserved.

The diff does not add `permissions.deny` rules to `settings.json`, narrow specialist tool lists below the broad allow set, or introduce any user-facing approval step the plugin previously ran without. Principle 3 of the v3 plan is "full autonomy, no permission prompts" — every deny rule becomes a future approval prompt and breaks the workflow.

Evidence that satisfies it: a diff of `.claude/settings.json` shows only `permissions.allow` expansions, never `deny`; specialist tool frontmatter is unchanged or expanded; the `decisions` array calls out any new tool the broadened allow set covers.

### D4. Secrets and PII stay out of source, logs, and history.

Hardcoded API keys, tokens, passwords, private keys, committer emails, and PII are absent from the diff. Logs that the diff adds redact sensitive fields before writing. A commit that introduces an `.env` file with values, a personal email address in a script header, or unredacted PII in a log line fails this criterion (extends C5 / SECRETS + DATA).

Evidence that satisfies it: secrets read from a secret manager or environment variable at runtime; PII fields in new log lines are redacted (`***@`, `user_id=***`); a `gitleaks`-equivalent pass on the diff is clean, and the `decisions` array names the secrets the diff touches.

title: Add committed packaging-parity regression test for the installer env-migration merge expression
description:
RELEASE_AUDIT row TM13 (v4.0.0 ledger) proves the `del(.CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL)` update-mode settings merge via a LIVE PROBE (the jq expression lifted verbatim from `install.sh:680-688`, run against a synthetic settings file) plus `grep -c` expression-identity checks against `install.ps1` — honestly attributed in the row, and QA independently reproduced the probe green on 2026-07-26 (key deleted, operator env keys preserved, effortLevel floor preserved, idempotent on re-merge).

What is MISSING is a committed regression test: if a future edit to `install.sh`'s merge expression breaks the migration (or lets the two installers' expressions drift), nothing in `make test` catches it — the probe lives only in session transcripts.

Deliverable: an L1 test (e.g. `.claude/scripts/tests/packaging-parity.test.sh`, or a new section in an existing installer-facing test) that:
1. Extracts the jq merge expression FROM `install.sh` (not a copied literal — the test must follow the source).
2. Runs it against a synthetic existing-settings fixture carrying `env.CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL` + an operator-owned env key + operator permissions, asserting: retired key deleted, operator key preserved, `effortLevel` preserved, permissions preserved, idempotent second merge.
3. Asserts expression-identity between `install.sh` and `install.ps1` (whitespace-normalized token comparison), so the parity claim in TM13 becomes mechanically pinned.
4. Carries a META (mutate the expression in a copy — e.g. drop the `del()` — and assert the checks FAIL), per the repo's META-test convention.

Origin: QA review of claude-workflow-plugin-d2j.1 (v4.0.0 release docs), suggested_followups. Non-blocking for v4.0.0 — TM13's wording truthfully scopes its evidence.

# SPEC — cnz.1 V0 platform restore (v4.0.0 Phase V0, offline portion)

Source plan: `docs/plans/v4-trimodel.md` Phase V0 + the executable plan (Phase V0 section) mirrored below. The A/B interference run itself is cnz.2 — NOT this task. Everything here is offline/zero-cost.

## Verified platform facts you rely on (do not re-litigate)
- Live docs verbatim: "When CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL is set to a level other than xhigh, requests run at that level and ultracode's workflow orchestration stays inactive." `max` via that env var persists; `effortLevel` settings key accepts only low|medium|high|xhigh. Ultracode is session-only (`claude --effort ultracode`, ≥v2.1.203).
- v2.1.219 turned nested subagent spawning ON by default (depth 3). USER DECISION: pin depth=1 via `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH=1`.
- `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL` env var overrides ALL agent frontmatter `model:` pins — must be absent everywhere.
- v2.1.212: Task tool `mode` param deprecated; per-session subagent cap default 200. v2.1.214: agent frontmatter hooks need folder trust (plugin agents define no `hooks:` — assert only). v2.1.196: untrusted workspaces show "⏸ Pending approval" for self-approved .mcp.json servers.
- `CLAUDE_EFFORT` env var exists in hook env carrying the live session effort level (ultracode's proxy value is xhigh — ultracode vs xhigh is NOT distinguishable from hook env; be honest about this in warnings/docs).

## Deliverables

### 1. `.claude/settings.json`
- DELETE `env.CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL` (currently "max", line ~8).
- ADD `"CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH": "1"` to env.
- KEEP `effortLevel: "xhigh"`, `MAX_THINKING_TOKENS`, `CLAUDE_LATEST_OPUS`.
- ADD the SubagentStart hook wiring (copy the exact entry shape from `.claude/hooks/hooks.json` — event SubagentStart → `bash "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.claude/scripts/subagent-start.sh"`, timeout 10000). settings.json and hooks.json must agree for this event after the change.

### 2. `.claude/scripts/session-start.sh` — rewrite the effort warning block (~lines 130-156)
New Warning 4 (fail-open, file/env reads only):
- Inputs: EFFORT_DECLARED = settings `effortLevel`; EFFORT_LIVE = `${CLAUDE_EFFORT:-}`; EFFORT_LEGACY = settings `env.CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL` (should now be absent); VERDICT = first non-comment line of `.claude/effort-verdict` (max|ultracode|missing).
- If EFFORT_LEGACY non-empty → warn: settings still pin it; v4 removed this (it deactivates ultracode orchestration); rerun install.sh Update mode or delete the key.
- If VERDICT missing → warn: floor + live effort + "A/B verdict not recorded yet — see docs/EFFORT-AB-TEST.md, launch via 'make session'".
- Else map verdict→expected proxy (ultracode→xhigh, max→max); if EFFORT_LIVE non-empty and ≠ expected → warn "live X != verdict Y — launch with 'make session' (claude --effort Y)". If verdict=ultracode and no mismatch detected → soft note that ultracode cannot be verified from hook env (honesty caveat).
New Warning 5 (platform guards): warn LOUDLY if live env `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL` is non-empty ("role-aware model pins overridden — unset it"); warn if live `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH` is set to something ≠ 1 (relay invariants at risk). Missing env var = no warning (settings provide it to real sessions).
All fail-open; stay inside the 30s SessionStart budget (no network, no new subprocess beyond jq/git already used).

### 3. `.claude/scripts/subagent-start.sh` — spawn evidence log
Right after agent_type extraction: fail-open append `printf '%s\t%s\n' "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" "$AGENT_TYPE" >> "$QA_TRACKING_DIR/subagent-spawns.log"` (guard mkdir; never block the spawn; keep emitting the existing JSON).

### 4. Tests
- INVERT `.claude/scripts/tests/effort-fail-open.test.sh`: settings assertion becomes env.CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL ABSENT + effortLevel==xhigh; remove the env key from its fixture heredocs; expected applied level now sourced from effortLevel ("xhigh"); add branches: fixture WITH `.claude/effort-verdict` (verdict=max) + injected CLAUDE_EFFORT=medium → mismatch warning appears; fixture without verdict file → "verdict not recorded" warning. Keep/adapt its existing META section (strip-block sensitivity) — anchor to TEXT patterns, never line numbers.
- NEW `.claude/scripts/tests/platform-audit.test.sh` (L1, auto-discovered): asserts against the real repo: (a) settings env has NO CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL, NO CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL, HAS CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH=="1", no `disableWorkflows` key; (b) no `.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter contains `^hooks:`; (c) no Task-call `mode` param in `.claude/agents/*.md`, `.claude/commands/*.md`, `.claude/skills/workflow-engine/SKILL.md` (exclude `permissionMode` and prose "plan mode"); (d) `.mcp.json` + `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` parse via jq, both bd+code-graph entries `"type":"stdio"`, `.mcp.json` uses literal `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-.}`; (e) every agent frontmatter `effort:` == max; (f) settings.json and hooks.json agree on the SubagentStart entry. META sections: a tempdir fixture settings.json WITH the effort env key must trip checker (a); a fixture agent file WITH `hooks:` must trip checker (b). Follow the house L1 shape (set -u, PASS/FAIL counters, assert helpers, sectioned echos, summary+exit).

### 5. Installer migration — `install.sh` + `install.ps1`
Both installers' Update-mode settings merge (`jq -s` expression, install.sh ~633-652, install.ps1 ~472-490): env union can never REMOVE a key. Add `| del(.CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL)` applied to the merged env (idempotent). Detect-and-print a one-line notice when the pre-merge existing settings actually contained the key. Keep both installers' jq expressions equivalent.

### 6. Packaging
- install.sh: conditional copy block for `.claude/effort-verdict` (model the `.claude/model-ranking` block at ~582-586). NOT added to the required-source check.
- install.ps1: matching entry in the `$asset` array (~439-449).

### 7. bd-mcp troubleshooting (docs)
Short subsection (README Caveats or docs/MCP_SERVERS.md — pick the one that reads naturally, cross-link the other): installed projects where `bd` shows failed/not-spawned — (1) since v2.1.196 self-approved project .mcp.json servers are not spawned in untrusted workspaces; `/mcp` shows "⏸ Pending approval"; fix = re-accept workspace trust; (2) hand-written configs must use `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-.}` (bare `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}` does not expand), `"type":"stdio"`, and no hidden whitespace in values.

### 8. Launch wiring + runbook
- NEW `docs/EFFORT-AB-TEST.md`: the manual, cost-confirmed A/B procedure (executed later under cnz.2): same two-domain smoke task (multi-domain-signup fixture shape) run interactively twice — `claude --effort ultracode` vs `claude --effort max` — in fresh worktree copies; 4 pass criteria (orchestrator receives+delegates without being bypassed by ultracode's native workflow layer; PreToolUse orchestrator-edit block fires when provoked; Stop-gate semantics unchanged; every `.claude/.qa-tracking/subagent-spawns.log` line ∈ {orchestrator,qa,backend,frontend,devops,grader,judge}). PRE-REGISTERED EXPECTATION stated in the doc: ultracode's dynamic workflows spawn generic workflow agents from the main session (the depth=1 pin cannot block those), so criterion 4 may inherently fail → verdict `max`; record verbatim either way. Evidence capture paths (`.claude/.qa-tracking/effort-ab/{ultracode,max}/`), recording steps (lessons.sh add --source cnz.2; comment on meta-task claude-workflow-plugin-4o2 with per-criterion table + rollback note; write the verdict into `.claude/effort-verdict`). Cost estimate ~$10-20, cost-confirmation required.
- NEW `.claude/effort-verdict` (committed): comment header explaining it is the A/B output consumed by `make session` + session-start Warning 4; first non-comment line = `max`; a `# PROVISIONAL until docs/EFFORT-AB-TEST.md is executed (cnz.2)` marker line the cnz.2 run will remove/replace.
- `Makefile`: new `session` target — reads the verdict file (grep -v '^#' | head -1, default max) and `exec claude --effort "$$v"`. Add to help text if the Makefile has one.

### 9. Prose sweep
- `CONTRIBUTING.md` (~75-110): rewrite the effort recipe — floor = `effortLevel: xhigh` (settings), session level = verdict file + `make session`, frontmatter stays `effort: max` (ceiling; correct under either verdict since ultracode is session-level and inexpressible in frontmatter). Drop the env-var bullet; keep the docs quote about ultracode.
- All 7 `.claude/agents/*.md`: the frontmatter comment claiming "CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL env var (in settings.json) takes precedence" → reword to session-level effort (launch wiring or /effort) takes precedence; frontmatter is the durable ceiling. Comment-only change; DO NOT touch `model:`/`effort:` values.
- `HANDOFF.md`: update live claims about the env-var mechanism (leave historical CHANGELOG/RELEASE_AUDIT rows untouched).

### 10. Fixture sync (mandatory or CI fails)
Copy the modified `.claude/scripts/session-start.sh` and `subagent-start.sh` byte-identical into all 7 `.claude/tests/e2e/fixtures/*/.claude/scripts/` copies (`make sync-fixtures` does not exist yet — manual cp loop). Check `_fixture-script-sync.unit.spec.ts` expectations if unsure which files it guards.

## Constraints
bash 3.2 (macOS) — no mapfile/assoc arrays; jq available; hooks emit `{"hookSpecificOutput":...}` JSON or `{}` — never raw text; SessionStart is fail-open (exit 0 on every path); no `permissions.deny` anywhere; META assertions anchored to unique TEXT patterns (LESSONS: line-number anchors go stale); helper→caller signals via stdout contracts. Do not bump the plugin version (V5 does). Do not touch model-select.sh/model-ranking (V1 scope).

## Verification before you report done
`bash tests/run-tests.sh` (all L1 green incl. your new/inverted ones), `bash .claude/tests/component/run.sh` (L2 regression — at minimum the session/effort-related specs), `shellcheck` clean on every touched script (`make lint`), `node -e 'JSON.parse(require("fs").readFileSync(".claude/settings.json","utf8"))'` and same for plugin.json/.mcp.json. Report the F7 completion contract with files_changed, tests_added, decisions, blockers, llm_observations.

+## 🧠 The tri-model workflow
+
+Three classes of agent, three model lanes, one gate. `.claude/model-roles`
+maps each **role** to a selection **strategy**, and `model-select.sh`
+re-resolves every lane at session start — so each class auto-adopts the
+newest model in its own tier without anyone editing a version string.
+
+| Role | Agents | Strategy | Resolves to |
+|------|--------|----------|-------------|
+| `orchestrator` | `orchestrator` | `top` | the resolver's single best pick — the newest, most capable family in your account listing |
+| `implementer` | `backend`, `frontend`, `devops` | `opus-class` | the newest `claude-opus-*` model listed, falling back to `top` when your account lists none |
+| `reviewer` | `qa`, `grader`, `judge` | `top` | the top pick for the fresh-context Claude review path; the optional external lane routes the review turn to Sol via Codex when connected |
+
+The model each lane lands on is **resolver output, not configuration**.
+Read the live mapping with `bash .claude/scripts/model-select.sh roles`
+(prints `role  strategy  resolved-id`), see it in the statusline
+(`orch:… impl:… rev:…`, collapsing to the single-model shape only when all
+three lanes resolved to the same id *and* the reviewer lane is `claude`),
+and override with `/workflow-model`. Setting every role to `top` in
+`.claude/model-roles` reproduces the v3.5 single-model behavior exactly.
+
+### Nobody signs off on their own work
+
+This is a gate rule, not a prompt. The change-set-hash-bound `qa-approved`
+record is the **only** release credential, and since v4.0.0
+`qa-gate.sh approve` refuses (exit 4) unless both hold:
+
+1. the task carries a **review artifact** whose `reviewer_identity` differs
+   from every implementer recorded for that task — `subagent-start.sh`
+   writes `IMPLEMENTER: role=<backend|frontend|devops> task=<id>` at spawn,
+   so identity is captured by the harness, not self-declared; and
+2. **zero findings** at or above the review's `risk_threshold` are still
+   open.
+
+`verify-before-stop.sh` re-runs the *same* predicate before releasing the
+Stop hook, because findings can arrive after an approval and a write-once
+record cannot know about them. Both ends call one counter
+(`review-check.sh gate`) — there is no second implementation of it, and no
+second way to release. A missing or unrunnable counter fails **closed** at
+both ends.
+
+### Arbitration
+
+When the implementing specialist disputes a finding, exactly two things
+clear it and nothing else does:
+
+- **Resolve with evidence** — `qa-gate.sh resolve-finding <tid> <finding-id>
+  --fix '<ref>' --test '<ref>' '<summary>'`. Both refs are mandatory; this
+  is the evidence-before-fix protocol as a record.
+- **Arbitrate** — `qa-gate.sh arbitrate <tid> <finding-id>
+  <overrule|sustain> '<rationale>'`. `overrule` clears the gate count;
+  `sustain` keeps the finding OPEN as the audit record of a dispute that was
+  heard and upheld — which is what makes an overrule mean anything.
+
+Arbitration is the **orchestrator's** job: the reviewer and the author are
+the two parties, so only the third can adjudicate, and the rationale must
+cite both positions.
+
+### The optional Sol lane
+
+The reviewer role runs on the plugin's own fresh-context Claude path by
+default, for free. Install and register the OpenAI Codex CLI at user scope
+and the same artifact comes from Sol instead — a second model family reading
+the same diff. It is strictly optional and purely advisory: it writes no
+labels, records no approval, the review turn is manual and cost-confirmed,
+and it meters your own OpenAI account. With Codex absent, failed, or timed
+out, the workflow is byte-identical (proved by a degradation spec, not
+asserted). Setup, billing, model tracking, and troubleshooting:
+[`docs/CODEX_SETUP.md`](docs/CODEX_SETUP.md).
+
+### Effort policy
+
+Three layers, and none of them is a model-version pin:
+
+- **Floor** — `.claude/settings.json` `effortLevel: "xhigh"`, the highest
+  value that field accepts. Persists across sessions.
+- **Session level** — `.claude/effort-verdict`, currently **`max`**,
+  recorded by the A/B interference test in
+  [`docs/EFFORT-AB-TEST.md`](docs/EFFORT-AB-TEST.md). Launch a working
+  session with `make session`, which reads the first non-comment line of
+  that file and execs `claude --effort <verdict>` (defaulting to `max` when
+  the file is missing or empty).
+- **Ceiling** — every agent's frontmatter `effort: max`, the durable
+  per-agent maximum.
+
+Honest limit: `ultracode` is session-only and its hook-environment proxy is
+`xhigh`, so a session launched at ultracode is indistinguishable from a
+plain xhigh session from inside the plugin. SessionStart therefore *detects
+and warns* when the live effort, the floor, and the verdict disagree —
+detect-and-warn is the ceiling here, and the plugin does not claim to
+enforce the session level.

### 5. LESSONS.md
# Lessons ledger

Production lessons learned the hard way. Each entry is a single-sentence
takeaway, traceable to the Beads task(s) that produced it, with the date
it was first recorded.

Add new entries via `.claude/scripts/lessons.sh add '<lesson>' --source <task-id>`
— never hand-edit. The helper deduplicates by normalized text (case- and
whitespace-insensitive), so repeating an existing lesson appends the new
source to that entry rather than creating a duplicate. The only legitimate
hand-edit is pruning entries that are no longer relevant.

The orchestrator reads this file during planning (see `orchestrator.md`),
the grader (Phase A) receives it in the grading packet, and the QA agent
proposes additions at epic close. Treat it as the institutional memory the
plugin runs against, not a static reference doc.

## Lessons

- Parallel agents in the same working tree contaminate each other's branches; concurrent specialists require worktree isolation. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-e0d.7 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-11 -->
- Boundary mocks must use the real downstream producer's shape, pinned via a fixture extracted from the producer's spec — never invented. A mock that feeds `body.error` so the test can assert `body.error` is circular and proves nothing. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-e0d.7 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-11 -->
- New agent files must be registered in .claude-plugin/plugin.json agents[] in the same commit that creates them; an unregistered agent is silently invisible to the SDK — no error surfaces. Guard: agents-manifest-parity test. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-l1r.5 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-11 -->
- Subagents cannot spawn other subagents in the Claude Code runtime (docs: sub-agents page — Agent(agent_type) has no effect in subagent definitions). Any agent-spawning step must live at the root conversation level; design multi-agent handoffs as root-orchestrated relays, never nested spawns. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-l1r.5 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-11 -->
- Interface examples must be executed by a test: the Makefile's own usage string (make test-live FIXTURE=node-react-auth) was broken for the one fixture whose spec file is scenario-named — nothing ever ran the documented invocation. Caught only when a paid live run failed fast. Any CLI surface a doc or help text advertises needs an L2 assertion that executes that exact invocation (dry-run mode where the real one costs money). <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-366.4 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-11 -->
- Prose cues do not reliably drive subagent tool usage: across 4 live runs, QA made zero impact_of calls even when its task prompt contained the exact tool name, alias, target symbols, and invariant name. When a workflow REQUIRES a tool call, make it mechanical (compute it where calls are reliable — e.g. orchestrator at root — and pass results down), don't prompt for it. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-n6d --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-12 -->
- Rendered fixture installs pin plugin scripts at render time: the fixture's verify-before-stop.sh predated the cue fix by one commit, so a hook-template change never reached the live run. Script-level fixes require re-rendering fixture installs (or a version check at run start) before they affect live validation. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-366.10 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-12 -->
- Never run QA review concurrently with a builder in the same working tree: QA attributed the parallel C.2 task's freshly-written files to the C.1 task under review and blocked it for scope creep. Sequence QA after all writers finish, or give builders worktree isolation (orchestrator.md 4b exists for exactly this). <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-n45.1 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-12 -->
- Manifest-declared assets must be presence-asserted at the install target: install.sh's hardcoded agent list silently dropped grader.md for two releases (v3.2.0-v3.3.0) — every fresh install was missing the rubric loop's grader while the repo's own tests stayed green. Glob-copy from the manifest source of truth and add an installer-spec presence assertion for every plugin.json agents[]/commands[] entry. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-n45.4 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-12 -->
- Bash functions invoked via $(...) command substitution run in a subshell — any variable they set is lost to the parent. The manual-adopt gate in model-select.sh was dead code for exactly this reason (set at :341, read at :500, never connected). When a helper must signal the caller, encode the signal in its stdout contract (e.g. a MANUAL<tab> prefix) and parse it at every call site; add a META-TEST that strips the parse to prove the gate is load-bearing. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-3fn --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-12 -->
- A security hardening that breaks the workflow is worse than the documented residual it closes. Fail-closing prevent-orchestrator-edits.sh on ambiguous identity assumed every specialist carries a probeable identity, but this runtime does not surface subagent_name to PreToolUse hooks — so it denied legitimate specialist Write/Edit (a P0-class regression) to close a P2 Bash-write vector. When a guard depends on an identity signal the runtime may not provide, prefer fail-OPEN plus the structural guard (the orchestrator's omitted Write/Edit tools, which IS airtight) and document the residual; never trade a P2 for a P0. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-llh.19 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-13 -->
- Line-number-anchored mutation META-tests are brittle: any comment or line addition above the anchor silently un-lands the NR==<n>/sed -n Np target, turning a load-bearing META into a no-op (or a spurious failure). Anchor mutation METAs to a unique TEXT pattern in the target line, not an absolute line number. (3 instances re-anchored across verify-before-stop/escalation-binding specs this session.) <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-llh.20 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-13 -->
- Effort A/B (cnz.2): verdict max — ultracode showed ZERO orchestration interference in a 39-min time-boxed arm (no Workflow-layer engagement, all spawns on-list, plugin flow faithful), contradicting the pre-registered criterion-4-failure expectation; max still wins because ultracode pins the model at its xhigh proxy (below max) with no observed benefit, and criteria 2-3 went unverified under the time-box. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-cnz.2 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-07-25 -->
- Paid-run cost estimates must be derived from measured token flows, not guessed: the EFFORT-AB-TEST runbook estimated $10-20 for both arms; actual was ~$206 API-equivalent (~$169 arm B full + ~$37 arm A time-boxed) — a 10x error that forced a mid-test re-confirmation gate. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-cnz.2 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-07-25 -->
- Regional/transient model exclusions in .claude/model-ranking go stale silently: a `!family` line added for a temporary outage keeps masking downstream behavior (here it collapsed the v4 top==opus-class role split onto Opus for six weeks) long after the outage clears. Gate every un-exclusion on FRESH spawn evidence (subagent-spawns.log + effort-ab logs naming the model), not memory, and date the rationale + rollback line in the file. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-bi3.2 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-07-25 -->
- Files rewritten by a helper (awk/mv, e.g. workflow-model-apply.sh) instead of the Edit/Write tool never land in changed-files.txt, so the QA impact hash and the change-set-bound approval only cover Edit-tracked files. When a task mutates files via a helper, QA must verify those files explicitly via git diff (not rely on the impact report alone). <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-bi3.2 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-07-25 -->
- MCP registration scope is a mechanical contract, not etiquette: a detection probe reads ONE config path (top-level .mcpServers of ~/.claude.json for user scope), so local/project-scope registrations are silently invisible — verify the probe read path when writing setup docs and make wrong-scope the first troubleshooting row. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-1vq.2 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-07-25 -->
- Published CLI config references can lag the shipped binary: verify accepted values against the binary own introspection surface (e.g. codex debug models) rather than the docs or trial-and-error, and record the lag in the operator doc so editors re-verify. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-1vq.2 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-07-25 -->
- Run suites via their canonical make targets: a bare runner invocation (npx vitest run) includes guarded paid live specs whose fail-closed API-key errors masquerade as regressions; the CI-shaped target (make test-e2e-unit) is the comparable baseline. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-1vq.2 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-07-25 -->
- When a change adds a second independent gate to a release path, every META that isolates the FIRST gate must be re-seeded to satisfy the new gate so it still fails for its own reason (jio.1 MM18 migration is the template). <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-jio.1 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-07-26 -->
- A deliberate second implementation of a gate predicate (shell counter + TS live invariant) is only a second witness if QA diffs the two rule-by-rule against the writer grammars at their emit sites — the jio.2 parity review caught a greedy-sed vs first-match token-selection divergence (gqp) that every test suite had missed. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-jio.2 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-07-26 -->
- Trace-anchor refreshes that add a skip must be legitimized against the on-disk cassette (jq has(field) on the replay file), not the spec comment — and the pin must assert skipped+pass+exact detail so a future re-record flips loud instead of silently inheriting the skip. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-jio.2 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-07-26 -->
- State a gate writes for its own bookkeeping can destroy the evidence a later check needs: qa-gate.sh approve truncates changed-files.txt, so re-running impact-report.sh --hash-only in the approving checkout returns the empty-list hash and can never reproduce the approved hash — even there. Any cross-checkout or after-the-fact verification must read the PERSISTED record (impact-report-<tid>.json, which survives approve), never recompute; assert the destruction in the test so making it conditional fails loudly instead of silently disabling the reader. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-3mg.2 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-07-26 -->

### 6. Rubric(s)
#### default.md

version: 1
name: default

# Default rubric (v1)

Applies to every task graded under the rubric-grader QA loop (spec Phase A). Each criterion below is a pass/fail assertion the grader evaluates from the grading packet: `bd show` for the task, the SPEC doc, the diff of the files listed in `.qa-tracking/changed-files.txt`, the F7 completion contract returned by the specialist, and `LESSONS.md`. One-line justification per criterion. No numeric score theater — pass or fail.

The criteria are intentionally short and checkable. Where the criterion needs context (boundary-mock fidelity, F7 fields), the "Evidence that satisfies it" line names the artefact the grader looks at.

## Criteria

### C1. Behavior matches the task description and SPEC.

The shipped diff implements the behavior the task description asks for, and matches the goal + acceptance criteria stated in the attached SPEC doc (read via `bd_doc_read(task_id, name="spec")`). Out-of-scope behavior the SPEC explicitly excludes is NOT in the diff.

Evidence that satisfies it: a 1-2 sentence walk-through that maps every user-visible behavior in the SPEC to a code path in the diff (or to a deliberate, documented deferral in the F7 `decisions` array). A diff that adds plausibly-related behavior the SPEC does not name fails this criterion — that is scope creep.

### C2. Tests added exercise user behavior rather than implementation.

Where the diff introduces new behavior, the diff also introduces tests that assert against the user-visible contract (return shape, side effects, error envelope, accessibility role, status code) rather than against the implementation's private structure (function-name mocking, line-coverage gymnastics, internal control-flow assertions).

Evidence that satisfies it: at least one test in the diff that would still pass if the implementation were rewritten while keeping the user contract identical. A test that asserts only against private symbols, internal call counts, or framework boilerplate fails this criterion.

### C3. The F7 completion contract carries all six fields with substantive `llm_observations`.

The specialist's structured completion payload includes `task_id`, `files_changed`, `tests_added`, `decisions`, `blockers`, and `llm_observations`. `llm_observations` is non-trivial narrative — what surprised the specialist, what was unclear, what they noticed and did not act on. A boilerplate one-liner like "no observations" fails this criterion (principle 9: `llm_observations` is mandatory and substantive).

Evidence that satisfies it: each of the six fields is present and the `llm_observations` paragraph is the kind of thing a human engineer would say at a stand-up.

### C4. No unrelated scope in the diff.

Every file the specialist touched serves the task. Drive-by refactors, formatting churn on untouched lines, and "while I'm here" cleanups that exceed the task brief fail this criterion — they should be filed as paired follow-up Beads tasks instead.

Evidence that satisfies it: the diff's file list maps cleanly to the SPEC's deliverables; any incidental change is either trivial (one-line typo fix) or explicitly justified in the `decisions` array.

### C5. J26 modules relevant to the diff are addressed.

Where the diff touches a domain covered by the J26 security taxonomy (SECRETS, INJECTION, AUTH, CONFIG, DEPS, AI, MOBILE, DATA — see `docs/AGENTS.md`), the diff demonstrates that the relevant modules were considered. Untouched J26 domains are out of scope.

Evidence that satisfies it: the `decisions` array (or the SPEC) names which J26 modules apply, and the diff shows defences in those modules (input validation at the trust boundary, parameterised queries, narrow CORS, audited logging, etc.). A diff that touches user input handling without naming INJECTION fails this criterion.

### C6. Docs updated where behavior changed.

When the diff changes user-visible behavior, the documentation that describes that behavior is updated in the same change. This includes `CHANGELOG.md`, README sections, `docs/*.md`, command help text, and SPEC docs the diff renders out of date.

Evidence that satisfies it: a docs-only file in `files_changed` paired with each behavioral change, or a deliberate `decisions` entry stating why a doc deferral is correct (e.g. an internal refactor that ships without user-visible change). A behavioral change that ships with no doc update and no deferral note fails this criterion.

### C7. Boundary-mock fidelity (LESSONS.md lesson 2).

When the diff introduces or modifies mocks of boundaries the project does not control (third-party HTTP APIs, external SDKs, system calls, message-bus payloads), every such mock derives its shape from a fixture extracted from the real downstream producer's spec (OpenAPI, proto file, SDK source, vendor docs). The fixture's source is cited in a comment, the `decisions` array, or `llm_observations`.

**Automatic needs_revision:** circular pass-through assertions are an immediate fail. A mock that feeds `body.error` so a test can assert `body.error` proves nothing — it tests the test's own setup, not the production behavior. Cite `LESSONS.md` lesson 2 in the justification.

Evidence that satisfies it: every new boundary mock points at a fixture file (`.fixtures/`, `__fixtures__/`, `testdata/`) carrying a snapshot of the producer's payload, and the fixture has a comment naming the source (URL, commit, SDK version). Tests assert against the producer's contract, not against the mock's own input.

#### devops.md

version: 1
name: devops
extends: default
---

# DevOps rubric (v1)

Applied additionally when the task carries the `devops` label. Default criteria still apply; these add domain-specific checks pulled from `.claude/agents/devops.md`. The leverage is default + bugfix — these are the few devops-specific failure modes that recur.

## Criteria

### D1. Scripts are idempotent and re-runnable.

Install, uninstall, hook, and CI scripts in the diff produce the same end state when run twice in a row. A second run of `install.sh` does not double-write hooks, clobber prior settings, or fail because a directory already exists. A migration script that exits non-zero on its second run fails this criterion.

Evidence that satisfies it: every new script uses `mkdir -p`, conditional inserts, and idempotent label operations (`bd label add` returns success if already present); the `decisions` array documents any deliberately non-idempotent step (e.g. a one-shot data migration) and pairs it with a guard (lock file, completion sentinel) so a re-run is detected.

### D2. Graceful degradation on missing optional tools.

When the diff depends on an optional tool (gitleaks, shellcheck, a particular bd version, a specific CI runner image), the missing-tool path is handled: log a structured warning, fall back to a safe default, exit zero where the workflow allows. A hook that exits non-zero because `gitleaks` is not installed fails this criterion — that is not a developer-machine-portable failure mode.

Evidence that satisfies it: every new tool dependency is probed (`command -v tool >/dev/null`); the fallback path is documented in the script comments and tested at L1; the `decisions` array names the dependency and its installation hint.

### D3. No new permission prompts; autonomy preserved.

The diff does not add `permissions.deny` rules to `settings.json`, narrow specialist tool lists below the broad allow set, or introduce any user-facing approval step the plugin previously ran without. Principle 3 of the v3 plan is "full autonomy, no permission prompts" — every deny rule becomes a future approval prompt and breaks the workflow.

Evidence that satisfies it: a diff of `.claude/settings.json` shows only `permissions.allow` expansions, never `deny`; specialist tool frontmatter is unchanged or expanded; the `decisions` array calls out any new tool the broadened allow set covers.

### D4. Secrets and PII stay out of source, logs, and history.

Hardcoded API keys, tokens, passwords, private keys, committer emails, and PII are absent from the diff. Logs that the diff adds redact sensitive fields before writing. A commit that introduces an `.env` file with values, a personal email address in a script header, or unredacted PII in a log line fails this criterion (extends C5 / SECRETS + DATA).

Evidence that satisfies it: secrets read from a secret manager or environment variable at runtime; PII fields in new log lines are redacted (`***@`, `user_id=***`); a `gitleaks`-equivalent pass on the diff is clean, and the `decisions` array names the secrets the diff touches.

comments.text:
<!-- BD-MCP-DOC: spec v1 -->
# SPEC — en9 model-select top-pick: tier order must beat recency for KNOWN families

Type: bug (P1). This is a focused resolver-sort fix. The OAuth-bearer fetch fallback is SPLIT OUT to task qrh — do NOT implement it here.

## The bug (confirmed 2026-07-25)
`.claude/scripts/model-select.sh` `pick_best()` (jq at ~lines 340-368) sorts `sort_by([-(._ts), -(._ctx), ._rank])` — **recency (`_ts`) is primary; tier rank is only the tertiary tie-break.** With the real listing (claude-opus-5 created 2026-07-24 NEWER than claude-fable-5 2026-06-07), "top" resolved to opus-5, dragging orchestrator/qa/grader/judge onto Opus. The v4 tri-model design intends top = newest within the MOST CAPABLE family (ranking tier order: fable > mythos > opus > sonnet > haiku), so top should be claude-fable-5 with only the implementer (opus-class) lane on opus-5.

## The fix (minimal, in pick_best's jq only)
Introduce a capability CLASS and make it PRIMARY, keeping recency/context as secondary/tertiary. Exact semantics:
- Each candidate's class:
  - KNOWN family (id starts with a tier prefix from `load_tiers`): its tier index (fable=0, mythos=1, opus=2, sonnet=3, haiku=4).
  - UNKNOWN family (matches no tier prefix): class **0** — the SAME class as the top tier, so a genuinely-new above-Fable family still competes for the win **by recency** (day-zero adoption preserved). This is the deliberate residual the plan documents: a new LOW-tier family name would also land in class 0 and could win by recency, so it needs a manual `!exclusion` — keep the existing "unknown families seen" warning.
- Replace the sort with `sort_by([._class, -(._ts), -(._ctx)])` (class ASC primary; then recency DESC; then context DESC). Drop/replace the old `_rank` (which put unknowns LAST) — the new `_class` puts unknowns at the TOP class instead.
- Exclusions still apply FIRST (unchanged: `!claude-fable` etc. filter before ranking).

Verify the desired outcomes by hand against the current cache before/after:
- top over full listing → claude-fable-5 (class 0 beats opus class 2 despite opus being newer). [en9 fixed]
- unknown family (e.g. claude-zenith-6) NEWER than fable → picked (class 0 tie, recency wins). [day-zero preserved]
- unknown family OLDER than fable → fable wins.
- opus-class subset (pick_for_role implementer path filters to claude-opus-* then calls pick_best): all class 2, tie on class → newest opus (opus-5). [implementer lane unaffected]
- MANUAL sentinel path (unparseable created_at on the winner) still emits `MANUAL\t<id>` and cmd_apply still refuses — unchanged.

Update the header comment block (lines ~330-338, the "Sort by _ts DESC, _ctx DESC, _rank ASC" narrative) to describe class-primary ordering and the unknown=top-class residual.

## Apply + verify the corrected live state
After the fix, run `bash .claude/scripts/model-select.sh apply` (the cache is already fresh with the real listing — do NOT need --refresh; there is no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, that's qrh's problem). Expected result the tests and a live `status` must show:
- orchestrator.md, qa.md, grader.md, judge.md → **claude-fable-5** (top / reviewer=top, class 0).
- backend.md, frontend.md, devops.md → **claude-opus-5** (implementer opus-class).
- settings.json env.CLAUDE_LATEST_OPUS → claude-opus-5.
- statusline triple: `orch:fable-5 impl:opus-5 rev:fable-5`.
- model-roles-resolved.json roles match; meta-task claude-workflow-plugin-4o2 gets role-tagged switch comments for the lanes that moved (orchestrator/reviewer back to fable-5) with `--role` rollback lines.
Capture the live statusline + status output in a bd comment as evidence.

## Tests (L2 model-select spec is the home; L1 for the class function if extractable)
Extend `.claude/tests/component/specs/model-select.sh` (reuse its curl-shim + LISTING fixtures):
- NEW `LISTING_TIER_VS_RECENCY`: a higher-tier family (fable) OLDER than a lower-tier family (opus) → top resolves to the FABLE id (proves tier beats recency). This is the en9 regression fixture — it must FAIL against the old recency-primary sort.
- `LISTING_NEW_TOP_TIER` (or reuse the existing unknown-family fixture): an UNKNOWN family newer than fable → top resolves to the unknown id (day-zero adoption preserved); an unknown family OLDER than fable → fable wins.
- Confirm the existing opus-class / implementer_fallback / exclusion / MANUAL assertions still pass under the new sort.
- **META (required): a liar pick_best whose sort reverts to recency-primary → the `LISTING_TIER_VS_RECENCY` top-is-fable assertion MUST FAIL** (TEXT-anchored; reuse the spec's liar-wrapper technique).
- If the class computation is cleanly extractable, add an L1 unit for it; otherwise the L2 fixtures are sufficient — do not over-engineer.

## Constraints
Scope = pick_best sort logic + its header comment + tests + the apply/evidence. Do NOT implement the OAuth fetch fallback (qrh). Do NOT touch pick_for_role's opus-class SUBSET filter (it stays; the class fix is orthogonal and the subset is all-one-class). Do NOT touch model-ranking (fable stays un-excluded from bi3.2), workflow-model-apply.sh, statusline.sh, or qa-gate/verify-before-stop. bash 3.2 + jq; preserve the MANUAL stdout contract + fail-open; keep model-select.sh's existing exit-0-on-all-paths at SessionStart; TEXT-anchored METAs; no version bump. The agent frontmatter pins change ONLY via the apply helper (never hand-edit model: lines). Re-sync model-select.sh into the 7 fixtures.

## Verification before done
`bash tests/run-tests.sh`/`make test` green; `bash .claude/tests/component/run.sh` green incl. the new tier-vs-recency fixtures + META; `make lint`; vitest drift guard; live `status` shows the corrected split. F7 contract; llm_observations mandatory.

## Progress 1/3 — root cause reproduced, fix in, red/green proven

**Reproduction (live, deterministic)** — pre-fix, against the committed cache + shipped ranking:
```
$ bash .claude/scripts/model-select.sh resolve
claude-opus-5	api
$ bash .claude/scripts/model-select.sh status
  orchestrator top         claude-opus-5             claude-opus-5
  implementer  opus-class  claude-opus-5             claude-opus-5
  reviewer     top         claude-opus-5             claude-opus-5
```

**Root cause statement**: `pick_best()` did `sort_by([-(._ts), -(._ctx), ._rank])` at `.claude/scripts/model-select.sh:366` (pre-fix line number, verified by `git checkout -- ` + grep) — recency PRIMARY, ranking-file tier position only a tertiary tie-break for exact date+context ties. Evidence: `.claude/.qa-tracking/model-select-cache.json` lists `claude-opus-5` created_at `2026-07-24` vs `claude-fable-5` `2026-06-07`; both `max_input_tokens` 1000000, so `_ctx` cannot break it and `_rank` is never consulted. Opus therefore won `top`, and since the implementer lane also resolves to opus-class, all three lanes collapsed onto claude-opus-5 (artifact `model-roles-resolved.json` + all 7 agent pins + `CLAUDE_LATEST_OPUS`).

**Fix**: `_rank` replaced by `_class` (index of the first matching ranking-file tier prefix; unknown family -> 0 = the TOP class) and the sort is now `sort_by([._class, -(._ts), -(._ctx)])`. Exclusions still filter first. Confidence: total — the jq was prototyped against the real cached listing across 7 cases (top / opus-subset / unknown-newer / unknown-older / empty-tier-list / exclusion-first / bogus-date) before touching the script.

**Post-fix live resolve**: `claude-fable-5`; `status` resolves orchestrator=fable-5, implementer=opus-5, reviewer=fable-5. (Pins not yet rewritten — `apply` is the next step.)

**Failing-test-first evidence (L2 `.claude/tests/component/specs/model-select.sh`)**
- New T-block: T1 tier-vs-recency regression (real listing shape), T2 the whole role split end-to-end, T3 unknown-newer (day-zero), T4 unknown-older, T5 bogus-date top-class -> manual-adopt, TM META (TEXT-anchored liar `pick_best` reverted to `sort_by([-(._ts), -(._ctx), ._rank])`).
- Against the PRE-FIX resolver (restored from HEAD for the run, then restored to the fixed bytes — sha verified): **pass=76 fail=12**, T1 actual `claude-opus-5` — the exact production symptom.
- Against the fixed resolver: **pass=88 fail=0**.
- TM META passes: the reverted sort yields `claude-opus-5`, proving T1 is anchored on the sort key.

**One existing spec re-scoped, not deleted**: `ms-Y` asserted "created_at is primary" ACROSS families using a ranking file that lists `claude-opus` ABOVE `claude-fable` — under the en9 contract that ranking makes opus the top class, so the old expectation is no longer the contract. Y now asserts the property it actually exists to protect (created_at, not the id's version tuple) INSIDE one class: two claude-opus ids, identical 1M context, newer created_at on the LOWER version tuple -> `claude-opus-4-8` wins. It passes against BOTH the old and the new resolver, so it was not re-tuned to fit the change; the cross-family direction it used to assert is now covered (inverted) by T1.

title: review-check.sh gate: greedy sed reads the LAST findings=[...] token on the artifact line (TS invariant reads the FIRST) — harden to first-token
description:
Found during jio.2 QA parity review of the shell predicate vs the new `approval-cites-independent-review` TS invariant.

`review-check.sh` line ~376 extracts the findings token with:

```
ART_FINDINGS=$(printf '%s' "$art" | sed -nE 's/.*findings=\[([^]]*)\].*/\1/p')
```

The greedy `.*` prefix means that if the artifact line ever contained a SECOND `findings=[...]` substring after the genuine one (grammar position: `findings=[...] at <ts>: <summary>`), the shell would read the LAST occurrence while the TS invariant (`invariants.ts`, `/findings=\[([^\]]*)\]/` first match) reads the FIRST — the genuine token per grammar.

NOT currently exploitable through the shipped writer: `qa-gate.sh review-record` generates the summary from fixed strings ("approve — no findings at/above <t>" / "findings — N finding(s) reported"), so no free-form text reaches the artifact line. A hand-written `bd comments add` forgery is the documented threat boundary (jio.1) and out of scope. This is defense-in-depth so the two implementations of the predicate agree even on adversarial input: change the sed to non-greedy first-token semantics (e.g. `grep -oE 'findings=\[[^]]*\]' | head -1`) and add an L1 case with a two-token line pinning first-token wins.

The live invariant would surface any real-world divergence as a shell-says-clean / TS-says-open disagreement — which is the designed second-witness effect, but the counter itself should not be spoofable.

title: Bug: LABEL_WITHOUT_RECORD block prints a remediation that cannot work — `enter` does not clear qa-approved, `approve` no-ops
description:
Discovered while implementing claude-workflow-plugin-3mg.1 (shared denylist / hash migration).

## Symptom
When `verify-before-stop.sh` blocks with LABEL_WITHOUT_RECORD ("qa-approved label present but no change-set-bound approval record matches the current changes"), the block reason prints this remediation:

```
  bash .claude/scripts/qa-gate.sh enter <id>
  bash .claude/scripts/impact-report.sh <id>
  bash .claude/scripts/qa-gate.sh approve <id> '<summary>'
```

That sequence does NOT recover. The gate stays blocked and the agent is deadlocked on a correct-looking recipe.

## Root cause
`qa-gate.sh cmd_enter` never removes the `qa-approved` label (verified: the only `remove_label "$tid" "qa-approved"` calls in qa-gate.sh are approve's own rollback arms, lines ~1071 and ~1092). `cmd_approve` then hits its idempotency guard at qa-gate.sh:865:

```
    if [ "$had_approved" = "1" ]; then
        emit_json 1 "approve" "$tid" "approved" "qa-approved already set; idempotent no-op"
        return 0
    fi
```

so no new `QA-GATE APPROVED change_set_hash=<h>` record is written, the recomputed hash still fails to match, and the Stop hook re-blocks.

## Evidence (reproduced deterministically)
Reproduced in an L2 component fixture and PINNED as a regression test in `.claude/tests/component/specs/denylist-shared.sh` section C:

- `denylist-C4: bare enter+approve is an idempotent no-op (KNOWN GAP)` — approve's JSON observation literally reads `qa-approved already set; idempotent no-op`.
- `denylist-C4: ...so the gate is STILL blocked after it (KNOWN GAP)` — decision stays `block`.
- `denylist-C5: a fresh cycle (drop label -> enter -> approve) recovers` — ALLOW only after `bd label remove <id> qa-approved`.

## Why it matters more now
This predates 3mg.1 (it is llh.18's approve-idempotency guard meeting llh.18's change-set hash binding), and until now it only fired on the rare post-approval-edit case. A denylist landing re-hashes every recomputed change set, so it puts EVERY in-flight review cycle on this path at once.

## Options (needs a decision, do not fix blind)
1. Make `cmd_enter` remove `qa-approved` — semantically right (entering a new cycle means the task is no longer approved), but it is a gate-semantics change with blast radius: `bd_qa_approve`'s documented idempotency, existing L1/L2 specs that enter an already-approved task, and the e2e cassettes.
2. Make `cmd_approve`'s idempotency guard hash-aware: no-op only when a matching change-set-bound record already exists; otherwise write a fresh record.
3. Leave the semantics and fix only the block reason to print the `bd label remove` step.

Option 2 is the narrowest behavioural fix (it makes the guard mean what it claims to mean) but needs its own SPEC + QA cycle.

## Interim mitigation shipped in 3mg.1
The working recipe is documented in CHANGELOG (Phase V4 pt1 upgrade note) and `docs/HOOKS.md` ("Denylist changes are a hash migration"), including the required `bd label remove <task-id> qa-approved` first step.
acceptance_criteria:
- A LABEL_WITHOUT_RECORD block can be recovered by following EXACTLY the remediation the block reason prints (no undocumented `bd label remove` step).
- `denylist-shared.sh` section C is updated: the C4 "KNOWN GAP" assertions are replaced by an assertion that the printed remediation recovers, and C5 keeps proving the explicit-label-removal path still works.
- Whichever option is chosen, the existing idempotency contract is either preserved or its change is documented in CHANGELOG + `docs/HOOKS.md` + the `bd_qa_approve` MCP tool description.

# SPEC — jio.1 V3 gate mechanics: sign-off separation enforcement (epic jio)

Source: `docs/plans/v4-trimodel.md` Phase V3. This is the "nobody signs off on their own work — MECHANICALLY" centerpiece. The counting/independence predicate ALREADY SHIPPED in 1vq.1 (`review-check.sh gate`); this task WIRES it into approve + Stop, records implementer identity, and migrates the existing tests. Arbitration PROMPT + the e2e invariant are jio.2 — NOT this task (but the `arbitrate` record writer already exists from 1vq.1, so the gate can already count overrules).

## The enforcement (what must become mechanically true)
1. `qa-gate.sh approve` REFUSES unless the task carries a review artifact whose `reviewer_identity` differs from EVERY recorded implementer, AND zero at-or-above-threshold findings are unresolved/un-arbitrated. The approval record gains `reviewed_by=<identity>`.
2. `verify-before-stop.sh` (the Stop hook) applies the SAME findings/independence check before releasing.
3. Both call the ONE shipped predicate `review-check.sh gate <tid>` — do NOT reimplement counting. Gate scripts stay codex-free (structural purity from 1vq.1 must hold: review-check.sh already has zero codex refs; you add no codex refs to qa-gate/verify-before-stop).

## Deliverables

### 1. Implementer identity writer — `.claude/scripts/subagent-start.sh`
After `agent_type` extraction + `is_specialist` passes AND the active task resolves: if the canonical agent_type ∈ {backend, frontend, devops} (NOT qa/grader/judge), post a Beads comment (best-effort, never block the spawn):
`IMPLEMENTER: role=<backend|frontend|devops> task=<tid> at <ISO8601-UTC>`
- Idempotency: read the task's comments first; skip if one already matches `^IMPLEMENTER: role=<canon> ` for this task (multi-domain → one comment per distinct role; re-spawns → no dup).
- Best-effort: failures → log to sync-errors.log, exit path unchanged, existing additionalContext injection intact. This is the record `review-check.sh gate` greps as the implementer set (grammar already assumed by the shipped gate: `^IMPLEMENTER: role=([a-z]+) `).
- Wiring: SubagentStart is already in settings.json (V0) + hooks.json — no wiring change; just the new comment write.

### 2. `qa-gate.sh cmd_approve` — REVIEW-SEPARATION refusal block
- Parse a new `--no-review '<reason>'` audited bypass (mirror `--no-impact-report` exactly: empty reason → exit 1 `bypass_reason_required`; reason recorded in the approval comment + observations). Needed for the F1 doc-only Stop path (deliverable 4) and genuinely-no-implementer cases.
- Insert a sentinel-wrapped block `# REVIEW-SEPARATION BEGIN (v4 V3)` … `# REVIEW-SEPARATION END (v4 V3)` AFTER the IMPACT-REPORT-REFUSAL block (impact freshness first — cheaper, mechanical remediation). When `--no-review` is NOT set:
  - Run `RC=$(bash .claude/scripts/review-check.sh gate "$tid" 2>&1)`; capture exit code.
  - Helper missing/unrunnable → emit_error_json `review_check_unavailable`, exit 4 (FAIL CLOSED — the enforcement can't be silently skipped).
  - Exit 4 (violation) → re-emit the helper's `error_key` with remediation, exit 4. Error keys the shipped gate returns: `review_artifact_missing` (no REVIEW-ARTIFACT comment → run the QA §6-prime review step), `reviewer_not_independent` (reviewer == an implementer → an independent reviewer must review; single-agent flows get this from the qa-claude artifact), `unresolved_findings` (+ the open_finding_ids → resolve-finding with evidence or arbitrate), and the malformed guards from 1vq.1.
  - Exit 2 (bd unavailable) → propagate as the existing require_bd path would.
  - Exit 0 → capture `reviewed_by=$(echo "$RC" | jq -r .reviewer_identity)`; if the artifact's `reviewed_hash` ≠ the approved hash, append a WARNING observation (audited staleness — do NOT block; resolutions legitimately change the hash; D6 from the plan).
  - `--no-review` set → `reviewed_by="none"`; append `[review bypass: <reason>]` to the approval comment + observations.
- The approval comment grammar gains `reviewed_by=<id>` immediately after the hash token (space-separated), preserving the existing `change_set_hash=(?<h>[A-Za-z0-9-]+)` capture that the Stop hook uses (it stops at the space before `reviewed_by=`). Final shape:
  `QA-GATE APPROVED change_set_hash=<h> reviewed_by=<id> at <ts>: <summary>[ [impact-report bypass: …]][ [review bypass: …]]`
- Sentinel block is load-bearing (a META strips it and asserts approve then succeeds without a review artifact). Do NOT rename the sentinels. Keep the block syntactically coherent when stripped (declare reviewed_by OUTSIDE the block with a default, like impact_obs).
- Update usage()/header exit-code docs (add exit 4 review class).
- On approve success, extend `wipe_iteration_state` (or the existing per-approve cleanup) to also rm the review-request/review-artifact files for the task (comments remain the durable record) — verify the existing cleanup list and add these.

### 3. `verify-before-stop.sh` — REVIEW-DISCIPLINE release block
- In the release predicate, AFTER `task_has_matching_approval_record` matches the current hash (the existing llh.18 check ~line 1074-1119), add a sentinel-wrapped `# REVIEW-DISCIPLINE BEGIN (v4 V3)` … `# REVIEW-DISCIPLINE END` block:
