The F1 auto-approve call in verify-before-stop.sh (~line 703-770, the doc-only/beads-state/empty fast path that calls `qa-gate.sh approve`) must now pass `--no-review "F1 <FASTPATH_CLASS> fast path: no reviewable source changed"` so the doc-only auto-approve doesn't trip the new review-separation refusal (a doc-only change has no implementer and no reviewer). ### 5. Test migration (LOAD-BEARING — the existing suite calls approve)
Every existing L2 spec that calls `qa-gate.sh approve` on a task with a real change set will now REFUSE without a review artifact. Migrate them so the suite stays green AND the new enforcement is proven:

- Audit the specs: rubric-loop.sh, qa-gate.sh spec, bd-compat.sh, any component spec whose flow reaches approve. Fix each; report the list.

### 6. NEW tests
- L1 `review-separation.test.sh` (or extend an existing qa-gate L1): via crafted fixtures/comment sets — approve refuses with each error_key (missing artifact; reviewer==implementer → reviewer_not_independent; open at-threshold finding → unresolved_findings); approve passes after resolve-finding (fix+test) OR arbitrate overrule; `--no-review` audited; the approval comment carries `reviewed_by=` and the old hash-capture still matches. - L2 `verify-review-discipline.sh`: seed label + matching-hash approval record + an open at-threshold finding → Stop BLOCKS citing the finding ids; after `arbitrate overrule` → Stop RELEASES; a `[review bypass:` (F1) record → Stop releases. - L2 subagent-start identity: spawn payload agent_type=backend + active task → IMPLEMENTER comment posted once; re-spawn → no dup; agent_type=qa → NONE; two roles → two records. META: mutate the idempotency grep so dups post → assertion fails.
- Degradation: confirm the reviewer-lane-degradation structural-purity grep STILL passes (you added no codex refs to the gate scripts).

## Bootstrapping note (this repo's own gate)
After this lands, THIS repo's approve refuses without a review artifact. That is intended: qa.md §6-prime (shipped 1vq.2) has QA author a qa-claude artifact + review-record before the packet. When jio.1 itself reaches QA, the QA agent must produce that artifact (implementer here = devops; reviewer = qa-claude; independent → passes). If the QA flow doesn't produce it, approve refuses — the mechanical backstop doing its job. Make sure your L2 fixtures model this real flow.

bash 3.2 + jq; call the shipped `review-check.sh gate` (do NOT reimplement counting); gate scripts stay codex-free (structural purity holds); fail CLOSED on the new checks (helper-missing/violation → refuse/block), matching how impact-report refusal fails; sentinels load-bearing + TEXT-anchored METAs (LESSONS llh.20); the approval-comment hash capture MUST stay backward-compatible (space-terminated tokens); do NOT add arbitration PROMPT guidance (jio.2) or the e2e invariant (jio.2); no version bump; re-sync qa-gate.sh/verify-before-stop.sh/subagent-start.sh into the 7 fixtures.

Full L1 (`make test`) + L2 (`bash .claude/tests/component/run.sh`) green INCLUDING the migrated specs; `make lint`; vitest drift guard; the new METAs proven sensitive (strip → the protected assertion fails). # Lessons ledger

Production lessons learned the hard way. Each entry is a single-sentence
takeaway, traceable to the Beads task(s) that produced it, with the date
it was first recorded.

Add new entries via `.claude/scripts/lessons.sh add '<lesson>' --source <task-id>`
— never hand-edit. The helper deduplicates by normalized text (case- and
whitespace-insensitive), so repeating an existing lesson appends the new
source to that entry rather than creating a duplicate. The only legitimate
hand-edit is pruning entries that are no longer relevant.

The orchestrator reads this file during planning (see `orchestrator.md`),
the grader (Phase A) receives it in the grading packet, and the QA agent
proposes additions at epic close. Treat it as the institutional memory the
plugin runs against, not a static reference doc.

## Lessons

- Parallel agents in the same working tree contaminate each other's branches; concurrent specialists require worktree isolation. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-e0d.7 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-11 -->
- Boundary mocks must use the real downstream producer's shape, pinned via a fixture extracted from the producer's spec — never invented. A mock that feeds `body.error` so the test can assert `body.error` is circular and proves nothing. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-e0d.7 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-11 -->
- New agent files must be registered in .claude-plugin/plugin.json agents[] in the same commit that creates them; an unregistered agent is silently invisible to the SDK — no error surfaces. Guard: agents-manifest-parity test. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-l1r.5 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-11 -->
- Subagents cannot spawn other subagents in the Claude Code runtime (docs: sub-agents page — Agent(agent_type) has no effect in subagent definitions). Any agent-spawning step must live at the root conversation level; design multi-agent handoffs as root-orchestrated relays, never nested spawns. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-l1r.5 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-11 -->
- Interface examples must be executed by a test: the Makefile's own usage string (make test-live FIXTURE=node-react-auth) was broken for the one fixture whose spec file is scenario-named — nothing ever ran the documented invocation. Caught only when a paid live run failed fast. Any CLI surface a doc or help text advertises needs an L2 assertion that executes that exact invocation (dry-run mode where the real one costs money). <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-366.4 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-11 -->
- Prose cues do not reliably drive subagent tool usage: across 4 live runs, QA made zero impact_of calls even when its task prompt contained the exact tool name, alias, target symbols, and invariant name. When a workflow REQUIRES a tool call, make it mechanical (compute it where calls are reliable — e.g. orchestrator at root — and pass results down), don't prompt for it. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-n6d --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-12 -->
- Rendered fixture installs pin plugin scripts at render time: the fixture's verify-before-stop.sh predated the cue fix by one commit, so a hook-template change never reached the live run. Script-level fixes require re-rendering fixture installs (or a version check at run start) before they affect live validation. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-366.10 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-12 -->
- Never run QA review concurrently with a builder in the same working tree: QA attributed the parallel C.2 task's freshly-written files to the C.1 task under review and blocked it for scope creep. Sequence QA after all writers finish, or give builders worktree isolation (orchestrator.md 4b exists for exactly this). <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-n45.1 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-12 -->
- Manifest-declared assets must be presence-asserted at the install target: install.sh's hardcoded agent list silently dropped grader.md for two releases (v3.2.0-v3.3.0) — every fresh install was missing the rubric loop's grader while the repo's own tests stayed green. Glob-copy from the manifest source of truth and add an installer-spec presence assertion for every plugin.json agents[]/commands[] entry. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-n45.4 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-12 -->
- Bash functions invoked via $(...) command substitution run in a subshell — any variable they set is lost to the parent. The manual-adopt gate in model-select.sh was dead code for exactly this reason (set at :341, read at :500, never connected). When a helper must signal the caller, encode the signal in its stdout contract (e.g. a MANUAL<tab> prefix) and parse it at every call site; add a META-TEST that strips the parse to prove the gate is load-bearing. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-3fn --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-12 -->
- A security hardening that breaks the workflow is worse than the documented residual it closes. Fail-closing prevent-orchestrator-edits.sh on ambiguous identity assumed every specialist carries a probeable identity, but this runtime does not surface subagent_name to PreToolUse hooks — so it denied legitimate specialist Write/Edit (a P0-class regression) to close a P2 Bash-write vector. When a guard depends on an identity signal the runtime may not provide, prefer fail-OPEN plus the structural guard (the orchestrator's omitted Write/Edit tools, which IS airtight) and document the residual; never trade a P2 for a P0. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-llh.19 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-13 -->
- Line-number-anchored mutation META-tests are brittle: any comment or line addition above the anchor silently un-lands the NR==<n>/sed -n Np target, turning a load-bearing META into a no-op (or a spurious failure). Anchor mutation METAs to a unique TEXT pattern in the target line, not an absolute line number. (3 instances re-anchored across verify-before-stop/escalation-binding specs this session.) <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-llh.20 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-13 -->
- Effort A/B (cnz.2): verdict max — ultracode showed ZERO orchestration interference in a 39-min time-boxed arm (no Workflow-layer engagement, all spawns on-list, plugin flow faithful), contradicting the pre-registered criterion-4-failure expectation; max still wins because ultracode pins the model at its xhigh proxy (below max) with no observed benefit, and criteria 2-3 went unverified under the time-box. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-cnz.2 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-07-25 -->
- Paid-run cost estimates must be derived from measured token flows, not guessed: the EFFORT-AB-TEST runbook estimated $10-20 for both arms; actual was ~$206 API-equivalent (~$169 arm B full + ~$37 arm A time-boxed) — a 10x error that forced a mid-test re-confirmation gate. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-cnz.2 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-07-25 -->
- Regional/transient model exclusions in .claude/model-ranking go stale silently: a `!family` line added for a temporary outage keeps masking downstream behavior (here it collapsed the v4 top==opus-class role split onto Opus for six weeks) long after the outage clears. Gate every un-exclusion on FRESH spawn evidence (subagent-spawns.log + effort-ab logs naming the model), not memory, and date the rationale + rollback line in the file. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-bi3.2 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-07-25 -->
- Files rewritten by a helper (awk/mv, e.g. workflow-model-apply.sh) instead of the Edit/Write tool never land in changed-files.txt, so the QA impact hash and the change-set-bound approval only cover Edit-tracked files. When a task mutates files via a helper, QA must verify those files explicitly via git diff (not rely on the impact report alone). <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-bi3.2 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-07-25 -->
- MCP registration scope is a mechanical contract, not etiquette: a detection probe reads ONE config path (top-level .mcpServers of ~/.claude.json for user scope), so local/project-scope registrations are silently invisible — verify the probe read path when writing setup docs and make wrong-scope the first troubleshooting row. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-1vq.2 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-07-25 -->
- Published CLI config references can lag the shipped binary: verify accepted values against the binary own introspection surface (e.g. codex debug models) rather than the docs or trial-and-error, and record the lag in the operator doc so editors re-verify. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-1vq.2 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-07-25 -->
- Run suites via their canonical make targets: a bare runner invocation (npx vitest run) includes guarded paid live specs whose fail-closed API-key errors masquerade as regressions; the CI-shaped target (make test-e2e-unit) is the comparable baseline. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-1vq.2 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-07-25 -->

# Default rubric (v1)

Applies to every task graded under the rubric-grader QA loop (spec Phase A). Each criterion below is a pass/fail assertion the grader evaluates from the grading packet: `bd show` for the task, the SPEC doc, the diff of the files listed in `.qa-tracking/changed-files.txt`, the F7 completion contract returned by the specialist, and `LESSONS.md`. One-line justification per criterion. No numeric score theater — pass or fail.

The criteria are intentionally short and checkable. Where the criterion needs context (boundary-mock fidelity, F7 fields), the "Evidence that satisfies it" line names the artefact the grader looks at.

## Criteria

### C1. Behavior matches the task description and SPEC.

The shipped diff implements the behavior the task description asks for, and matches the goal + acceptance criteria stated in the attached SPEC doc (read via `bd_doc_read(task_id, name="spec")`). Out-of-scope behavior the SPEC explicitly excludes is NOT in the diff.

Evidence that satisfies it: a 1-2 sentence walk-through that maps every user-visible behavior in the SPEC to a code path in the diff (or to a deliberate, documented deferral in the F7 `decisions` array). A diff that adds plausibly-related behavior the SPEC does not name fails this criterion — that is scope creep.

### C2. Tests added exercise user behavior rather than implementation.

Where the diff introduces new behavior, the diff also introduces tests that assert against the user-visible contract (return shape, side effects, error envelope, accessibility role, status code) rather than against the implementation's private structure (function-name mocking, line-coverage gymnastics, internal control-flow assertions).

Evidence that satisfies it: at least one test in the diff that would still pass if the implementation were rewritten while keeping the user contract identical. A test that asserts only against private symbols, internal call counts, or framework boilerplate fails this criterion.

### C3. The F7 completion contract carries all six fields with substantive `llm_observations`.

The specialist's structured completion payload includes `task_id`, `files_changed`, `tests_added`, `decisions`, `blockers`, and `llm_observations`. `llm_observations` is non-trivial narrative — what surprised the specialist, what was unclear, what they noticed and did not act on. A boilerplate one-liner like "no observations" fails this criterion (principle 9: `llm_observations` is mandatory and substantive).

Evidence that satisfies it: each of the six fields is present and the `llm_observations` paragraph is the kind of thing a human engineer would say at a stand-up.

### C4. No unrelated scope in the diff.

Every file the specialist touched serves the task. Drive-by refactors, formatting churn on untouched lines, and "while I'm here" cleanups that exceed the task brief fail this criterion — they should be filed as paired follow-up Beads tasks instead.

Evidence that satisfies it: the diff's file list maps cleanly to the SPEC's deliverables; any incidental change is either trivial (one-line typo fix) or explicitly justified in the `decisions` array.

### C5. J26 modules relevant to the diff are addressed.

Where the diff touches a domain covered by the J26 security taxonomy (SECRETS, INJECTION, AUTH, CONFIG, DEPS, AI, MOBILE, DATA — see `docs/AGENTS.md`), the diff demonstrates that the relevant modules were considered. Untouched J26 domains are out of scope.

Evidence that satisfies it: the `decisions` array (or the SPEC) names which J26 modules apply, and the diff shows defences in those modules (input validation at the trust boundary, parameterised queries, narrow CORS, audited logging, etc.). A diff that touches user input handling without naming INJECTION fails this criterion.

### C6. Docs updated where behavior changed.

When the diff changes user-visible behavior, the documentation that describes that behavior is updated in the same change. This includes `CHANGELOG.md`, README sections, `docs/*.md`, command help text, and SPEC docs the diff renders out of date.

Evidence that satisfies it: a docs-only file in `files_changed` paired with each behavioral change, or a deliberate `decisions` entry stating why a doc deferral is correct (e.g. an internal refactor that ships without user-visible change). A behavioral change that ships with no doc update and no deferral note fails this criterion.

### C7. Boundary-mock fidelity (LESSONS.md lesson 2).

When the diff introduces or modifies mocks of boundaries the project does not control (third-party HTTP APIs, external SDKs, system calls, message-bus payloads), every such mock derives its shape from a fixture extracted from the real downstream producer's spec (OpenAPI, proto file, SDK source, vendor docs). The fixture's source is cited in a comment, the `decisions` array, or `llm_observations`.

**Automatic needs_revision:** circular pass-through assertions are an immediate fail. A mock that feeds `body.error` so a test can assert `body.error` proves nothing — it tests the test's own setup, not the production behavior. Cite `LESSONS.md` lesson 2 in the justification.

Evidence that satisfies it: every new boundary mock points at a fixture file (`.fixtures/`, `__fixtures__/`, `testdata/`) carrying a snapshot of the producer's payload, and the fixture has a comment naming the source (URL, commit, SDK version). Tests assert against the producer's contract, not against the mock's own input.

# DevOps rubric (v1)

Applied additionally when the task carries the `devops` label. Default criteria still apply; these add domain-specific checks pulled from `.claude/agents/devops.md`. The leverage is default + bugfix — these are the few devops-specific failure modes that recur.

## Criteria

### D1. Scripts are idempotent and re-runnable.

Install, uninstall, hook, and CI scripts in the diff produce the same end state when run twice in a row. A second run of `install.sh` does not double-write hooks, clobber prior settings, or fail because a directory already exists. A migration script that exits non-zero on its second run fails this criterion.

Evidence that satisfies it: every new script uses `mkdir -p`, conditional inserts, and idempotent label operations (`bd label add` returns success if already present); the `decisions` array documents any deliberately non-idempotent step (e.g. a one-shot data migration) and pairs it with a guard (lock file, completion sentinel) so a re-run is detected.

### D2. Graceful degradation on missing optional tools.

When the diff depends on an optional tool (gitleaks, shellcheck, a particular bd version, a specific CI runner image), the missing-tool path is handled: log a structured warning, fall back to a safe default, exit zero where the workflow allows. A hook that exits non-zero because `gitleaks` is not installed fails this criterion — that is not a developer-machine-portable failure mode.

Evidence that satisfies it: every new tool dependency is probed (`command -v tool >/dev/null`); the fallback path is documented in the script comments and tested at L1; the `decisions` array names the dependency and its installation hint.

### D3. No new permission prompts; autonomy preserved.

The diff does not add `permissions.deny` rules to `settings.json`, narrow specialist tool lists below the broad allow set, or introduce any user-facing approval step the plugin previously ran without. Principle 3 of the v3 plan is "full autonomy, no permission prompts" — every deny rule becomes a future approval prompt and breaks the workflow.

Evidence that satisfies it: a diff of `.claude/settings.json` shows only `permissions.allow` expansions, never `deny`; specialist tool frontmatter is unchanged or expanded; the `decisions` array calls out any new tool the broadened allow set covers.

### D4. Secrets and PII stay out of source, logs, and history.

Hardcoded API keys, tokens, passwords, private keys, committer emails, and PII are absent from the diff. Logs that the diff adds redact sensitive fields before writing. A commit that introduces an `.env` file with values, a personal email address in a script header, or unredacted PII in a log line fails this criterion (extends C5 / SECRETS + DATA).

Evidence that satisfies it: secrets read from a secret manager or environment variable at runtime; PII fields in new log lines are redacted (`***@`, `user_id=***`); a `gitleaks`-equivalent pass on the diff is clean, and the `decisions` array names the secrets the diff touches.

<!-- BD-MCP-DOC: spec v1 -->
# SPEC — jio.2 V3 arbitration prompt + live-harness invariant + acceptance tests (epic jio)

Source: `docs/plans/v4-trimodel.md` Phase V3 (the prompt + invariant half; jio.1 shipped the gate ENFORCEMENT — approve/Stop refusals, IMPLEMENTER writer, review-check counting). The `arbitrate`/`resolve-finding` record writers already exist (1vq.1) and the gate already COUNTS overrules (review-check.sh gate). This task adds: the orchestrator's arbitration GUIDANCE, the live-harness INVARIANT that proves the whole chain, and the acceptance-scenario tests. Enforcement lives in the gate count (shipped), NOT in these prompts.

## Deliverables

### 1. `.claude/agents/orchestrator.md` — new §5d "Arbitration"
Place after §5c (the REVIEW-RELAY section from 1vq.2). Guidance only — the gate count enforces; this tells the orchestrator HOW to arbitrate:
- **Trigger:** an at-or-above-`risk_threshold` finding exists that the implementing specialist DISPUTES (the specialist's F7 `decisions`/`blockers` contests it, or QA/Sol and the specialist disagree). While such a finding is unresolved AND un-arbitrated, `qa-gate.sh approve` refuses `unresolved_findings` and the Stop hook blocks — so the orchestrator must act to unblock.
- **Two legitimate resolutions** (either clears the finding in the gate count):
  1. RESOLVE with evidence — the implementer fixes it and records `qa-gate.sh resolve-finding <tid> <finding-id> --fix '<ref>' --test '<ref>' '<summary>'` (evidence-before-fix: the fix AND the test that proves it; both `--fix` and `--test` mandatory).
  2. ARBITRATE — the orchestrator reads BOTH positions (the finding's evidence in the review artifact + the specialist's rebuttal in its F7), DECIDES, and records `qa-gate.sh arbitrate <tid> <finding-id> <overrule|sustain> '<rationale citing both positions>'`. `overrule` = the finding is not blocking (clears it); `sustain` = the finding stands (keeps it open — an audit record of a considered-and-upheld dispute; the implementer must then resolve it).
- **Arbitration is the ORCHESTRATOR's job, not QA's or the implementer's** — it is the independent third party. State that the rationale must cite both sides (so the audit trail shows a real adjudication, not a rubber stamp).
- **J21 interaction:** update the J21 `choose approve` guidance — `choose approve` now routes through `cmd_approve`, which REFUSES while unresolved at-threshold findings exist. So a J21 "accept and move on" decision does NOT bypass review separation; the orchestrator must arbitrate (overrule) or the implementer must resolve FIRST, then approve. Find the existing J21/`choose` guidance in orchestrator.md and qa.md and correct any wording implying `choose approve` is an unconditional escape.
- Scope: guidance + the exact `arbitrate`/`resolve-finding` command grammars (which already exist). Do NOT change the gate scripts (enforcement shipped in jio.1). Do NOT add new sentinels.

### 2. Live-harness invariant `approval-cites-independent-review` — `.claude/tests/e2e/lib/invariants.ts`
Add one invariant function + register it in the `INVARIANTS` map (the one-row-edit + META convention). The property: for EVERY `QA-GATE APPROVED …` record observable in the trace, (a) the record carries `reviewed_by=<x>` with x≠none, OR the record carries the `[review bypass:` marker (F1/doc-only audited escape) → that record is exempt; (b) when x≠none, an earlier `REVIEW-ARTIFACT v1 …` comment exists whose `reviewer=` is NOT in the set of `IMPLEMENTER: role=` roles recorded for the task; (c) replaying the finding count over the comments preceding the approval yields ZERO open at-or-above-threshold findings (a finding is open unless a later `RESOLVED <id> …` with non-empty fix=+test= OR a latest `ARBITRATION <id> decision=overrule` clears it).
- **Trace surface:** the current Trace captures label events + hook decisions but NOT bd comment text. Add an OPTIONAL `beadsComments` field to `TraceSchema` in `.claude/tests/e2e/lib/trace.ts` (e.g. `Array<{task: string, text: string, order: number}>` or the minimal shape the invariant needs). Wire the recorder (best-effort) to populate it from the run's bd comment history where the recorder already has bd access; if that's too invasive, populate it from the tool-call/bd-capture stream the recorder already records. When the field is ABSENT (old traces / recorder didn't capture), the invariant returns `{pass:true, skipped:true, detail:"…"}` — EXACTLY the house pattern used by `completion-contract` (always skipped) and `label-milestones` (skips pre-3.5 traces). Honest approximation, documented in the detail string, citing this task.
- The invariant reads the comment grammars byte-exactly as jio.1/1vq.1 write them: `^QA-GATE APPROVED .* reviewed_by=(\S+)`, `[review bypass:`, `^REVIEW-ARTIFACT v1 .* reviewer=(\S+) .* risk_threshold=(\w+) .* findings=\[([^\]]*)\]`, `^IMPLEMENTER: role=([a-z]+) `, `^RESOLVED (\S+) .* fix=(\S+) test=(\S+)`, `^ARBITRATION (\S+) decision=(\w+)`. Reuse the severity order critical>high>medium>low>info. Do NOT reimplement the whole review-check counting in TS beyond what the invariant needs — but this is the live-trace check, so a faithful re-expression of the same predicate is expected and correct (it's a second, independent implementation guarding the same property, which is the point of a live invariant).

### 3. Unit-spec positive case + the two plan-mandated METAs — `.claude/tests/e2e/specs/_invariants.unit.spec.ts`
Using the synthetic-trace builders already in that file (extend `goodTrace()` or add a helper to attach `beadsComments`):
- POSITIVE: a trace with IMPLEMENTER role=backend + REVIEW-ARTIFACT reviewer=qa-claude findings=[] + QA-GATE APPROVED reviewed_by=qa-claude → invariant `pass:true`.
- **META 1 (plan-mandated): forge reviewer==implementer** — REVIEW-ARTIFACT reviewer=backend with IMPLEMENTER role=backend → invariant `pass:false` citing the invariant name (reviewer not independent).
- **META 2 (plan-mandated): strip an arbitration comment** from a trace that has an at-threshold finding (REVIEW-ARTIFACT findings=[R1-F1:high], IMPLEMENTER backend, QA-GATE APPROVED) with NO RESOLVED/ARBITRATION for R1-F1 → invariant `pass:false` (open at-threshold finding); adding the `ARBITRATION R1-F1 decision=overrule` back → `pass:true` (proves the arbitration clears it).
- Plus a skip case: trace WITHOUT `beadsComments` → `pass:true, skipped:true`.
- Follow the file's existing META convention (each invariant gets a positive + a violation asserting pass:false and naming the invariant). Ensure the coverage-assertion (the test that every INVARIANTS entry has a META) still passes with the new entry.

### 4. Wire the invariant into fixtures + acceptance-scenario L2 tests
- Add `- name: approval-cites-independent-review` to the `invariants:` block of the e2e `fixture.yaml`s where a full approve flow runs (the multi-domain / happy-path fixtures at minimum — check which fixtures reach approval; a fixture whose recorder lacks beadsComments will simply skip, which is safe). Do NOT add it to doc-only/failure fixtures where it's irrelevant.
- L2 acceptance scenarios (extend the shipped `verify-review-discipline.sh`/`review-separation` specs OR a new `arbitration-acceptance.sh`): (a) a seeded SELF-REVIEW (implementer authors its own review artifact, reviewer==implementer) → approve REFUSES reviewer_not_independent [jio.1 covers the refusal; jio.2 frames it as the acceptance scenario]; (b) a seeded DISPUTED at-threshold finding → approve refuses; after `qa-gate.sh arbitrate <tid> <fid> overrule '<rationale>'` → approve PASSES and the Stop hook releases; (c) after `arbitrate <fid> sustain` → still refuses (sustain does not clear). Use the REAL writers. If jio.1's specs already cover (a)/(b)/(c) mechanically, jio.2's job is the ARBITRATION-decision-flow framing + the invariant; don't duplicate — extend/reference.

### 5. Docs
- CHANGELOG: add the arbitration + invariant to the Phase V3 entry (or a sibling entry).
- docs/AGENTS.md and/or docs/HOOKS.md: document the arbitration flow (orchestrator §5d) + the new invariant in the invariants list, briefly.

## Constraints
Prompts + TS invariant + tests; the gate ENFORCEMENT is already shipped (jio.1) — do NOT modify qa-gate.sh/verify-before-stop.sh/review-check.sh/subagent-start.sh logic; do NOT add gate sentinels. The invariant is a SECOND independent implementation of the same predicate for live traces (expected). Keep the beadsComments Trace field OPTIONAL + skip-when-absent (house pattern; don't destabilize existing recorded traces or the drift guard). TEXT-anchored METAs; comment grammars byte-exact to the shipped writers; no version bump; bash 3.2 for any shell test; fixture-sync check (agent .md copies / the TS lib is under .claude/tests/e2e — verify the drift guard scope empirically). arbitrate/resolve-finding are the existing 1vq.1 writers — cite them, don't reimplement.

## Verification before done
`make test` (L1) + `bash .claude/tests/component/run.sh` (L2) green incl. any new/extended acceptance spec; `make test-e2e-unit` (the vitest pool that runs `_invariants.unit.spec.ts`) green with the new invariant's positive + two METAs proven sensitive (a mutation flips pass:false) + the coverage assertion passing; `make lint`; drift guard; `make check` (AgentLint on the edited orchestrator.md — no new H/S). Report the F7 completion contract; llm_observations mandatory (note whether the recorder actually captures beadsComments on live traces or the invariant skips, and confirm the two METAs are sensitive).

# QA plan — jio.2 (V3 arbitration prompt + approval-cites-independent-review invariant + acceptance tests)

## Review modules executed
- Impact scan (3a, FIRST action): read impact-report-claude-workflow-plugin-jio.2.json (15 files, server=code-graph, hash 832d13f9 matches current change set). Markdown files unindexed (expected); TS lib files carry internal graphs. Symbol follow-ups: impact_of(readBeadsComments) → 5 callers (runFixture + new spec only); impact_of(TraceSchema) → no recorded callers (schema surface). Blast radius confined to the e2e harness — no production hook script touched (verified: git diff of qa-gate.sh/verify-before-stop.sh/review-check.sh/subagent-start.sh vs HEAD is EMPTY).
- AI module (prompt-construction surface): orchestrator.md §5d + qa.md corrections reviewed line-by-line against the shipped writers; every factual claim verified against qa-gate.sh source (choose approve → cmd_approve delegation confirmed at :1268; empty_fix/empty_test refusal confirmed at :1750/:1756; error_key table matches review-check.sh emit sites; Stop-hook review-discipline wiring confirmed in verify-before-stop.sh :463/:1159-1205).
- SECRETS: no new secrets/PII in the diff (test fixtures use synthetic identities; AgentLint S-findings byte-identical to the last committed report).

## Parity review (priority 2 — shell vs TS second implementation)
Rule-by-rule comparison of invApprovalCitesIndependentReview vs review-check.sh cmd_gate:
- sev ranks (critical5/high4/medium3/low2/info1/unknown0): IDENTICAL.
- threshold default unknown→high(4): IDENTICAL.
- first-line-only parsing (split("\n")[0]): IDENTICAL.
- latest REVIEW-ARTIFACT wins (tail -1 vs artifacts[len-1]): IDENTICAL, TS scoped to records PRECEDING the approval — documented STRICTER rule; sound (at gate time all records precede the approval, so the real writer path is unaffected; only post-hoc records are rejected, which is the point — the ORDERING unit test pins it).
- findings token split (IFS=',' + strip-space + first-colon fid/sev): IDENTICAL incl. the no-colon→rank-0→below-threshold degenerate.
- RESOLVED: latest record + unanchored fix=\S/test=\S non-emptiness: IDENTICAL.
- ARBITRATION: latest wins, only overrule clears, sustain keeps open: IDENTICAL.
- vg8 malformed-artifact guard (no well-formed findings=[...] → violation, never zero): IDENTICAL.
- independence: reviewer∉implementers IDENTICAL; TS additionally rejects reviewed_by∈implementers (stricter, sound — self-signed approval record).
- ONE divergence found, in the shell's disfavor: sed 's/.*findings=\[/' is greedy → shell reads the LAST findings=[...] token on the line; TS reads the FIRST (genuine per grammar). Not exploitable via the shipped writer (review-record generates the summary from fixed strings); filed as hardening chore claude-workflow-plugin-gqp. The invariant-as-second-witness would surface any live divergence — exactly the design intent.
- Writer grammars byte-verified against emit sites: qa-gate.sh :990 (APPROVED), :1721 (REVIEW-ARTIFACT), :1770 (RESOLVED), :1812 (ARBITRATION), subagent-start.sh :145 (IMPLEMENTER, roles backend|frontend|devops all match [a-z]+).

## META sensitivity — independently reproduced (priority 1, all byte-restored, md5 93f6f7c6 verified pre==post)
1. Neuter independence (`false && implementers.has(reviewer)`) → META-TEST 1 + narrow-skip broken-chain RED (2 failed).
2. Open findings non-fatal (`open.length > 99999`) → META-TEST 2 + sustain + latest-wins + evidence-free-resolve RED (4 failed).
3. Sustain clears (`|| decision === "sustain"`) → sustain + latest-wins RED (2 failed) — signature distinct from #2.
4. Absence-skip → silent pass (drop skipped:true) → SKIP case RED (1 failed); run3/run4 anchors pin the same skip independently.
5. Register META-less invariant ("meta-less-dummy") → META-COVERAGE it.each row RED (1 failed).

## beadsComments capture (priority 3)
- readBeadsComments is a pure read of the SAME post-run-flushed issues.jsonl the label capture uses (runFixture.ts: flushFixtureBeads :1212 → readBeadsIssues :1218 → readBeadsComments :1242). No new bd invocation.
- Real-bd round-trip RAN on this machine (not skipped): "captures gate RECORD comments in write order" 1570ms green — 3 grammars written via real bd comments add, captured in write order.
- Skip honesty: absence(undefined)→skip; empty[]→vacuous pass; empty+bd-crash signature→llh.25 skip. The bd-crash skip requires records.length===0, so a captured-but-broken chain can NEVER skip — pinned by the "narrow" unit test (broken chain under crash signature still FAILS).

## Anchor refresh legitimacy (priority 4)
Both cassettes verified on disk: jq has("beadsComments") → false for run3 (node-react-auth-2026-06-12T00-50-56) and run4 (…02-18-12) — recorded 44 days before the field existed. The refreshed pins assert skipped===true AND pass===true AND the exact detail string, so a future re-record carrying beadsComments flips them loud. Honest refresh per llh.4/llh.15 precedent; nothing pinned away.

## Prompts (priority 5)
§5d cites the real grammars (resolve-finding --fix/--test both mandatory; arbitrate overrule|sustain; latest-wins; error_key table matches the helper's emit keys). J21 choose-approve corrected in orchestrator.md (§5a cap note, exit-6 row) and qa.md (J21 block, 6f override note); stale-claim sweep for "does not (yet)"/"V2 audit trail"/"do not wire into Stop hook" → zero hits. §5c/§6p.3 corrections are factually right post-jio.1 (verify-before-stop.sh really does run review-check.sh gate; fails closed). Guidance-only — no new enforcement added to prompts.

## Tests run
- L1 make test: 22/22 (incl. jio.1 review-separation 47 asserts).
- L2 component: 29/29 specs, 839/839 asserts — incl. NEW arbitration-acceptance.sh 33/33 (A1 self-review refuses both ends; A2 disputed finding refuses by id; A3 sustain still refuses both ends; A4 overrule → approve rc=0 AND Stop ALLOW; A5 both decisions + rationales verbatim on the trail; A6 resolve-finding path independent of arbitration, empty --test refused error_key=empty_test).
- e2e-unit: 15 files, 423 passed / 5 skipped; _invariants 102/102; drift guard 161/161.
- make lint rc=0; manifest OK; make check → 86/100, findings byte-identical to last committed report (no new H/S; none touch orchestrator.md).
- tsc: single pre-existing TS2345 at specs/_lib.unit.spec.ts:136 — reproduced byte-identical on clean stash; jio.2 adds ZERO new type errors. Filed claude-workflow-plugin-k4i (bug, discovered-from jio.2). NOT blocking (no CI lane runs tsc).

## Observations
- docs/al-*.md (16 files) deleted in the working tree: AgentLint's own report rotation on make check (reproduced identically by QA's run, which also wrote al-2026-07-26-015335). Tool-managed; commit-hygiene note for the orchestrator, not a defect.
- CHANGELOG "+21 cases" vs F7 "+23": both true under their own counting (21 it() in the invariant describe; +2 static tests in META-COVERAGE). Nit, no action.
- Independent review artifact recorded: REVIEW-ARTIFACT v1 reviewer=qa-claude model=claude-fable-5 reviewed_hash=832d13f9… findings=[] at 2026-07-26T01:54:50Z; review-check.sh gate rc=0, independent=true vs implementers=[devops].

## Verdict
Clean at/above high. Two follow-ups filed (k4i tsc pre-existing; gqp sed hardening). Packet assembled; returning needs-grading.

Deliverables:
1. orchestrator.md NEW §5d "Arbitration" (after §5c). Guidance only: trigger = disputed at/above-risk_threshold finding (approve refuses unresolved_findings, Stop blocks, orchestrator must act). Two legitimate resolutions: RESOLVE with evidence (resolve-finding --fix + --test, both mandatory) or ARBITRATE (orchestrator reads BOTH positions, records arbitrate <overrule|sustain>; overrule clears, sustain keeps open as audit record). Arbitration is the ORCHESTRATOR's job (independent third party); rationale must cite both sides. J21 interaction: correct any wording implying `choose approve` is an unconditional escape (it routes through cmd_approve, which refuses on unresolved findings). Scope: guidance + exact existing command grammars; do NOT change gate scripts; do NOT add sentinels.
2. Live-harness invariant approval-cites-independent-review in .claude/tests/e2e/lib/invariants.ts + registry row. Property, for EVERY QA-GATE APPROVED record in the trace: (a) reviewed_by=x with x≠none OR `[review bypass:` marker → exempt; (b) an EARLIER REVIEW-ARTIFACT v1 whose reviewer= is NOT in the task's IMPLEMENTER role set; (c) replaying preceding records yields ZERO open at/above-threshold findings (open unless later RESOLVED with non-empty fix=+test= OR latest ARBITRATION decision=overrule). Trace surface: OPTIONAL beadsComments field on TraceSchema; recorder populates best-effort; ABSENT → {pass:true, skipped:true} (house pattern: completion-contract / label-milestones). Grammars byte-exact to shipped writers; severity order critical>high>medium>low>info; faithful second implementation of the same predicate is expected and correct.
3. _invariants.unit.spec.ts: POSITIVE (backend implementer + qa-claude reviewer findings=[] + approval → pass) + META 1 (plan-mandated: reviewer==implementer → fail naming the invariant) + META 2 (plan-mandated: strip arbitration from an at-threshold-finding trace → fail; restore overrule → pass) + skip case (no beadsComments). Follow the file's META convention; coverage assertion must still pass.
4. Wire the invariant into fixture.yaml invariants: blocks where a full approve flow runs (skip-safe); L2 acceptance scenarios (extend shipped specs OR new arbitration-acceptance.sh): (a) seeded SELF-REVIEW → approve refuses reviewer_not_independent; (b) seeded DISPUTED at-threshold finding → refuses; after arbitrate overrule → approve passes AND Stop releases; (c) after sustain → still refuses. REAL writers. Don't duplicate jio.1's mechanics — frame the arbitration decision flow.
5. Docs: CHANGELOG Phase V3; docs/AGENTS.md and/or docs/HOOKS.md (arbitration flow + invariant).

Constraints: prompts + TS invariant + tests only; do NOT modify qa-gate.sh/verify-before-stop.sh/review-check.sh/subagent-start.sh; no new sentinels; beadsComments OPTIONAL + skip-when-absent; TEXT-anchored METAs; byte-exact grammars; no version bump; bash 3.2; verify drift-guard scope empirically.

### 5. LESSONS.md (lessons list verbatim; preamble elided — file at /Users/edk0/Desktop/projects/claude-workflow-plugin/LESSONS.md)

- Parallel agents in the same working tree contaminate each other's branches; concurrent specialists require worktree isolation. <!-- e0d.7 -->
- Boundary mocks must use the real downstream producer's shape, pinned via a fixture extracted from the producer's spec — never invented. A mock that feeds `body.error` so the test can assert `body.error` is circular and proves nothing. <!-- e0d.7 -->
- New agent files must be registered in .claude-plugin/plugin.json agents[] in the same commit that creates them; an unregistered agent is silently invisible to the SDK. <!-- l1r.5 -->
- Subagents cannot spawn other subagents; design multi-agent handoffs as root-orchestrated relays, never nested spawns. <!-- l1r.5 -->
- Interface examples must be executed by a test: any CLI surface a doc advertises needs an L2 assertion executing that exact invocation. <!-- 366.4 -->
- Prose cues do not reliably drive subagent tool usage: when a workflow REQUIRES a tool call, make it mechanical, don't prompt for it. <!-- n6d -->
- Rendered fixture installs pin plugin scripts at render time: script-level fixes require re-rendering fixture installs before they affect live validation. <!-- 366.10 -->
- Never run QA review concurrently with a builder in the same working tree. <!-- n45.1 -->
- Manifest-declared assets must be presence-asserted at the install target; glob-copy from the manifest source of truth. <!-- n45.4 -->
- Bash functions invoked via $(...) run in a subshell — encode caller signals in the stdout contract and META-test the parse. <!-- 3fn -->
- A security hardening that breaks the workflow is worse than the documented residual it closes; never trade a P2 for a P0. <!-- llh.19 -->
- Line-number-anchored mutation META-tests are brittle: anchor mutation METAs to unique TEXT patterns, never line numbers. <!-- llh.20 -->
- Effort A/B (cnz.2): verdict max — ultracode pinned the model below max with no observed benefit. <!-- cnz.2 -->
- Paid-run cost estimates must be derived from measured token flows, not guessed (observed 10x error). <!-- cnz.2 -->
- Regional/transient model exclusions in .claude/model-ranking go stale silently; gate every un-exclusion on FRESH spawn evidence, date the rationale. <!-- bi3.2 -->
- Files rewritten by a helper (awk/mv) never land in changed-files.txt; QA must verify those files explicitly via git diff. <!-- bi3.2 -->
- MCP registration scope is a mechanical contract: verify the probe read path when writing setup docs. <!-- 1vq.2 -->
- Published CLI config references can lag the shipped binary; verify against the binary's own introspection surface. <!-- 1vq.2 -->
- Run suites via their canonical make targets: bare runner invocations include guarded paid specs whose fail-closed errors masquerade as regressions. <!-- 1vq.2 -->

Evidence: walk-through mapping every SPEC behavior to a code path (or a documented F7 deferral). Plausibly-related-but-unnamed behavior = scope creep = fail.
- C2. Tests added exercise user behavior rather than implementation. At least one new test would still pass if the implementation were rewritten with the user contract identical; tests asserting only private structure fail.
- C3. The F7 completion contract carries all six fields with substantive llm_observations (task_id, files_changed, tests_added, decisions, blockers, llm_observations; boilerplate one-liner fails).

- C5. J26 modules relevant to the diff are addressed (SECRETS, INJECTION, AUTH, CONFIG, DEPS, AI, MOBILE, DATA); decisions/SPEC name the applicable modules and the diff shows the defences. Untouched domains out of scope.
- C6. Docs updated where behavior changed (CHANGELOG, README, docs/*.md, help text) or a deliberate decisions deferral; behavioral change with neither fails.
- C7. Boundary-mock fidelity (LESSONS lesson 2). Mocks of unowned boundaries derive shape from a fixture extracted from the producer's spec, source cited. Automatic needs_revision: circular pass-through assertions.

#### 6b. devops.md (version 1, extends default)
- D1. Scripts are idempotent and re-runnable (same end state twice; non-idempotent steps documented + guarded).
- D2. Graceful degradation on missing optional tools (probe with command -v; safe fallback; documented + L1-tested).
- D3. No new permission prompts; autonomy preserved (no permissions.deny; no narrowed tool lists; no new approval steps).
- D4. Secrets and PII stay out of source, logs, and history (no hardcoded credentials/emails/PII; new log lines redact; gitleaks-equivalent clean).

CHANGES:
- .claude/scripts/qa-gate.sh:
  - cmd_enter: sets rubric-pending alongside qa-gate-entered (fresh + idempotent paths); clears stale rubric-satisfied on re-enter; observations cite the rubric state.

Malformed input -> stdout JSON envelope with error_key naming the offender (missing_key:<k>, verdict_invalid_enum, criterion_results_not_array, iteration_not_number, invalid_json, empty_input, file_not_found, unknown_flag, etc.) + non-zero exit. On satisfied: posts comment "RUBRIC <version> iteration <n>: satisfied — all criteria pass"; removes rubric-pending; adds rubric-satisfied. On needs_revision: posts comment "RUBRIC <version> iteration <n>: needs_revision — failed: <names>"; labels unchanged (the qa-blocked round-trip is the QA agent's move per principle 7).
  - cmd_approve: NOT hard-gated on rubric-satisfied (principle 6). Warns loudly in observations when rubric-pending is still present (the agent's prompt in A.2 enforces the override-reason rule). Drops rubric-pending (cycle ends); preserves rubric-satisfied (audit trail).

- .claude/scripts/tests/qa-gate-grade-record.test.sh: 87 assertions across 9 sections. Covers enter rubric-pending + re-enter clearing stale rubric-satisfied + idempotent refresh; grade-record satisfied (comment "RUBRIC v1 iteration 1: satisfied — all criteria pass" + label flip); grade-record needs_revision (comment with failed criterion names + labels unchanged + qa-blocked NOT auto-added); --file variant + nonexistent-file error_key; 9 malformed-input cases each asserting the structured error_key; approve-with-rubric-pending WARNING + still-succeeds + cycle ends; approve-with-rubric-satisfied audit-trail preserved; status rubric state across not-entered/entered/post-satisfied; structural sanity (frontmatter version: 1 on every rubric file, extends: default on domain files, applies_to: bug on overlay, iteration_cap=3 in config); META-TEST that awk-stubs the satisfied-branch label flip in a tempdir copy of qa-gate.sh and asserts rubric-satisfied is NOT set under the stub — proving the Section 2 assertion is sensitive to the production behavior, not vacuous.

KEY DECISIONS:
1. grade-record input shape: --file <path> OR stdin (tty-detected). Both forms exist so the QA agent can pipe (natural pattern) or attach a saved verdict for replay/debugging. tty detection prevents a hang when an operator types the subcommand alone.
2. Structured error envelopes via new emit_error_json (separate from emit_json) so the QA agent can branch on error_key without parsing prose. agent-centric per bd-mcp conventions.
3. Comment shape exactly matches spec wording: "RUBRIC <v> iteration <n>: <verdict> — <summary>" where summary is "all criteria pass" for satisfied OR "failed: <names>" for needs_revision (defensive: if needs_revision arrives without any failing criteria, summary cites required_fixes count instead).

5. Approve label policy: drop rubric-pending (cycle ends, regardless of verdict). Preserve rubric-satisfied if present (audit trail). Both consistent with the "labels are the record" thin-wrapper rule (principle 7).
6. Domain rubrics kept short (4 criteria each) per spec ("the grader's leverage is default + bugfix"). Each criterion is a checkable assertion with an "Evidence that satisfies it" line.

title: Bug: runFixture beads diff misses tasks created via BD_NO_DAEMON/MCP paths (flush race); rubric spec used naive strict assertion
description: Live attempt 3 (trace rubric-revision-loop-2026-06-11T21-45-00-465Z.jsonl) demonstrated the full relay loop (grader spawned at ROOT twice, grade-record invoked, Stop approved) but failed at beadsTasksCreated.length>0: the trace's beads diff is EMPTY despite two mcp bd_create_task calls + one Bash 'BD_NO_DAEMON=1 bd create' visible in toolCalls. comments.text: ROOT CAUSE SHARPENED: re-pinning agent .md frontmatter to claude-opus-4-7 did NOT unblock subagent spawns this session — they still failed instantly on claude-fable-5 (0 tool calls). The harness caches agent definitions at SESSION START; mid-session file rewrites don't take effect until restart. Two consequences for the model-select feature: (1) its whole mechanism (SessionStart rewrites pins) only affects the NEXT session, so a freshly-adopted model is never validated in the session that adopts it; (2) if the cached pin's model loses spawn access mid-session, ALL subagent spawns brick until session restart OR an explicit per-spawn model override. Unblocked this session by passing the Agent tool's model='opus' override (takes precedence over cached frontmatter). This strengthens the mechanical-fix need: spawn-probe validation must run in the adopting session, and there should be a documented per-spawn override escape.

### Root cause (recap)
Trust-boundary inversion: the Stop hook released on `qa-gate.sh status == approved`, which reduces to `has_label qa-approved` — a token (a) any agent can mint via a bare `bd label add` (P0), and (b) bound to a task-id, never to the bytes shipping (P1).

### Fix mechanism (change-set-bound, tamper-evident record; reuses n6d machinery)
**`qa-gate.sh approve`** (`.claude/scripts/qa-gate.sh`):
- Added shared helper `compute_change_set_hash()` that delegates to the ONE canonical implementation — `impact-report.sh --hash-only` (sha256 of the sorted, denylist-filtered changed-files list). No 4th copy of the denylist; the refusal block now also calls this helper.
- After setting `qa-approved`, approve writes the canonical hash INTO the approval comment: `QA-GATE APPROVED change_set_hash=<h> at <ts>: <summary>`. Computed OUTSIDE the IMPACT-REPORT-REFUSAL sentinel block so (a) the `--no-impact-report` bypass path still binds, and (b) the n6d META-strip stays coherent (verified: n6d strip META still green). Empty hash → degrades to legacy unbound comment + sync-errors.log warning (labels remain the lifecycle source of truth; approval is not aborted).

Spec 0.5 trail (repro → root cause → fix → flip → audit). Surface: `.claude/scripts/verify-before-stop.sh` + `.claude/tests/component/specs/verify-before-stop.sh` only. No commits, no paid runs.

### 1. REPRO captured RED (failing-first)
Added an L2 spec block `vbs-llh18-miss` (fresh git+beads fixture, empty test_cmd so the test pass is skipped, real plugin scripts symlinked). Builds a LEGIT change-set-bound approval (label + matching `QA-GATE APPROVED change_set_hash=<h>` record, hash == `impact-report.sh --hash-only`), then changes exactly ONE variable: removes `impact-report.sh`.

PRE-FIX run (`run.sh --filter verify-before-stop`): **pass=63 fail=2** —
- PASS sanity: with impact-report.sh PRESENT the matching record RELEASES (isolates the variable to script-presence).
- PASS precondition: impact-report.sh absent.
- **FAIL** `MISSING impact-report.sh -> FAIL-CLOSED (decision:block)` — the harness `miss_decision` returned `ABORT` (empty stdout + non-zero exit), NOT `block`.
- **FAIL** block-reason check — no reason at all (script aborted before emitting).

### 2. ROOT CAUSE = `set -e` abort on a bare command-substitution assignment
`verify-before-stop.sh` line 25 `set -e`. At the approved-path check, `CURRENT_CS_HASH=$(current_change_set_hash)`. `current_change_set_hash()` does `[ -f "$IMPACT_REPORT_SCRIPT" ] || { printf ''; return 1; }` → returns **1** when the script is MISSING. A bare `X=$(cmd)` whose RHS exits non-zero trips `set -e` → the whole script ABORTS with empty stdout + exit 1. Per the hooks contract only exit 2 / a JSON `decision:block` blocks a Stop; **exit 1 + empty stdout is NON-blocking → Claude ALLOWS the Stop (FAIL-OPEN)**. The implementer's intended fail-closed branch (`if [ -z "$CURRENT_CS_HASH" ]` arm of `LABEL_WITHOUT_RECORD`) was UNREACHABLE in this sub-case — the abort happens at the assignment, before the `if`.
Empirically confirmed in isolation: `bash -c 'set -e; f(){ printf ""; return 1; }; X=$(f); echo after'` → prints nothing, exit 1; with `X=$(f) || true` → continues, rc 0, X empty.
ASYMMETRY proving it's exactly this: the PRESENT-BUT-FAILING case fails CLOSED correctly (function body ends `|| printf ''` → rc 0 → empty hash → LABEL_WITHOUT_RECORD block fires). Only MISSING (no `|| ...` guard at the call site) aborts. Producer/consumer inconsistency too: `qa-gate.sh approve` REFUSES (exit 2) when impact-report.sh is missing, while the consumer fails open.

### 3. FIX (QA-verified one-liner, applied)
`verify-before-stop.sh` call site → `CURRENT_CS_HASH=$(current_change_set_hash) || true`. The assignment now yields rc 0 + empty hash on a missing script, so the missing-script case falls into the existing fail-CLOSED `LABEL_WITHOUT_RECORD` branch (its `[ -z "$CURRENT_CS_HASH" ]` arm → "could not be recomputed (impact-report.sh missing/failing)" → `emit_block`). Load-bearing-comment added at the site explaining the `set -e` semantics.

### 4. AUDIT for other `$(...)`-under-`set -e` fail-open instances in the approved-path block
`set -o pipefail` is NOT set → a pipe's rc is its last element only, so the `... | jq ... || echo` and `... | head -15` forms are all rc-0-safe. Of every command-sub assignment between the approved-path check and EOF, exactly ONE other had a bare (unguarded) form: `INTENT_JSON=$(compute_intent_payload)` (QA-required BLOCK path). `compute_intent_payload` ends in a bare `jq -nc ...`; with literal args it won't realistically fail, but it is the same anti-pattern on the block-emission path — a `jq` failure would abort mid-block → fail open. Hardened defensively: `INTENT_JSON=$(compute_intent_payload) || INTENT_JSON='{}'` (fallback keeps the block firing with a valid empty payload). Noted as defensive hardening, NOT a second active exploit (it falls through to a fail-closed default, unlike the P0 line). No other bare instances found.

| MISSING impact-report.sh (legit approval) | ABORT → ALLOW (fail-open) | **decision:block** ✅ (fail-closed) |

My two added comment blocks shifted the `CHANGE_COUNT" -gt 15` truncation guard 1131→1153, which broke the truncation META-TEST's `NR==1131` absolute-line anchor. ## FIX applied (NOT approved — left for QA) — llh.19

Owned files only: `prevent-orchestrator-edits.sh`, `post-edit.sh`, `settings.json` + their tests; plus 2 stale lines in `docs/HOOKS.md` that described these scripts. Sibling files (verify-before-stop.sh/invariants.ts; README/WORKFLOW) untouched.

### Fix mechanism
1. **settings.json** — both the PreToolUse (deny) and PostToolUse (track) matchers widened `^(Write|Edit|MultiEdit)$` → `^(Write|Edit|MultiEdit|Bash)$` so Bash now reaches both hooks.
2. **prevent-orchestrator-edits.sh** — added `is_bash_write()` heuristic detecting write-shaped Bash (heredoc-to-file, `>`/`>>` into a path, `tee`, `sed -i`, `perl -i`, `dd of=`, `cp`/`mv`/`install` into the tree), with an explicit transient-sink exemption (`/tmp`, `/dev/null`, `/var/tmp`, `/private/tmp`, fd dups like `2>&1`). Decision logic split into two flags:
   - `IS_WRITE_TOOL` (unambiguous Write/Edit/MultiEdit) and `IS_BASH_WRITE` (heuristic).
   - **Confirmed orchestrator** → deny BOTH (write tool + write-shaped Bash).
   - **Unknown identity + write TOOL** → **fail CLOSED** (deny).
   - **Unknown identity + write-shaped Bash (heuristic only)** → ALLOW (anti-overreach — see boundary below).
   - **Specialist / any known non-orchestrator identity** → allow.
3. **post-edit.sh** — added `extract_bash_write_paths()` (mirrors the same shapes/exemptions) so a Bash-laundered edit's target source path(s) are recovered into `changed-files.txt` and become visible to the QA change-set. Refactored the append loop to track 0..n paths; transient sinks and reads produce no entry.

### Threat-model boundary (honest)
- **Primary guard remains the orchestrator's omitted Write/Edit tools.** This hook is defense-in-depth.
- The Bash-write detector is a **raise-the-bar HEURISTIC, not airtight.** A determined orchestrator can obfuscate (base64→sh, operator built from a var, `python -c`/`node -e` writer). We deliberately do NOT chase those — an arms race in a string parser produces false positives that strangle legitimate Bash.
- **Fail-closed is scoped to the unambiguous Write/Edit TOOLS, NOT the Bash heuristic.** Found by **dogfooding**: this plugin's own live hook fired on my edits because this runtime does not surface `subagent_name` for the top-level agent. Widening the matcher to Bash + fail-closing the heuristic bricked ordinary Bash (any command merely *mentioning* `> file` / `sed -i` / `tee` in a quoted arg, grep pattern, or comment was denied). Resolution: fail-closed only on the definite write tools; an unknown-identity write-shaped Bash is allowed. The residual gap (identity-less orchestrator laundering via Bash) is exactly the "determined orchestrator could obfuscate" boundary already declared out of scope.

- `prevent-orchestrator-edits.test.sh`: **31/31** (incl. META-test neutralizing `is_bash_write` → orch-Bash-write DENY flips to ALLOW; the 8 write-shapes; 9 anti-overreach legit-Bash; fail-closed for 3 write tools + unprobed-field; the 2 new heuristic-not-fail-closed cases).

comments.text:
ROOT CAUSE = (b) DERIVER GAP — variable-indirected `bd create`. Evidence-before-fix.

## Evidence chain

1. The trace DOES set qa-pending at task creation (so case (a) "workflow never sets it" is FALSE, and case (c) "stale decl" is FALSE — qa-pending is a real, current milestone). The orchestrator created the two child tasks with:
```
BD=./.claude/bin/bd
BE=$("$BD" create "Backend: POST /auth/login with JWT issuance" -t feature -p 2 \
  -l backend,feature,qa-pending \
  --description "..." --json | jq -r '.id')
FE=$("$BD" create "Frontend: LoginForm component" -t feature -p 2 \
  -l frontend,feature,qa-pending \
  --description "..." --json | jq -r '.id')
```
(BD= assignment + `"$BD" create … -l …,qa-pending` confirmed at lines 4/6/11/18 of the trace's flattened Bash command stream. The fixture provisions a local bd shim at .claude/bin/bd; the model aliased it as $BD and invoked through the variable.)

2. The deriver (lib/labelEvents.ts) only matches a LITERAL `bd` token before `create`:
```
BD_CREATE_RE = /\bbd(?:\s+-{1,2}\w[\w-]*(?:=\S+)?)*\s+create\b/g
```
`"$BD" create` has no literal `bd` word, so BD_CREATE_RE never matches → the `-l backend,feature,qa-pending` slice is never scanned → ZERO qa-pending add-events derived. The SAME blind spot exists for BD_LABEL_RE / BD_UPDATE_RE (all anchored on `\bbd`), but only `create` carried qa-pending in this run.

   Contrast: the later `bd update …`, `bd comment …` calls in the SAME run used the literal `bd` (matched fine) — proving the gap is specifically the variable-indirected invocations, of which only the two creates carried a label.

3. OFFLINE RE-EVAL (BEFORE fix) — ran deriveBeadsLabelEvents + INVARIANTS['label-milestones'] against the real recorded trace via a throwaway vitest spec:
   - DERIVED add labels: ["qa-gate-entered","rubric-pending","qa-approved"] — qa-pending ADD count = 0
   - label-milestones [qa-pending, qa-approved]: pass=false, skipped=undefined
   - detail: "missing milestone label add(s): [qa-pending] — declared order: [qa-pending, qa-approved]; observed add events (in order): [qa-gate-entered, rubric-pending, …, qa-approved]; net-diff adds: [backend, feature, frontend, qa-approved]"
   This reproduces the paid-run FAIL exactly (same observed adds, same net-diff adds as the reported evidence).

## Why this is NOT (a) or (c)
- NOT (a) workflow gap: qa-pending IS produced — via creation labels (`-l …,qa-pending`). The flow does set it; the deriver just can't see the variable-indirected form. (Confirmed there is no separate `bd label add qa-pending` / `bd update --add-label qa-pending` anywhere — creation labels are the sole source, exactly as in 9ke run-3.)
- NOT (c) stale decl: qa-pending remains the genuine "queued for QA" milestone that the orchestrator stamps at creation; qa-gate.sh approve still removes it (the remove events ARE in the stream). Rewriting the fixture decl would HIDE a real recorder blind spot, not fix it. The invariant must keep asserting the real qa-pending→qa-approved ordered transition.

## Fix (case-b prescription)
Extend lib/labelEvents.ts so the four `bd …`-anchored Bash scanners ALSO recognize the `$VAR`/`${VAR}` indirection the orchestrator uses for its bd wrapper (BD=./.claude/bin/bd; "$BD" create …). The recorded trace then yields the qa-pending creation-label add → label-milestones PASSES offline on the real trace. Add a unit test for the missed `"$BD" create -l …,qa-pending` shape + a META assertion. No fixture/invariant-logic change (decl + invariant are correct).

== Schema constraint that drove the signal choice ==
`HookOutputSchema` (lib/trace.ts) does NOT carry `stop_hook_active` per event. The recorder (runFixture.ts ingestMessage, hook_response branch) captures ONLY the hook's STDOUT (`msg.output` → `{}`), never its STDIN — so `stop_hook_active` is unobservable per-event. Confirmed by dumping the django trace: the 2 allow Stops carry `response={}`, `decision=null`, `reason=''`, dur 16/17ms.

== H3 exclusion signal (chosen) ==
A Stop:allow is an H3 re-entry guard iff it is a BARE `{}` allow (empty response object, no decision, no reason — `isBareAllowOutput`) AND it is PRECEDED in hook-stream order by a Stop:block (`classifyStopAllows`). Rationale: the H3 guard (verify-before-stop.sh:553-558) fires ONLY because a prior Stop:block set `stop_hook_active=true` and forced re-entry; it short-circuits with `echo "{}"` BEFORE the change-set pipeline. So "bare {} after a block" mirrors exactly when H3 can fire — the cleanest available proxy for "this allow did NOT evaluate the change-set." An allow with NO preceding block cannot be an H3 guard → it is a release allow (handled by the approval branch) or, with changes present + bd healthy + no approval, a real leak.
KEY: every non-blocking exit in verify-before-stop.sh emits a bare `echo "{}"` — INCLUDING the genuine QA-approved release (line 1375). So output-shape alone cannot distinguish H3 from a legit release; the preceding-block correlation is what separates them.

== bd-skip condition (chosen) ==
`beadsUnavailable(trace)`: `beadsLabelEvents` is PRESENT (post-3.5) AND contains an ATTEMPTED gate write (a `qa-gate-entered` or `qa-pending` ADD — only `qa-gate.sh enter` / a qa-pending create-label produce these) AND `beadsLabelTransitions` is EMPTY (net diff = what actually persisted to issues.jsonl). Gate-entered-but-nothing-persisted = bd crashed (the daemon stack-overflow). The trace does not carry sync-errors.log, so this structural signature IS the in-trace bd-unavailable evidence. Narrow on purpose: does NOT fire on pre-3.5 (no events), empty-events-array (recorder saw no activity), or healthy runs (transitions non-empty).

== invStopRequiresApproval decision order ==
1. 0 allows → PASS (vacuous).
2. sawApproval (qa-approved/qa-deferred in transitions) → PASS, preserving the EXACT legacy detail "N Stop:allow event(s) with qa-approved/qa-deferred recorded on: [...]" (phase-b run3/run4 anchors pin this substring).
3. nonH3 allows == 0 (all allows are H3 re-entry guards) → PASS "all H3 re-entry guards … gate blocked and did not leak". ← DJANGO lands here.
4. beadsUnavailable → SKIP (honest-skip; covers a bd-crash run that ALSO has a non-H3 allow, so bd-down never produces a false leak).
5. no beadsLabelEvents at all (pre-3.5) → SKIP (approval unobservable; a release allow is a bare {} indistinguishable from a benign release; mirrors the label-milestones pre-3.5 skip / llh.4).
6. bd healthy + non-H3 release allow + no approval + fileWrites present → FAIL "gate leaked" (real-leak detection preserved). fileWrites empty → vacuous PASS.

== invLabelMilestones bd-skip ==
Inserted AFTER the success check and BEFORE the failure return: `misordered.length===0 && beadsUnavailable(trace)` → SKIP. Only purely-MISSING milestones skip; an affirmative MISORDER (adds visible in the stream) is a real defect the net-diff outage cannot explain and still FAILS. The existing pre-3.5 skip (no events) is untouched, so phase-b run3/run4 keep their "trace lacks beadsLabelEvents (pre-3.5 recording)" SKIP.

== DJANGO RE-EVAL (THE key evidence) — trace: cassettes/replays/python-django-bug-2026-06-13T19-56-33-557Z.jsonl ==
stop-requires-approval: BEFORE = FAIL ("Stop hook emitted 2 allow decision(s) but no task transitioned to qa-approved or qa-deferred — gate may have leaked"). AFTER = PASS ("2 Stop:allow event(s), all H3 re-entry guards … gate blocked and did not leak"). Both allows (idx 70/71) are bare {} after the blocks at idx 62/63.
label-milestones: BEFORE = FAIL ("missing milestone label add(s): [qa-pending, qa-approved]"). AFTER = SKIP ("bd unavailable (daemon crash) … milestone adds [qa-pending, qa-approved] could not be recorded"). beadsLabelEvents shows attempted qa-gate-entered adds; beadsLabelTransitions=[].
(In-repo regression-anchored by 3 tests loading the actual cassette + an inline reproduction of the OLD verdict = FAIL.)

== NO-REGRESSION (known-good) ==
node-react-auth 06-13 (cassettes/replays/node-react-auth-2026-06-13T16-52-03-909Z.jsonl): stop-requires-approval stays PASS via the approval branch (sawApproval=true). label-milestones stays FAIL on qa-pending — a PRE-EXISTING, non-bd issue (bd was healthy → correctly NOT masked by the bd-skip; proves the skip is narrow).

## ROOT CAUSE (changed_files-vs-diff_summary divergence) — evidence-before-fix

The Stop hook's "changes require QA" decision and its rendered "N file(s) changed / Files changed" display are driven by **three different sources** that disagree:

1. `CODE_CHANGES_DETECTED` (the gate-fires-or-not flag): set true by the **git-status fallback** (verify-before-stop.sh ~L461-491) which iterates `git status --porcelain` and keeps any path passing `is_tracked_change`. The denylist (`DENYLIST_REGEX`, L86) does **NOT** exclude beads-state files — `.beads/issues.jsonl`, `beads.db`, `.qa-tracking/*` all pass as TRACKED. So a Stop fired right after a `qa-gate enter` label-write (which mutates `.beads/issues.jsonl`) trips `CODE_CHANGES_DETECTED=true`.
2. `CHANGE_COUNT` / `CHANGED_FILES` (the rendered display, L901-921) read **only** from `TRACKING_FILE` (`.qa-tracking/changed-files.txt`), filtered by `is_tracked_change`. When post-edit never tracked the beads write (it doesn't), that file is empty/absent → `CHANGE_COUNT=0` (or `?`).
3. `diff_summary` in the J18 intent payload (`compute_intent_payload`, L376-379) comes from **raw** `git diff --stat HEAD` (no denylist) → it shows the `.beads/issues.jsonl` line.

Net effect = the self-contradictory payload from the bug report: `changed_files=[]`, `0 file(s) changed`, empty Files list, yet `decision=block` + `diff_summary` lists only beads state.

## Harness bug found + worktree-isolation constraint (methodology, cont.)

**Two harness/invocation issues found & worked around (no production edits):**

1. **stdin-drain early-stop.** `mutation-sweep.sh` line 426 runs the per-mutant test-cmd WITHOUT redirecting stdin, so the parser's `while read … < mutants.txt` fd0 is inherited by the test subprocess; a hook's `INPUT=$(cat)` drains the remaining mutant records, terminating the sweep after ~3-4 mutants (explains the earlier killed:3/4, generated:56 anomaly). Fix: prefix the test-cmd with `exec </dev/null;`. (Filed as a discovered-from harness bug — see code_bugs_filed.)

2. **mutation.conf clobbers env timeouts.** Line 66 `. "$CONF"` hard-sets `MUTANT_TEST_TIMEOUT_S=60`, overriding any env var (the `${VAR:-60}` default never applies because conf already set it). title: impact_of cue does not reach QA on clean-flow runs: hook template fires only on Stop-recovery; SKILL delegation step and orchestrator QA-prompt composition carry no impact_of instruction; qa.md 3a alone empirically insufficient (4 live runs, 0 calls)
notes:
OPEN.

=== FINDING ===

After 366.9 shipped the impact_of cue to two surfaces (qa.md 3a FIRST-ACTION wording + verify-before-stop.sh Stop-block QA-Task heredoc), live run 4 STILL had 0 impact_of calls. The 366.9 fix is necessary but not sufficient: the cue does not actually reach QA via the channels we assumed in any clean-flow run.

=== EVIDENCE (4 live runs, all 0 calls) ===

- Run 1: cassettes/seed/node-react-auth-2026-06-11T23-34-49-784Z.jsonl (pre-fixes; QA's frontmatter stripped MCP tools entirely — fixed by 366.6).
- Run 2: cassettes/seed/node-react-auth-2026-06-12T00-50-56-312Z.jsonl (post-366.6; tools available but unused; 366.9 traced root-cause to verify-before-stop.sh heredoc).
- Run 3: same run 2 trace re-evaluated offline post-366.8/366.9 (offline only; not a paid run).
- Run 4: cassettes/seed/node-react-auth-2026-06-12T02-18-12-871Z.jsonl (LIVE, ~1376s, ~$5.46; post-366.8 + 366.9, fixture.yaml preserved end-to-end; satisfiesInvariants evaluated LIVE for the first time).

Run-4 cue-channel inspection (anchored in _phase-b-run4-trace.unit.spec.ts):
  - Stop hook fired 4 events: 2 block, 2 allow.
  - Both block reasons start with 'QA approval required (iteration 1, runner=npm, technical checks passed).'
  - Neither block reason contains 'FIRST: for every changed file' or 'impact_of'.
  - The fixture-local script that ran is at .claude/tests/e2e/fixtures/node-react-auth/.claude/scripts/verify-before-stop.sh — last touched in a8a7bcf 'v3 upgrade + G8 test harness' (predates 8f07ea9 '366.9 cue fix' to the repo's copy). Hooks.json uses CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.claude/scripts/verify-before-stop.sh, so the fixture-rendered copy is what runs in-fixture.
  - The repo's .claude/scripts/verify-before-stop.sh DOES have the cue at lines 977-982; the fixture render is the stale copy.

Orchestrator's free composition compensated, somewhat — the first QA Agent invocation prompt (toolu_018kaX5SpZ2NttWtT3X72aCJ) DID contain:
  Section 6: 'Code-graph regression check — use mcp__plugin_claude-workflow_code-graph__impact_of (or the mcp__code-graph__impact_of alias) on the key new/modified symbols (createApp, LoginForm, the new /auth/login handler) so the qa-queried-impact-of invariant is satisfied for this trace.'

This was the most explicit cue we have ever shipped: tool name, alias, and INVARIANT NAME. The model still did not call impact_of. So the open-loop is not 'cue did not reach QA' but 'cue did not move QA' even when on-the-nose. (The second QA spawn — toolu_01R6B2xH139kD5RTUXq49tEo — was an epic-level re-application after the orchestrator prematurely closed the epic; it omitted impact_of entirely from its prompt, which adds a second failure mode.)

The qa.md 3a FIRST ACTION wording is in the QA agent's system prompt for every spawn (it's part of the loaded agent definition, claude-workflow:qa). 4 live runs have now demonstrated it is empirically insufficient on its own.

=== ROOT CAUSE ===

The impact_of cue has three failed delivery channels in a clean-flow run:
  1. Stop-hook QA-Task heredoc (verify-before-stop.sh) — fires ONLY when QA needs to be re-spawned after a Stop block-then-recover cycle; on a clean flow where the orchestrator delegates to QA proactively (no block needed), the heredoc never fires. AND on fixture runs the fixture-local stale render lacks the cue regardless.
  2. SKILL.md / workflow-engine SessionStart injection — does not mention impact_of at all (we checked the SessionStart additionalContext in run-4 — no impact_of reference).
  3. Orchestrator's free-composed QA delegation prompt — depends on the orchestrator model picking up qa.md 3a's FIRST ACTION wording. Run 4 shows this can happen (orchestrator named the tool + invariant) but is unreliable across spawns (second QA spawn omitted it).
  4. qa.md 3a itself — IS in QA's system prompt, but the FIRST ACTION wording lives in section 3a of a long document and is empirically not weighted high enough relative to the per-spawn Task prompt.

=== DESIGN OPTIONS ===

(carried from 366.9 notes, refined with run-4 evidence)

  A. Tighten qa.md 3a further: lead the entire file with a FIRST ACTION call-out block above the frontmatter / above the role description. Mechanical, no new code surface; but 4 live runs say in-agent-system-prompt cues alone are insufficient.

  B. Mid-Task budget assertion: extend verify-before-stop.sh to detect 'QA approved with fileWrites > 0 AND impact_of calls = 0' and emit a soft block (one re-iteration) — turns the cue from prose into a hard requirement enforced by the gate itself. Risk: false-positive when impact_of is genuinely unavailable; mitigated by checking toolsAvailable.

  C. **Mechanical: orchestrator pre-computes impact_of at root and embeds results in the QA delegation packet** — the orchestrator HAS the code-graph tools and is the one composing the Task prompt for QA anyway. Pre-running impact_of on the changed-symbol seed set turns QA's job from 'remember to invoke a tool the model often forgets' to 'verify the impact analysis the orchestrator already produced'. This is the design the orchestrator's role-split should encode (the parallel to orchestrator.md section 5a + qa.md section 6 RUBRIC-RELAY).

  D. SKILL.md injection of impact_of cue at SessionStart — universal across all spawns of all agents, in the always-loaded context. Cheapest broadcast surface. Same in-prompt weight problem as (A) but fires earlier in the context window.

Preferred path: combine (C) + (B). (C) makes the right behaviour the easy one; (B) catches regressions when the orchestrator skips its pre-compute. (A) and (D) alone are insufficient per 4 live runs of evidence.

=== HANDOFF ===

Standalone bug (no parent epic). Carries past Phase B. Future paid run is the only way to verify a fix — see anchor _phase-b-run4-trace.unit.spec.ts for the current-state baseline; flipping the 'impactCalls.length === 0' assertion red is the success signal.

Evidence anchored: _phase-b-run4-trace.unit.spec.ts (10 active assertions, all green on this trace).

title: Bug: signup route returns 404 instead of 500 when the data-access layer throws a falsy value
description:
Discovered during QA of 40c.1 via independent fault-injection probing (7 error shapes fuzzed through the 500 path).

ROOT CAUSE: server/src/routes/signup.js outer catch does 'return next(err)'. When the store (or any downstream) throws a FALSY value (null/undefined/0/''/false), Express treats next(falsy) as next() — i.e. 'continue routing' — so the request SKIPS the central error handler in app.js and falls through to the catch-all 404 (not_found) instead of the intended 500 (internal_error).

REACHABILITY: NOT reachable today. The in-memory store throws only EmailTakenError; validateSignup guarantees password is a string before hashPassword (so its TypeError cannot fire); and node-postgres rejects with Error objects. This is a defense-in-depth gap in the 'every unexpected failure funnels to a leak-free 500' invariant, most relevant when the Postgres-backed store lands (claude-workflow-plugin-5x8).

IMPACT: LOW. No information disclosure — the 404 body is a static structured envelope with no internals/stack/secret (fuzz-verified). Only the status code and error code are 'wrong' (404 not_found vs 500 internal_error).

FIX (one line): normalize non-Error throws in the route's outer catch, e.g. 'return next(err instanceof Error ? err : new Error("non-error thrown in signup"));'. Add a regression test that injects a falsy throw from store.insert and asserts 500 + internal_error. Best handled alongside 5x8.
